review: This is a new lounge for Aer Lingus as on previous occasions they would use the lounge of a partner airline. The lounge is not overly large but more than enough space for passengers embarking on the four flights they were operating when we were there. There is a small area with food. Sandwiches, salads and wraps during all opening hours and hot food choices late afternoon and evening. The evening hot choices on our visit were Chicken in a mushroom sauce, Boiled potatoes with parsley, steamed green beans and tomatoes and macaroni cheese. I sampled all these and they were very good. Two cakes were on offer as dessert. All the time bags of crisps (chips) and pretzels and fresh apples and oranges were there too. A small selection of wines and beers, including a sparkling wine, and sodas were self-serve. Pleasant and quiet with staff who, while not exactly chatty and communicative, were professional. They cleared tables and refreshed food regularly. Toilets were clean and more than adequate. I didn't see any shower facilities, however that does not mean they were not there.

A small, clean lounge with plenty of seating, a well-stocked, self-serve bar and some food options. Some windows overlooked the runways and boarding gates but, understandably, the other windows overlooking a shabby storage area had blinds fully closed. A few nibbles, a couple of sandwich and wrap options and a beef stew were available. My partner had the stew and left it after a couple of bites as the meat was mainly fat and gristle and the sauce bland and unappetising, a real disappointment. Two flavours of potato crisps (chips in the US) were consumed and these, jalapeno and BBQ, were very good. Staff were helpful and kept the tables and other areas clean and tidy. It was good that the lounge was only a short walk from the gate too.

While the decor etc is nice, the food is absolutely awful. Soup, cheese and crackers is the height of it. It is truly appalling. The staff themselves seem embarrassed by the mostly empty display cabinets.
This is the most underated lounge i have been to. The food, drink and desert options are good and its quite comfortable too. Would definitely recommend

The lounge is spacious, good light and the food options are good. While there is not an a la carte offer or substantial buffet, the sandwiches, pies, salads and sweets were more than enough and all very tasty. Cleanliness could be a tiny bit better.

The Air China lounge at Beijing Capital International Airport is really terrible. I think it is the worst lounge of Air China. The food is terrible and the dishes are hard to swallow. Fortunately, there are more choices of drinks and snacks. The lounge is very crowded at noon and in the evening, and there are many people, which is not a good experience.

The computer says no. There is a famous scene in the British series "Little Britain" called "the computer says no". Captures perfectly the AENA lounge experience when they don't let you enter at 10.45am for a 3pm flight cos of their 4hr rule when it's only 1/3 full. The only thing they are good at is saying no reflecting an absence of knowledge of what the word reasonable means AENA that operates this VIP lounge and many others gets away with the most outrageously bad service.

Squalor. I find it difficult to understand how AENA that operates this lounge gets away with such an abysmal service standard. Food was disgusting - the small amount that was available. Glassware was filthy as was the general state of the place.

This is the worst lounge I've encountered in my life. Absence of dining during afternoon and evening. Only vile processed cheese and cold meat. Staff excel in being unfriendly and useless. In fairness to Air Europa they do not manage this lounge, AENA does which owns most Spanish airports.

The front facing staff show little evidence of ability in customer service. They are unfriendly and become belligerent in an immature manner when feedback is given about the poor facilities at this lounge. An example is a request to use the one shower. They tell you it is occupied and expect you go find the cleaners every 20 minutes to go see if it is free. A suggestion that they might have a waiting list and let passengers know when it is free was met with dismissive and I couldn't careless reactions. This airport has a long way to go to understand how to do customer service. If you want sarcasm and infantile behaviour, you can talk to your kids I guess. But not what you want here.

This marks the first time I have left a lounge to seek peace, quiet, and electrical outlets in the main concourse. This lounge is entirely enclosed without a single window. At 09:30 it was overcrowded. My first choice was sparkling wine - no luck. Second choice was a rum and coke - no rum. The food options were meager, nothing warm and little that was appetizing. The escalator up to the lounge was out of service, and there was no elevator. How does the EU permit a public facility that is handicap inaccessible? The only saving grace to an otherwise dismal experience was the pleasant, good humor of the entrance staff. This lounge is a shameful offering, particularly in comparison to the Sala Montvale in the international gates of MXP.

I have in the past been scathing of Air New Zealand. However, as time has passed the bar has been raised so significantly I cannot fault the lounge at Auckland airport. The standard of food and what is on offer given my experiences in other airports over the last 10 weeks is excellent. I can recommend the Air NZ lounge

The lounge is very spacious and the colours give a sense of calm. The staff are most friendly, chatty and  professional. The food choice for breakfast at this stage isn't diverse, but the effort they make into fresh-cooked foods e.g. omelettes is excellent. The barista made excellent coffee, almost as good as the coffees from cafes. The seat highlight is the outside garden with swinging seats with views.

Air Malta was using Lufthansa's Business Class Lounge at Terminal 2. Visiting it again, nothing noticeably had changed. Everything seemed to be back to normal. It is a pleasant enough place to relax, but only for a short time. The food and drinks were almost the same as before. The cold food, fruit and cereal section were excellent.  I was happy to drop in again.

Spacious and airy ambiance, the best thing about it, is the view towards the runway and apron. There is also an outdoor terrace with seating. A variety of seating and furniture, from bar-style stools and chairs to comfortable sofas. There was a small area with computers and the WiFi was swift. There was no area for privacy or partly secluded parts for relaxing. The food and drinks section was self-service. Many of the breakfast items were pre-wrapped (due to covid), and there were a few pastries. But there was no hot food on offer. There was a fair selection of alcoholic and non-alcoholic drinks.
Great food, lovely ambience. A mix of regional dishes and western with ample salad options , coffee and beverages. Cozy ambiance and good orientation of seating arrangement gave a sence of privacy

Second time I’ve used this lounge in Terminal 1 at Delhi Airport. Both times it was very busy, indeed this time a staff member went round until he eventually got me a seat, albeit on a bar stool which meant my knees were higher than the table! Foods pretty good, small range of hot dishes plus chefs cooking street food, and a couple of deserts. Tea, coffee and fruit drinks in cartons. Not many screens giving you the up to date flight information and no separate wifi, so if you don’t have an Indian phone then you’ll need a voucher (available at the lounge check in) to logon.

The international lounge of Air India at Delhi Airport is a disappointment. Old, not too clean with awful food and limited selections.  Unappetizing food, tired interior, substandard toilets. The difference is amazing and very disappointing. Definitely in need of an upgrade. Hardly any changes over the years. The service is not bad. but everything else needs work!

Worst customer experience ever. Flying Air India business class and looking for the lounge at Delhi airport. Lounge has been closed for 3 years and I need to pay to go to other lounge. Air India has lost a business class frequent flyer forever!
A nice lounge with plenty of seating and a strong Internet connection. Bar/beverage options were great but the food choices could include a bit more variety, not that it is lacking though.

Used Priority Pass to enter this lounge although being an economy class passenger. A nice experience considering that most facilities at Seychelles airport (SEZ) is rather small and outdated. Food options are quite limited so do not expect to be well-fed at the lounge, but the drink options are all there ranging from beer to liquors so clearly this lounge will satisfy alcohol lovers. Moreover, a nice Internet connection is offered for its customers so staying in the lounge should be the better option for most passengers staying in the waiting area.

Business lounge serving all airlines at Mahe. Customers can also pay a fee to use Lounge. Small buffet with comfortable chairs and good views of the runway. Food runs out quickly but is soon replenished. Staff are polite and professional and will assist you in connecting to their free wifi, as well as announcing flights. 2 tv screens and a few magazines but very little else. Toilets are clean but the hand dryers are inefficient.

This was such a disappointment although the seating was nice. The auto taps in the ladies toilet were mostly not functioning event though they were auto. The plastic soap dispenser was cheap and nasty. The food on offer at the commencement of my 'stay' was the same as it was on leaving and there were some hot dishes. Plenty of alcohol available. The welcome on entering was very miserable. I apologised for being deaf due to the air pressure issue having just flown in from Fort Lauderdale. A smile, a nod of understanding would have been welcome. She just wanted my ticket - no interest in my well being.  When I went to look around the duty free shops I came across a sign for the Signature lounge which was supposed to be available but that was closed. So really a poor experience.

This was by far the best airline lounge I have ever visited. You get seated to a table, you order for an incredible menu, they bring you Piper champagne, amazing cocktails, the best chocolate cake I have ever eaten, and incredible steak cooked perfectly, truly this was an amazing lounge for full fare paying business class passengers travelling with Air Canada on international routes.

Both my husband and I have platinum status on Star Alliance and we tried to use the Air Canada lounge. The woman at the lounge refused to let us in because according to her company policy, she cannot let in anyone no earlier than 3 hours before the flight. At that time, our boarding time was only in 3 hours and 10 min. Even after waiting 10 min, she said her “system” still wasn’t allowing her to let us in because the 3-hour rule is based on the flight departure time. When we complained that we had never heard of such rule, she said she only works for her company and that’s not her problem. After this experience, I will never fly Air Canada. They need to do a better job in training their employees (or hire better) as this was the worst form of CRM I have ever experienced in 40 years of business travel.

Never buy a day pass to the Air Canada  Maple Leaf Lounge. I did this and arrived at the lounge in Toronto, and we were denied access because they were full. This would be fine, however, the airline refuses to refund my money. They say that I was “scanned in,” which absolutely never happened, and I have told them that I would pay double the cost if they could produce a video or still image of anyone from my party spending one second in the Lounge. They have produced no evidence and have never refunded my money. Do not take the chance. I would also encourage you to avoid doing business with this dishonest company.

Absolutely unacceptable that there is a new 3 hour limit starting July 13th 2023. Last time I traveled it was unlimited, there was also no mention of the limit when upgrading to business class. Major reason I upgraded was to have access to the lounge. I don't think I will be flying with Air Canada again after this.

I used a 25K pass for this lounge which was well worth the pass. The Maple Leaf Lounge in Ottawa overlooks the ramp with large picture windows. I found all of the lounge to spotless, well stocked with beverages and food (hot and cold). Seats are very comfortable and the WIFI was very fast. Staff that were in the lounge were very friendly and helpful. A great spot to decompress before your flight!

Decent food. Rude server, scoffed at me when I asked for a alcoholic beverage and said no, I had to ask her why because she didn’t offer a explanation. She said only after 11am. Granted it was early but This is a international airport with people coming in from all time zones, don’t appreciate the judgement or lack of accommodation.

Very tragic lounge. Watched a customer being turned away at the front desk due to overcapacity. Lounge is extremely crowded and dated, probably due to cardholder access nowadays. To combat this an expansion triple the size wouldn't hurt. Food selection (particularly for breakfast) is dismal and low in quality. My hashbrowns were closer to mashed potatoes. Service is casual and only helps with picking up rubbish and used plates. I don't see anything being cleaned between settings. Overall feels very unexclusive and really disappointed with the quality of Air Canada's domestic lounges.

The Air Canada Lounge is an alternative for Star Alliance passengers at Frankfurt airport. The catering is the same as in the Lufthansa lounges. The food was fine, but not spectacular. But the lounge was stylish, with lots of light, and reat views of the apron. Furthermore, it was quiet and not to crowded at the time when I visited. I can really recommend the lounge

We stopped in the AC Signature Suite at YYZ for a few hours prior to a flight back to Europe. Our hand baggage, which was extensive, was checked into a luggage room, and we were ushered to the dining room. We had cocktails, champagne, and a three course meal. The food was of high quality - probably akin to what you'd find in a Michelin Plate restaurant. The wine list was small but well curated, and the waiting staff were friendly, professional, and skilled. After eating we found a quiet area with couches to sit back and relax on. The bar area was well-stocked with the bartenders very friendly. A buffet was available adjacent to the bar serving a different selection of food from the dining room, but all of very high quality. Bathrooms were perfectly clean despite the lounge being fairly full. Unfortunately there are no shower facilities. The lounge was physically in excellent condition with no signs of wear. Although I'm not a fan of AC's tendency to use dark woods and brooding lighting I felt it somehow worked very well here. There is no view of the ramps. Overall this is an excellent lounge experience - everything that AC's marketing promises for its Signature Class product is delivered here. The only real downside to the experience was it made the flight that followed seem very mediocre by comparison.

The lounge itself has a nice and relaxing atmosphere. There are plenty of seats and also some private areas. The stuff was very nice also. The choices of food were very limited and super small portioned, but tasty. What absolutely horrified me was that the food was "served" in cardboard boxes.

Lounge is boring and hardly anybody use it despite ample space. No alcoholic beverages offered, a huge fault. Good view. Good food with 4 hot dishes at the buffet. Coffee completely burnt and undrinkable. Not worth paying for (they charge 50 USD) - outside coffee shops much more cozy to engage with. No WiFi.

The Terminal 2 Power North lounge was a bit far from the security gate and on the extension side of Terminal 2. It was really large, new, shiny with nice view over the tarmac. Flight information was well displayed on a big screen. Seat was comfortable. Free WiFi was fast. Only drink was offered, snacks were available at a fee.

The ANA Terminal 2 Lounge is the worst lounge I have ever been to. They defeat the exclusivity of the lounge by opening it to Premium Economy Customers yet alone all the credit card and Star Gold customers and their guests makes this place an utter zoo. It is nice for the Premium Economy and credit card customers but it comes at the expense of the Business Class customers who the lounges are primarily supposed to cater to on an industry level. I had a 9 hr layover at Haneda and you would think by having long connection times from North America to Southeast Asia, ANA would create a nice and comfortable for their Business Class customers. The staff are very not personal and reserve. Shower wait times were 3 hours and once you did get a shower they kept making announcements. There were dirty dishes all over the place I will never havea layover at Haneda again.  From a business aspect it makes a Business Class Customer question why they should be paying more just to have the same lounge as Premium Economy. Their flight connections from Haneda are horrible too. ANA inflight service was a B+ but their Lounge is an F.

Please keep in mind that the lounges for international passengers are totally different from the others for domestic passengers. For example, when you visit in the morning, the former serves some food suitable for breakfast while the latter does nothing, except for a packet of arare, or Japanese rice crackers. I guess what ANA intends domestic passengers to do is as follows: ANA prepares such drinks as water, coffee, tea and beer, but on the other, they should buy some food and bring in. Many shops selling various kinds of food stand in the domestic terminal.

This ANA lounge is one of the best lounges in terms of overall quality. The highlight was how spacious, clean, quasi-luxurious the showers were. Not much wait time was amazing. The water functions had extra message nozzles etc which were unique. The food/drinks variety wasn't high, but the fresh & excellently live-cooked ramen/Udon made up for it. The ambience was another amazing thing: there's something so calming and pleasant about Japanese interior design... The staff were so polite and kind as well. No wonder ANA is 5 stars!

Understated and quiet, I really like this lounge. Accessible to certain Amex Card holders, it is a sanctuary from the depressing surroundings of Melbourne Airport. Not exactly First Class, however, the free snacks are edible, drinks are nice enough and service is pleasant. The front desk person was kind enough to mind my luggage whilst I went back to the Duty-Free shop for some iPhone accessories. Wifi is good, it's not crowded and full of screaming kids, and a far more pleasant experience than the rest of the airport or the 3rd world feel of a Qantas flight across the Pacific. They have showers and private facilities available, all clean and well maintained. The only reservation I have about this lounge is that too many people may latch on to it.

Easy checkin. Its not as packed even if the airport is busy. They have 3 entrees, veggies, pork and pasta. Some pastries and sandwiches. I was expecting more of authentic Korean Meal. The plug are a little bit worn out. Seats are pretty comfortable. Easy to navigate in the airport

Very spacious lounge, quiet atmosphere, comfortable seating and good views on the tarmac and runways. Choice of food is very limited, no comparison with Thai Airlines in Bangkok, and selection of alcoholic drinks limited, with no attendants to prepare cocktails.

Used this lounge as Emirates uses this lounge service at ICN. An appalling state of food options and customers in the lounge are having instant ramen noodle . Bar and beverage options are a bit better though.

As Gold Member Star Alliance I was granted entrance, so I won’t complain too much. It is a very nice looking lounge, but quite underwhelming related to food selection. Alcoholic drinks selection is quite modest too, but as it was morning I enjoyed some coffee (which was ok). What is offered is a bit disappointing considering Seoul Incheon Airport is Asiana’s home base. One thing was really excellent: their shower facilities! Clean, relatively spacious and comfortable with all amenities one needs.

Actually a very pleasant and spacious, bright lounge. Good selection of hot and cold food, even at breakfast. Varied selection of drinks, including Prosecco. Loads of charging points with International plugs. A pleasant place to work or chill waiting for your flight.
Over booked allocation, poorly managed, tables cleared but not wiped. Lacked atmosphere and looking very tired. Not value for money. Disappointed.

The Aspire lounge is no longer a ‘Business Lounge’ and has become a place for holiday families where many are ensuring that they get their money’s worth. Impossible to work - (quiet area might help) and certainly not now an attractive option for frequent flyers. From KLM my expectations are higher. The staff work hard to keep things in order but on this (and previous) occasion it was not a pleasant experience.

Two visits and same result. If this is the best American can do then they have a long climb ahead of them. While the drinks, including champagne were very acceptable, the food and seating were pretty poor. Lots of food items on offer, sadly, most of what was on display was a repetition of the same few choices. The hot food was tepid at best and very little choice. There is a risotto station which was closed on our most recent visit. One of the worst lounges we have ever used.

This is a huge and spacious lounge with a broad selection of tapas sized hot buffet items (chef inspired entrees e.g. grilled chicken, swordfish, squash curry, samosa chat), as well as cold buffet items (sushi - different kinds, sandwiches). The lounge also offer a wide selection of premium drinks and amenities (e.g. shower suites). Since OneWorld Alliance member airlines' business class passengers have access to the lounger, the lounge was very busy and crowded for early evening departure. The reception staff as well as the culinary staff and servers were warm and friendly. WiFi was fast and easy to log into. Seating was comfortable with a view of the runways.

Nothing Flagship about it at all. As international first class lounges go, this was one of the worst I’ve experienced and not at all what I expected. The reception staff were warm and friendly, so my visit began with a great start. But on entry I soon discovered it was a small space and overcrowded. There was no a la carte dining service like New York, instead there was a buffet service and what was on offer looked old and tired. So, I decided to give the food a miss thinking it was better to wait and have dinner on board. This would later prove to have been a mistake. I did, however, take advantage of the shower facilities and there was no waiting time and the shower room was nicely designed and the shower had great water pressure.

Located in Terminal 8 at JFK International Airport is the Chelsea Flagship Lounge. It’s the most exclusive of American Airlines 3 premium lounges at JFK. Here you can sip bespoke cocktails or guzzle vintage French champagne at the stunning circular bar. Or if you’re feeling a bit peck you can enjoy meal prepared by a chef from the a la carte menu. It was quiet and relaxed when I visited the staff outnumbered guests. The food was superb and the staff super friendly and eager to please. The only drawback was the so-called ‘relaxation area’. There are no where to grab some shut-eye just a strange series of modern curved single form lounges lined up in a row and separated by a strip of fabric suspended from the roof – very exposed and very strange. But if you have access to this lounge, then I recommend to use it.

American Airlines offers 3 lounges at JFK - Greenwich, Soho and Chelsea with Chelsea being the most exclusive and dedicated to Flagship First Passengers. The lounge features and amazing circular bar and full service restaurant where you can choose from a wide range of chef prepared pre-flight meals. They serve Krug champagne and offer an excellent selection of high quality wines. The atmosphere is calm and quiet. However there is no private space to rest or take a nap. the only option being preform shaped sleeping furniture separated by a fine gold curtain - very strange.

Warm welcome at reception. Thought the chicken sliders were a great hot food idea. Very popular. Seating areas were good with great views. Nice warm lighting.  Don’t expect the champagne to flow. Drinks options are limited cheap brand options. It’s not self service - you have to ask bartender, even for soft drink ! Liquor is a thimble sized amount drowned in soda - I’d just arrived. Smartly dressed. I asked for more whiskey as I couldn’t taste it and was told no at full volume which was very embarrassing. Observed this humiliation happening to several other passengers. Romany has an unfortunate manner and requires people skills training. We walked out.

Nice new club with fresh welcoming interiors and small, but decent food options. Check in staff was efficient and courteous. Unfortunately, the bar staff was rude and unprofessional, and the options subpar. If you're going for the updated interior and limited but tasty food, then it's worth a short stay. If you're grabbing a drink and expecting quality service and drink options, then find somewhere else.

On August 17th 2023 flight number AA5594 arrived in Charlotte on time flight crew perfect 10 we went to the Admirals Club and were told it was at capacity and denied access. The staff on duty today were very rude and not customer friendly, this is unacceptable based on paying for this service. I feel there is a need for some additional customer service training. I asked if there was a call list, the answer I received was why should we have to look for you just keep coming back to check. The persons facial expressions and tone of voice was that of a person trying prove his superiority of over the customers, by far very bad for customer relations. We will be asking for a refund and never will use American Airlines again .
Pathetic. I felt sorry for the attentive wonderful staff. The food offerings were below sub par. This is consistent after several visits this year. Please American, you really look bad

I had an unexpected 4 1/2 hour delay in DC on my way home to Cincinnati. (Flights were a mess due to fog.) Rather than trying to find a seat in the overcrowded gate house (due to delays), I paid for a day pass for the American E Lounge. It was the best decision that I made for the day that I had no control of! The lounge was wonderful with plenty of room, business friendly, wonderful food options, and the most attentive staff. I have to give extra thanks to bartenders Tiana and William who were so cordial to all of the frustrated travelers that came to the E lounge bar. Their service was above and beyond…everyone was served promptly and with a genuine smile! It was so very appreciated by everyone that they served. Tiana and William are the best!

Lounge feels a little cramped and has limited choices but staff is nice and crowd reasonable. And if I compare to the crowding challenges faced with Delta Skyclubs, it is a refreshing experience. Espresso machine was out of service but regular coffee was available. What remains a mastery is the difficulty to access the lounge Internet access at Admiral Clubs … faced the problem At multiple Admiral Clubs where it takes forever to get the authentication page.

American Airlines Flagship Lounge opposite Gate D30 in Miami International. Having been in various US airport lounges before was not expecting that much, but we were actually very impressed: comfortable, spacious (good views over one of the runways) and quiet with lots of available seating. Good choice of beers, wines and spirits along with soft drink and hot drink options. Good choice of food options: at least 3 hot food choices and a counter where a chef would also serve whatever they had prepared, and a nice selection of cold meats and chesses with salads and fresh breads. Business section where you could catch up on work etc. Nice area to while away the time before your flight, and would recommend. Should have got here earlier to take full advantage.

I am writing this review to acknowledge the level of kindness and dedication I received from American Airlines employees. I was flying from Doha to Nashville through JFK. My first 14.5- hour flight landed late at 9:30 am. I missed my connection in JFK. The next flight to Nashville is at 7 pm. There was nothing I could do, I wanted to take a shower and lay down for a couple of hours. Even though AA has no responsibility about the missed connection they went out of their way to help me. Sandra who sits at the VIP counter club with incredible grace worked so hard to find me an earlier flight but there was nothing available. Nevertheless, she was incredibly sympathetic and helpful. Thank you Sandra. AA should be proud to have you.

The only saving grace was the lovely attentive staff. The food and drink offerings were pathetic and truly terrible. The food tasted like it had already been re heated twice and was inedible. The drink choices were poor and the only cream for coffee was fake cream. Inexcusable. The staff seemed embarrassed, I felt bad for them. The Covid excuse doesn’t fly anymore. AA let your great staff be proud of what they offer and make your customers feel valued

I was very excited to check out the new DFW Admirals Club in Terminal E. However, very disappointed. The food bar with the hummus, dressing and dips appeared to be sitting out so long they had crust on the top of them and around the edges. Nothing looked like it was attended to in quite a while. Afraid to eat anything I didn't want to get food poisoning. I actually put on gloves and lifted silver bowls that hummus was in. Room temperature not good! Plan B “Soup” it was crusted and separated. It was so disgusting I grabbed a piece of fruit and went to my gate. Attendant did stir things a little but didn't rotate things out or offer to get me something fresh. Very disappointed!

I tried to recall why I never fly American but was reminded when I entered the Admirals Club. I presented my first class ticket and the agent said “ why do you think you have access to this club”. I stated that I thought my ticket allowed for it. I was informed that only on international travel. I asked if they had a daily rate and proceeded to pay with my platinum american express. The agent couldn't have been more rude or irritated. The lounge looked like a school cafeteria. I have no problem with their policies and I am happy to pay for extra services. American Airlines… you dont beat your competition with rude associates and doing things on the cheap. Now I recall why I dont travel with American.

First Class ticket in hand and over one Million Miles flown, I proceeded to the Admirals Lounge and was denied entry and told only if you pay the $450 fee and get their credit card would you gain access. My First Class Ticket meant nothing to the Staff or American Airlines My million miles flown Status means nothing to the staff or American Airlines. So I went to the B gate Admirals club just to double check if what I actually heard is true. I approached the lady at the desk and said I just want to confirm two things please. I am not looking to argue I just want to make sure I am correct in two things as I will write a review later. Can you please a confirm to me that my First Class ticket and my million mile status mean nothing to American Airlines in regards to gaining access to this lounge. She eventually confirmed what I said after trying to argue with me and tell me all the merits of buying the credit card etc. When I kept explaining to her “ I know it’s not your fault but I just want to confirm two things for my review”. And she kept on arguing and I finally had to tell her - you can write your review but I just need to confirm this. So I was harassed and badgered even just trying to get the facts straight after being told to go for a long walk and your million miles flown and First Class ticket neither matter at All to American Airlines To Add insults to Injury during the flight instead of 20 minutes into the flight or 20 minutes before landing— nope right in the middle about an hour 20 min from landing when half the plane was asleep they broke in for an almost two minute sales job of the Credit Card and bonus miles etc etc etc. American Airlines has become horrific and I will use up my miles but not be giving them anymore of my hard earned money.

Lounge does not have a lot of comfortable chairs. Food and drinks are doled out by a staff member upon request. In other words, unlike most other lounges, food and drink are not available for del-serve.

This lounge is a mixed lounge : business class passengers and pay to use together. The lounge despite rather large is very dated. Also not so easy to find. There is quite some food available what is replenished quite often, where it is going wrong are the drinks and the drinks service in particular. You cannot take your drinks by yourself, ok for the wine but for the soft drinks as well. The drinks are in a fridge not working very well - service people were extremely rude and long faced to everybody. The soft drinks were not chilled even lukewarm - when you were asking a soft drink they gave you a bottle of half a liter - the drink was not chilled at all - so i asked for a glass with ice - one cube - i had to insist to receive 3 cubes of ice.  Restrooms were soso

Visited both of the open Star Alliance lounges at VIE. They currently have an inane policy whereby you cannot consume anything in the lounge; it is all to go. Oddly, you can take the to go food and beverages and consume them outside of the lounge. It makes no sense. Offerings are very basic, water, juice, coffee, sandwiches. No wine or beer. Easily the worst lounges I have ever been to. I realize we’re battling a pandemic, but we are dealing with airline passengers crammed together in a metal tube, taking off masks to eat and drink. The lounge actually offers the ability to distance. In both lounges, the washrooms are very tiny, dated, and gave zero amenities.

Horrible lounge - very uncomfortable chairs, bad food. For pay as you go guests $40 if you pay USD and €25 if you pay Euro - despite the fact that these two currencies are roughly at parity. Really you are just as well off sitting on the floor outside. Total dump.

lounge_name: Madrid Puerta del Sol Aena lounge
review: This lounge is like the tedious inevitability of an unloved season. Only breakfast on offer was cold bread and cereal. They have not invested in a single toaster.

Terminal G is mostly used by Air France for short haul regional flights. The terminal itself is not really big and practical if you connect on two regional Air France flights, as long the flight arrive/depart from the same terminal. It gives you the feeling of a regional small airport. The same feeling is the in Air France’s business lounge in this terminal. It is easy to find, it is not too big and it is overcrowded. There is little choice of food and drinks. Lavatories are a too few for the crowds and though “shower facilities” are being displayed (for those connecting from long haul flights, as I did), definitely it is not great luxury or even practical. However, a big compliment to the staff: always used cups and dishes were taken and everything was cleaned up instantly.
A shame. No friendly welcome. Completely packed, therefore slow Wi-Fi. Dirty toilets. Bad food. Cheap Champagne. Rude passengers everywhere from other airlines.

The lounge in Koh Samui was small but pretty good. It had great air conditioning and the beverages were good (I didn’t try the food, but the choices were good). The staff members were polite and friendly. There are no flight announcements, but the supervisor comes out and calls out people for the particular flight that has started boarding. My complaints were that the toilets were dirty and smelly and the WiFi was very poor. Overall good lounge, definitely recommend!

Boutique lounge in keeping with the airline marketing philosophy. Good choice of food and beverages; massage recliners and a lovely hot shower. Well worth the extra B1500 to fly in Business Class to access this lounge

Island style – if I were only allowed to use two words to describe the airport. The airy wide open spaces, lack of walls, and abundance of palm trees just get you into the island lifestyle mood straight away. Tasteful, bright and light nautical/beach themes permeate the airport, and the executive lounge is no different. I actually wish I had missed my flight.

I had an economy ticket from Belgrade to Ljubjana, Slovenia, but I paid my way to Air Serbia Business lounge. Price was Euro 35. That was a total mistake. The lounge is a joke. It is dark, unfriendly with terrible food. Avoid it, please. In comparison it's much better to join one of the cafes elsewhere at the airport. An airport which by the way is more or less a dump.

Aeromexico has a lounge at Mexico City airport but it is closed for renovation. So Business Class passengers are sent to the Heineken lounge which is some distance from their flight gates. The lounge is Spartan, noisy and not a place to rest before a flight. Wi-fi is very difficult to access. To make matters worse, I was refused entry because having landed from Cuba, my onward flight left more than 3 hours later. When I was allowed in there was no food except yoghurt. The staff were very friendly but they have nothing to offer. Avoid if possible.

I think it is the worst lounge I have been. Crowded, uncomfortable, bad food or better said, no food at all. When they bring food out, it is like vultures, people run to it like they have never eaten before. It seems that people there love whatever is free. This lounge accepts just about anyone. You pay a fee and you get in... booze flows, I think that is why people pay to get in.

Appalling. Overcrowded, loud. people and bags and backpacks everywhere. Completely unrelaxing, impossible to work or read. This is what intercontinental business class passengers get? Definitely not worth paying for. This feels more like a bus terminal.
Well appointed lounge, comfortable seating and layout. Enjoyed the coffee we had. Did not eat anything because we had enjoyed lunch prior to arriving in the lounge area.

Dreadful, dated, filthy lounge. Poor, uncomfortable sagging seating. Areas under semi-permanent repair. Broken, stained table lamps. Bad food. Try to avoid passing through Shanghai Pudong airport if at all possible.

During my visit, the wine service area was completely empty. Despite menu signs listing a variety of wines, not a single bottle was available. Furthermore, the food selection was poor and meager. For a lounge of this class, the variety and quality of catering were unacceptable and did not meet basic expectations. Attached is photographic evidence showing only the empty stands. Staff made no attempt to restock the selection during my entire visit. This is unacceptable for a lounge experience

The aircon didn't work in majority of the lounge areas, except a little room which was selling merchandise. As a result guests had to sit on corners/thick-chairs which had a portable "cooler" which made little difference in the humid heat. The stuffy conditions made many guests wanting to shower. However, the controlled "booking" system meant many having to wait hours before they can use one. I got told it takes "this long because it's 30min per usage". Ridiculous! Nevertheless the showers and nap rooms were very clean and good standard. The cleanliness of other areas though, like for example the toilets were simply not good enough. Staffing was a bizzare issue. Despite being seen everywhere and being very hardworking, no one attended areas where guests needed help, like the tea bar and drinks bar. Guests had to go into the display area to help themselves to cognac etc. In the end, there was a lack of orderliness and the lounge became noisy. And the other area seriously need improving is the English skills. Simple words like "soy sauce / AC" couldn't be understood. The Chinese food offerings were sumptous though: amazing buffet and live wonton-soup making. Wonderful!

Above average lounge because it was not crowded to the rafters. Food and drink were also better than average in terms of taste and variety. They had Neuhaus chef doing a demo and gave out samples. Business class passengers on get a complimentary box of this chocolate on deplaning. Only downside is that if you are connecting in Brussels to an intra European flight to get Terminal A from B is torture since they only have 2 immigration officers processing a very long line. Not sure I would go through Brussels again. You would never make a tight connection.
Really bad lounge. Food is disgusting and SN staff at desk is the worst helping and unwelcoming. Seats are comfortable but that is all the lounge has for itself.

As the lounge opened at 5am, I was able to get in early to take a shower and a short sleep in the 'Nap Room' for a couple of hours. The Nap Rooms are quite modest and have firm single beds with a small pillow and blanket provided. The shower facilities were good. The lounge is large and spacious, with a variety of furnishings. There is also a colourful children's room and play area. There are two areas of food displays, and the selection was excellent. An attractive self-service bar has a few spirits and a wider selection of wines (including sparkling) and beers. The whole length of one side of the lounge has a clear sight of the apron. Within the lounge is also a shop displaying a selection of Neuhaus Belgian chocolates, which could be tasted before buying. In a joint venture, the airline with Nexus cars meant their product placements are also everywhere.

It isn't a large lounge, but a pleasant place to relax for a couple of hours. The variety of furnishings is interspersed with artificial greenery. There are a few semi-private cubicles to do some work or have a bit of privacy. It got busy for a while late afternoon. However, the staff were quick to clear leftovers. The food selection was modest, a salad bar, charcuterie, pastries and a few hot items. There were plenty of soft drinks, beers on tap, and a few spirits and wines. The lounge is not lavish whatsoever, but it functions well for a short time. There are shower facilities.

The Loft is designed rather beautiful and the people at reception desk are usually friendly, however the catering is really sub par : basic bakery products, jams out of dispensers , the cold cuts and cheeses are of a poor quality and I simply did not risk to eat anything from the "hot" better said lukewarm breakfast Drinks out of dispensers, wines and licor : the cheapest quality. For breakfast there are some salads on display suitable for a lunch. Most people of the service team are not speaking Dutch at all. The restrooms were not very clean, the computers did not work anymore and no newspapers or mags at all - the receptionist did explain those will not on offer again in the future.

Probably one of the dirtiest lounges I have ever seen with food left over everywhere. Showers (as advertised) were not available. Quality of food was extremely bad: canned cassoulet, greasy veal, gyro, all unhealthy. Meals were extremely salty. Deserts were all industrial margarine style. Chocolate stand was closed. Very limited choice of drinks. A sad experience.

Newly opened this week This is a wonderfully typical Centurion Lounge with one great exception. The staff is proactive, efficient, and extremely friendly. The food, as always is plentiful and quite good. I was there for breakfast so I wasn’t able to try out the impressive looking Whiskey Bar. There is also a terrific covered outdoor area with ramp views. All in all, a winner

As a Business Class passenger on an Air France Flight from HND to CDG, I had two options on which lounge to visit before boarding: JAL’s Sakura Lounge or Delta’s Sky Club. I visited the Delta lounge for the first time. Less company and more individual cares than the JAL’s counterpart. At the bar counter many kinds of liquor were served though I missed champagne. While I was taking a meal over a glass of red wine, one of the staff was pushing a cart loaded with fried chicken or something, which seemed to me their specialty, and approaching my table. She offered me one and naturally I took it. I found it delicious.

I returned from a trip to Mexico yesterday with my wife and 8-year-old child. On my way down the previous Saturday, we had a layover in SLC from GEG and took them to the Delta Lounge. I have a Reserve card and was going to use one of my passes for my wife and my daughter I assumed would just come along. After showing my boarding pass the attendant then typed some things to allow my wife in with one of my passes and we enjoyed some time in the lounge before flying out. On the way back yesterday we again stopped in at the lounge between flights. I scanned my boarding pass and the attendant then came over and I said I had another pass for my wife. They said all passes had been used a few days earlier. I said that must be a mistake because I had two and only used one for my wife. They told me both had been used, for my wife and child. The attendant then told me the charge for both of them to enter the lounge would then be $100. I understood the $50 for my wife but I was very taken aback that I was being charged $50 for my 8-year-old daughter who was only going to have a cookie or two! $50 for an adult I completely understand with liquor and food, but a child cannot possibly warrant a $50 charge. I paid the fee because we were already there and my daughter was looking forward to going back and having a cookie, but I felt, and have continued to feel, taken advantage of and this experience has left a very uncomfortable feeling with me. To add more insult once inside they closed down half the lounge's food serving area during dinner time and the lines backed up and the food coming out slowed down. I have always enjoyed the lounge when traveling by myself or with my wife but going forward cannot warrant the cost of bringing a small child so will not be going at all. I don't know if I will continue my business with Delta because of this. It was a very unfortunate ending to a great vacation. I called Medallion customer care to inquire about this and was very bluntly told that this is just the way it is. I think it may be time to give another airline a try.

Another overrun day in a Delta Sky Lounge in Atlanta. I travel through Atlanta at least 2x per week. The lounges in all concourses are over run and generally staffed with employees with abysmal attitudes. Terminal E on Sunday evening 9/10/2023 - very crowded, dirty (cleaned a side table myself from leftover food and drink), People using cell phones and devices without headphones. If Delta think's they are treating their best customers well, they are sadly mistaken. If there were any viable choice in the South East of the US, I would gladly abandon Delta as a "Diamond Medallion" all I get from Delta is constantly late flights, lounges that are overrun, and staffed by employees with bad attitudes.
Impressive food and drink offerings. Very fresh variety including vegan and ethnic. Comfortable seating and great view of tarmac. Gigantic improvement

The finest lounge I've ever visited in America. It is brand-new, with enormous windows, a large capacity, and an open, airy interior. With over 50 culinary options and excellent service, this restaurant takes the cake. Other airport lounges ought to emulate this one.
Beautiful lounge here in New York and very welcoming service. Special shout out to agent Marilyn Henry for her courtesy and sartorial correctness. Highly recommend.

This lounge is truly dreadful. There is plenty of of food but it was there for ages and looked absolutely ghastly high risk of getting sick from the food. The staff were on their phones the whole time. Just a pretty awful experience.

Having read about the refurbishment of the BA T5 first class lounge I was keen to see the improvements. What an anticlimax! The revamped check in area with its new red/terracotta colour scheme was underwhelming. We headed to the lounge via the dedicated security screening expecting great things, but the lounge looks exactly the same! This revamp is just a bit of window dressing, with no real improvement to the lounge itself. Yet again, style over substance. Not impressed ... disappointed!

The lounge is clean but the seats are worn, and there is not enough space to accommodate all the passengers travelling in Club and those with silver and having access to the lounge. Nothing wrong, decent sandwiches but no hot food only soup, decent choice of alcoholic beverages and acceptable wines. Service with a smile. vOnly a shame the restrooms are extremely basic and not very clean.

The lounge is very spacious with a wide variety of areas to sit and a kids play area. Food was amazing with hot cooked foods at breakfast. Alcoholic beverages were limited to wine / sparking wine as it was morning. Very clean and showers are available, which was great after connecting from an overnight flight from New York. Staff were welcoming and friendly.

Tatty and uncared for, the BA business lounge in Gatwick South Terminal seems to be unloved and uncared for. The staff try hard but there is little loyalty (they do not work for BA) Information on flights is scarce due to them not working direct and on one occasion they were told by BA to “stop bothering them” when they were trying to ascertain the status of a much delayed flight. Despite the flight having been delayed for over five hours the customers were kicked out of the lounge two hours before boarding as it was closing. I would certainly never fly with this truly rotten and totally incompetent airline again.

Crowded or rather "overcrowded" as usual. The catering staff in the lounge are nice, polite and helpful - in contrast to the reception BA staff who are rude, abrasive and have no right to be facing customers. The toilets are terrible, long queues to access one, no urinals so all men have to queue up for the single toilets. As with so many other parts of the famous BA cost-cutting, all magazines and newspapers have not been returned after Covid, and this is now a further drop in standards. Food is okay, but hot food is real canteen style and not a match on many airlines first class standards. To call this a "First" lounge is a disgrace, and you are probably better off going to one of the restaurants in the main departure hall. And one thing you will note, Heathrow public toilets are nicer and kept cleaner than the BA lounge facilities.

Flew London to Kalamata and as a Silver/Saphire member used the Galleries South Lounge. COVID had meant that food offerings had been stripped back to a bare minimum, but I am pleased that a full service has been resumed. Quite busy but found two comfortable seats easily enough. Had a decent full English breakfast with a glass of champagne and very good cup or two of coffee. Much better, BA.

We were at The British Airways Terminal 5 South Business Lounge at Heathrow Airport on the evening of April 24, 2023. We were shocked to see not one but three mice running under and around our chairs and table. The wait staff told me the lounge is infested with mice and that British Airways and Heathrow Airport have known about this for months. I was so disgusted that I left. I was then told by a flight attendant that their crew lounge is also infested with mice. Lastly, I was told by an airport meet and greet that the problem is not just limited to the British Air lounges. In addition to the active mice, the lounge was very dark, the tables were dirty as was the glassware. Totally disgusting and unacceptable. The health department needs to close the lounge in my opinion.

A pretty underwhelming experience. The staff on the desk to greet us were quite cold and unwelcoming. The same was true of the staff on the baggage storage desk and the shower suite desk. The shower facilities were in desperate need of refurbishment. As is the lounge in general. The food on offer was quite nice and the atmosphere was quiet and relaxed which is what we needed after a very long flight. Bottom line though is BA really need to improve the quality of their staff and give this particular lounge a refresh.

I travelled on a weekend which I never normally do, so was taken aback by how busy the lounge was. I did find a decent seat luckily, and tried from both the breakfast and lunch menu. Both offered a decent selection of nice food and beverages. On the wine side a really ordinary Prosecco was available to self serve but you needed to order champagne. I did find a really good Sauvignon which exceeded my expectations and only wish that happened more. The staff were very good at keeping a really busy lounge not looking too distressed with the volume of customers. Generally not a bad experience but hardly outstanding, I guess you need to head to the Gulf States for that.

Arrived from Johannesburg and went to the Concorde Room for breakfast. Thirty minutes after ordering nothing arrived, apparently order lost between the dining area and the kitchen. Lounge not busy so no excuse for this shoddy level of service. It was a chaotic shambles, and given that this is BA's flagship lounge it was extremely disappointing. I eventually went to the First lounge and had breakfast there. The staff in the Concorde lounge really need a refresher course, there is no excuse for getting something so straightforward wrong.

BA Business Class ticket holders access Escape Lounge, which is also a pay per use lounge. Compared with BA’s lounges around the world, this is as basic as it gets. Self service hot and cold snacks, soft drinks and tea/coffee. Alcohol on request from the bar. The wines are cheap and don’t compare to business class offerings at BA. Lounge is tidy. There’s a waste trolley on view where staff scrape dirty plates into the bin and stack dirty plates. Very off putting. Staff like to chat amongst themselves. The ‘meet and greet’ person on the lounge was glued to her chair and social media, shouting ‘Hiya’ and ‘See Ya’ every now and again. The lounge is a nice escape from the crowds downstairs with lots of charging points for devices.

Only a few USB ports are working. Food offerings were better than before. Drink choices have been limited to minimalist. No more Zacapa rum or Woodford Reserve. Not even Jack Daniels if u don’t like Bulleit Bourbon. That includes onboard. Packed lounge with sun boiling anyone sitting in its way as there’s no window shading. Staff were working hard I felt given the amount of people. Bottled water removed. Shame as it was handy. Only tiny 250ml beer cans available. No Tiger or Amstel choices…

Having paid BA over £7000 for our trip to Barbados we rather thought we might be able to get some breakfast before boarding. We tried a very overcrowded lounge soon after security and managed a small plate of baked beans. Toast and bacon were not on offer. A member of the lounge staff tipped us off that the business lounge in C satellite would be more comfortable so we went there. Much less crowded but the same lack of breakfast on offer.

The food was surprisingly good. Back to self service breakfast and lunch. Plenty of drinks selection but sadly no more Gentleman Jack or Woodford Reserve. Also no Zacapa rum which is  disappointing. Bulleit bourbon is simply awful. For a Saturday afternoon, there was plenty of seats. Staff all very polite and friendly.

Others have reviewed this quite harshly. Our experience could not have been better. In fact this is one of the best lounges we have visited and we have been to many other business lounges. Its nearly up there with Istanbul and Singapore. Very well laid out, with plenty of space and places to sit/eat. The choice and variety of food was excellent. We arrived just at the breakfast/ lunch changeover. So, we had a pretty great choice!! This lounge is in total contrast to the Swiss Business lounge at Zurich which we visited the day before that was just pathetic.  A very good lounge.

Way too crowded with many people walking around looking for a place to sit. No champagne at the champagne bar (although a staff member did bring a tray of filled glasses after mentioning that passengers were walking off with the bottles!) BA used to have a display in the terminal showing how crowded each of the T5 lounges were, but that wasn't visible this time. Staff were trying valiantly, but the number of people was simply too much for them to do more than the bare minimum of clearing glasses and dishes. Next time I think I'll just have a glass of champagne and some nice oysters outside - even if I have to pay, it will definitely be more comfortable and less stressful.
Awful experience. Overcrowded, inedible food, disgusting toilets. We left almost immediately and went to sit in the Terminal. BA should be ashamed of this facility.

The British Airways Lounge is excellent. I had a nice cream tea, though I avoided the tea and had strawberry Baileys instead, the scone was excellent the clotted cream great and the strawberry jam nice, after that I went through to the rest area where high-tech seats are available but I have a 20 minute limit, however since there were very few people waiting I just used another and another 20 minutes with no problem, Disadvantages of the BA lounge were that there were very few charging points available beside the seats in the rest area there was a charging point but elsewhere they were few and far between, The drink selection was good apart from a rather unusual absence of cognac Armagnac or brandy, however the strawberry Baileys and birthday cake Baileys along with a wide selection of other choices made up for the missing Brandy. The food was excellent.
Terminal 5B lounge is so much better than the T5A lounge. Nice and quiet. It is worth the train and walk back to the main terminal. The lounge at T5A is huge and quite impersonal.
Not British Airways best. Very badly laid out lounge, limited facilities and no views. However, staff very nice. The terminal is being rebuilt so hopefully this will improve.

Used on Wednesday 16 March before our flight to Barbados. Busy but could still find a comfortable seat, and a reasonable selection of drinks on offer. Coffee machines working this time (most were not November 2021), and very good coffee it was. Unfortunately and as I suspected in November 2021 the food offering has further declined: the hot offering was just a Bacon Roll only this time without even hash browns. A couple of nice pastries on offer. It is clear that BA are now using COVID as the excuse to downgrade their offerings and cost cut. What used to be a very nice lounge with a decent buffet breakfast selection has now gone for good, I fear.
Well organised lounge. Light, airy and decent food. Food was pretty good and coffee was excellent as you'd expect in Italy. Not so sure it'd be the best for a long stop but great for short.
Possibly the worst lounge with the most miserable staff. Many people haven't flown for a long time and lounges methods have changed. Poor food. Rude staff and disgusting toilets.

Nice views of the runway in one section but very crowded and thus uncomfortable. Good selection of drinks but their app system of ordering food (no buffet) means that when it gets delivered to your table means it is cold. Weird setup in there and certainly not conducive to a relaxed wait for your flight. I am sure that BA can do better, stressed passengers do not deal with the inevitable delayed flight as well as relaxed ones.
The lounge has been refurbished since my last visit but difficult to see any major changes. However, very pleasant and fantastically helpful staff - full marks to them!

Used this Lounge on 5th November before our flight to Tenerife. Still a reasonably comfortable place to wait for your flight with a good selection of drinks. However, since COVID-19 the standard of the food offering has declined dramatically with just a Bacon Roll and Hash Browns as the main hot offering. Food also has to be ordered by a Lounge App and you will be served at your table. At least 2 of the coffee machines were not working and causing problems. No longer a real Premium offering - one can only hope that when COVID eventually dies down the lounge can return to its former decent buffet. But I'm not holding my breath - BA may just use this as an excuse to become the new "normal" lounge service.

What a beautiful new lounge in E20 gate at Beijing capital airport. After 9 months closed and obliged to go to the awful BGS lounge, this lounge is amazing. Confort, good food, nice staff. All the usual seen in CX lounges in Hong Kong.

Their sit-down restaurant concept is genius. Bangkok is my home base now and they have a wide selection of food featuring their signature Pad Thai,unique for their Bangkok Lounge, and their usual dumplings, noodle dishes and more. Bangkok is not Cathay's largest lounge but it beats Thai Airways Royal Silk Lounge and Eva Airways Lounge at Bangkok. The lounge never was not overcrowded and I've flown out of there many times. The bar area, seating area and the work stations with PC monitors are comfortable and nice. The only thing the Bangkok Lounge is missing are showers.

The Cathay Pacific First Class lounge truly exceeds expectations. It’s one of the best lounges I’ve experienced better than even Qatar Airways’ renowned offering. From the complimentary massages to the exceptional five-star dining, every detail is top-notch. The food quality is outstanding, and the island bar offers fantastic service that enhances the entire experience. I felt incredibly welcomed and comfortable throughout my visit, thanks to the amazing staff who make this lounge so special. A huge thank you to them for creating such a memorable experience!

I visited it several times and disappointed. It was impossible to get a massage even if you're in transit for 4 hours. A sort of online booking for the lucky ones and especially their guest. The buffet was also  very limited. It's a total failure in terms of hospitality.

I was flying CX from BKK to HKG in economy, but as a member of Thailand Privilege, I was entitled to access the Miracle lounge, and used the one next to the gates G, to which the lounge provides a direct access. There was a reasonable choice of alcoholic beverages, good sandwiches, an excellent pumpkin soup and different kinds of soft drinks and ice creams. The lounge is quiet, gives a feeling of intimacy and seating is comfortable.

Took a flight with Cathay Pacific that consist of two flight with one flight being First Class and the other being Business class while I transit in Hong Kong Airport. Based on Cathay Pacific website, by right I should be able to use the First Class lounge (as it is stated they will honour the highest tier for the whole journey. I arrived in Hong Kong Airport at around 10pm and my departing flight is at 8am the following day. When I went to the first class lounge, I tried to double confirm on the lounge policy that I am eligible for the use of First Class lounge. The staff at the wing insist that I could only use the first class lounge until midnight and have to go to the business class lounge after. When I informed her that it’s stated otherwise in their website, she demanded that I show her. Despite showing her the website, she insist that the policy is such and I can’t enter the first class lounge after. When I requested to speak to the manager, she questioned me if I still want to use the lounge and brushed off my request. As I wanted to shower after my flight, I told her to arrange for me to speak to the manager. She agreed but clearly did not as I had to verified with the manager (whom I had to inform another staff after I showered) that no one had informed her of my request. The whole experience is just unwelcoming.

Lounge closed for renovations, over peak travel time at Easter? Nothing else open a this late hour at Logan. The BA lounge closes at 2100, CX could have used this one and extended the timing but chose to save money and not bother. Got a vague email about getting 'points' for the hassle. The real hassle is choosing a late flight thinking at least you can wait in the lounge and it will be open until 1230 only to find that nothing is open. Poor show from CX.

It is one of the biggest lounges and has sections like Bar, Tea House, Sleeping pods, Showers, Noodle Bar, Continental. I had a layover of 6 hours. They have plenty of showers so no waiting. If you are a business class traveler and transiting Hong Kong Airport, I highly recommend visiting this lounge.

What a terrible place. After a grumpy "welcome" (we were on a code share flight so had a boarding pass headed Air New Zealand but with a clear Cathay flight identified for our next leg) we entered the fetid atmosphere of a poorly ventilated overcrowded lounge. It was noisy, had very dirty seats, particularly those with a fabric covering which had stains and were thick with dust in crevices between the cushion and the chair. It was impossible to find a quiet space or to distance form other passengers, many of whom were talking loudly and some of whom were constantly coughing. The food offering was very poor; not everyone wants noodles or soup. We left the lounge exhausted, not refreshed. We won't be using it, or Cathay, again.
The lounge is disproportionately small in relation to the number of travelers it accommodates, which is its primary downside. Apart from this matter the lounge is fine.
An upgrade over the last lounge which was bad. However, this new lounge is crowded, hot and still dirty. Food selection is poor quality and no coffee machine is working at breakfast.

The check-in staff at Cairo are extremely friendly and efficient but my business class lounge experience borders on embarrassing. I found myself in the Alioth Lounge. Bright lighting with dated furniture. I didn't find anything enticing to eat.

I am waiting for my international flight in one of the Egypt Air lounges in terminal 3. One would expect that at this airline's home base there would be good lounges or at least one. That does not appear to be the case. The food selection is poor. There are a couple of hot dishes, some overcooked vegetables and a meat of some sort. The sandwiches look like the ones I have had on my internal flights, dry and unappealing. There are no showers and the washroom is rather small, although efforts are being made to keep it clean. No newspapers or magazines and a couple of televisions with Egyptian news. The internet connection seems to be quite weak. Of course, this being Egypt no alcoholic beverages are offered, although this is not the greatest failing. All in all a disappointment.

A make-shift lounge that was put together as the regular lounges (for some odd reason have closed). Very little seating, a small fridge with water, cold drinks and stale sandwiches, three empty bain-maries and that's it. I would be extremely upset had I used my own money to get in. Thankfully it has Wi-Fi and a decent coffee machine. Still very far off the mark for a paid airport lounge.

Nothing in appearance has changed since my last visit six months ago, except for a model of the A380 at the entrance. The staff are welcoming and prompt me to order some drinks and food. It was nice to begin the evening at the bar, being served champagne and warm cashews. The lounge features an elegant restaurant-style dining area with table service, offering a menu that showcases an enticing selection of dishes. Hard to resist. Yet as mine was a night departure to Abu Dhabi, I wasn't keen on having a full meal, as I expected dinner during the flight. Deciding to help myself to a light snack, I moved to settle in a quiet corner, where I was served coffee a couple of times. The staff are also attentive, making sure the place is tidy and leftovers are cleared promptly. Although not a large lounge, it never gets crowded, as at most it will accommodate just premium passengers per flight. So there is plenty of seating options and even a few quiet spots. I also like the decor, with ark oak panelling and pretty ornamental objects placed in them. It was another enjoyable time spent here before my short walk to the boarding gate.

On my flights to Asia, I deliberately break my journey in Abu Dhabi to refresh and relax before the next connecting flight. I have visited this huge 3-storey lounge several times, and have always enjoyed my stay. The staff are polite, friendly and accommodating. The plethora of seating areas means that even when busy, you can find cosy spots to relax and have some privacy. And on long layovers, having a private relaxation room for a few hours to get some sleep is a bonus. All floors have a view of the apron, and from the ground floor, you can also watch aircraft taking off. For hungry souls, the food choices are Middle Eastern, Asian and Western. The selection may not be extensive, nevertheless appetising. The main dining room is self-service. And there is also a chef who will prepare a selection of dishes to your liking, while on the third floor, the dining area is a buffet. What always impresses me is also the presentation of food. There are tea & coffee stations on all floors and snacks you can help yourself to. And of course, the fabulous Constellation Bar, serving champagne and cocktails, is a treat.

A first-class venue without a first-class experience. I am rarely impressed by non-airline lounges, as they lack the ambiance of an airlines own lounges. However, many carriers do not have their own lounges at all airports and Plaza Premium Lounges are a popular choice around the world. On my Etihad flight to Abu Dhabi, at the check-in desk, I was informed that I was eligible for the Plaza Premium First near Gate 1, and given directions. At the entrance, I was rewarded with a friendly welcome. At first glance, the view looked attractive with Christmas decorations and Poinsettia flowers. The place was, however, fairly busy and worse - noisy. It isn't a large venue, and although there are sections of different furnishings to choose from, there isn't any place for even the slightest of privacy or quietness. The focal point is the semicircular bar, which was well stocked with drinks and a small selection of cold cuts. And the friendly bar person kindly made an excellent gin-martini, and I managed to find a less crowded spot to settle down. There is a separate dining area with a selection of hot food. However, it was a dull, uninviting place. I guess I was unlucky to be there during a busy period. And I am sure it would have been a more pleasurable and relaxing experience had it not been so noisy. Nevertheless, I did enjoy a couple of drinks and a snack, and a little disappointed before moving on. To refer to it as a 'first class' lounge in my opinion is a gross exaggeration.

A very spacious lounge with three floors. The seat were comfortable. The pasta station offers a great variety of options. There were plenty of drinks. The shower was clean and well maintained but could be in shortage during peak hours.

Flying with Etihad from Singapore to Abu Dhabi, I visited the Ambassador Transit Lounge at Terminal 2. It's a pay lounge, but as a Business Class passenger, I could use it for free. It's a compact lounge, with a few choices of seating, and a small outdoor area designated mainly for smokers, and with a view of the apron. Although not crowded when I arrived, it was quite noisy, and there was no chance of a quiet relaxation time. The moment I entered, the staff were enthusiastic to point me in the direction of food and drink and informed that shower facilities are available. The shower room was very basic, just a towel, shampoo and body wash. However, I glanced at the food and drink available. At first sight, the choice was meagre and some buffet items just did not look appetising. However, there is a small cooking station, and I was treated to a very tasty noodle soup. On the beverages front, the usual soft drinks and coffees are self-service. There was a very small selection of spirits,  The overall ambiance of the lounge at first feels good, but the layout does not afford enough space for a quiet time. It is designed for a short stay and is not my choice for a relaxing time before a flight. The food display was also rather 'cheap' looking. If I had to pay to visit this lounge, expecting a touch of extravagance, I would be very disappointed. But I would give it the thumbs up for the pleasant and attentive staff.

Etihad's Business Lounge at the new Terminal A will impress. Taking up three floors, and covering a vast area, it has an extensive variety of seating, relaxing areas and dining options. Located near the C Gates, it has access to a few gates directly from the lounge. I had an extra long layover before my flight to Osaka, and upon welcoming me to the lounge, I was told I could have a private Relaxation Room available within half an hour. In the meantime, I was able to store my hand luggage and free to wander about. After momentarily exploring the floors via escalators, I was offered a room at the time allocated. It's modest, to say the least, with a single bed, pillow and blanket. As I had landed late at night, it was a welcome treat to get some proper sleep, which I did for about four hours. Waking up very early morning, following a shower and refreshed, I decided to explore each floor. It was eerily quiet, with a few other passengers wandering about like me. I kept bumping into very friendly staff greeting me and advising me of the various areas to relax and have some food and drink. On the ground floor alone, is an extensive dining area with bars, drinks and coffee stations, and at the 'live' kitchen a chef cooked breakfast for me. There are multiple self-service snack bars, tea and coffee stations, spread across all floors. While there was a good selection of International food items and cold buffets, the choice of hot food was disappointing. I have been in much smaller lounges that have more hot food dishes. The Constellation Bar on the third floor, is both stylish and attractive, with a backlit display of alcoholic bottles. The barmen will make a cocktail or mocktail at your request and even adjust measures to suit your liking. And naturally, at busy times this is the most popular area occupied by guests. There's a fair bit of walking to do, as the lounge is huge. The colour schemes and decor are varied, with different styles of furnishings, and make you feel you can enjoy different parts of the lounge. There's a large Family Room, Games Room, Prayer Room, as well as a Smoking Room. Then there's the huge lengthy glass panelling, giving views of the apron as well as sightings of aircraft. It was nice to sit by and watch the sunrise as the very first flights of the day took off. By lunch time however, the main bar and food stations began to get busy. Yet there were plenty of areas to choose to relax and call your own little space. This is one of the best lounges I have visited. And if you have a long layover, it's a perfect place to relax and enjoy.

It's a lounge I have visited before, and it caters to both First and Business Class passengers, thus elevating the dining experience with an a la carte menu and restaurant-style atmosphere. The entrance area is rather modest but has a fairly large model of an A380 aircraft on display. The receptionist welcomed me and offered to help store my cabin baggage. I love the ambiance of this lounge, with soothing colours. As you enter, on the left is the bar with a good selection of premium brand spirits and wines. To your right are all the various seating areas. And it's quiet, it never got crowded. The staff were extremely accommodating and seem to enjoy taking care of you. All the basic facilities are available such as a variety of furnishings, showers, a children's playroom, and prayer room. As my flight was late afternoon, I had decided to have an early lunch. Browsing at the buffet area, all of which looked very appetizing, I decided to help myself instead of ordering from the menu. I tried the Chicken Biriyani as well as Shepherd's Pie - both very tasty. After another glass of bubbly and some coffee, I retreated to sit by a view of the apron although there was nothing much to see. It was only a few minutes walk to my boarding gate.

There are several Coral lounges at Bangkok Airport, and despite my voucher indicating where to go, it took me a while to locate the Coral 'Cosmo' Lounge. A smiling face welcomed me, and I entered a long narrow and quiet place. On the left side of the lounge were rows of seating with tables for dining, and on the right, were comfortable sofas for relaxing. One side of the length of the lounge is open to apron views but was marred by too many screens and metal framings outside. At the far end was a view of the boarding gate areas below. There are shower facilities and I was told even some sleep rooms, which I was not able to see for myself. The bar was small, with a few choices of drinks, but the food department looked very inviting. Sprays of small yellow Oncidium Orchids placed between sections added a decorative touch. The hot food (mainly Asian) was in colourful heavy pans, and the seafood curry and rice I had was delicious. I was there for nearly two hours, and no more than five persons were in the lounge. The barman said that the place rarely got busy, which also suited me fine, as I do not enjoy overcrowded lounges. A bonus was having a complimentary 15-minute neck, shoulder and arm massage, which really made me feel good and pampered. Do remember to generously tip the masseur. For those who wished to exercise, a gym room provided the necessary equipment. The flight information screen wasn't working properly, and as the WiFi connected well, I was able to keep track of my flight boarding notices. I enjoyed a tranquil time here, and the staff were pleasant and engaging.

Flying from London to Bangkok via Abu Dhabi involved a rather long layover, and Etihad's Business Class Lounge was a welcome and restful retreat. Arriving well past midnight, I was pleased to see how empty it was. Following a quick shower (the attendant ensuring it was spotlessly clean), I was able to relax and take in the atmosphere. Storing your hand luggage is a bonus, enabling you to move around easily, without having to haul your cabin baggage with you. Choosing where to settle down, meant many options. There were bright spacious seating areas, quiet dimly lit zones, as well as semi-private booths with your own TV to keep you company. The variety of comfortable seating was impressive. There was also a semi-partitioned work area with several computers and desk space. The restaurant-style dining sections are spacious.
