The fairly extensive bar features somewhere in the central part of the lounge and has a wide selection of drinks from premium brand spirits, wines, and champagne to soft drinks. Both barmen were engaging in short bursts of conversation while keeping the drinks flowing. The food choice was extensive. From Middle Eastern to Indian, and Western cuisine as well as finger food, there was no shortage of choice. Several coffee stations were spread around, and helping myself to several cappuccinos, and settling in a booth with TV was a good way to pass some time as well. However, large lounges also feel rather impersonal, unlike small cosy ones where the staff make you feel welcome and interact with you. On my second visit, when on route back to London, arriving late evening, the ambiance at the lounge was quite different and disappointing. It was noisy, overcrowded, with luggage strewn all over, and with little space to sit and relax. What spoiled it even more, was the behavior of many passengers. Several had removed their socks and shoes, stretched out on couches occupying three or more seat spaces and exposing their feet close to other passengers. Fortunately, my stay lasted just over an hour and I was glad to leave.

Flying to Abu Dhabi mid-afternoon, I had the opportunity to visit Etihad's First & Business Lounge at Heathrow Terminal 4. I was welcomed by staff who wished me a pleasant stay. As I paused by the bar, even without requesting, I was immediately offered a glass of Joseph Perrier champagne. As they noticed me taking photos, I was quickly approached by a staff member to hold on a bit longer, until they had laid out all the lunchtime food. The display was very appetizing, even though there wasn't a vast selection of hot items. Opposite was a proper dining room with table service. The staff were chatty and made me feel relaxed and comfortable. The lounge isn't particularly large. There are no vast views of aircraft taking off. There are several styles of furnishings, and areas designated for quieter moments, as well as a children's playroom. The decor is soothing, with some of Etihad's logo colours of dark brown, sepia and yellow ochre. Complimenting the design is also dark wood pannelling, decorated with ornaments and airline memorabilia. As I had plenty of time before my flight, I decided to have a tasty light lunch of Moutabbal salad and another salad. The staff kept enticing me to try more Middle Eastern cuisine, but I gently refused, as I knew lunch would also be served on the flight. Later at the bar, I was treated to a Manhattan cocktail, before going to the boarding gate. On leaving, the manager introduced himself and inquired how I rated my experience and wished me a pleasant flight.

Visiting this lounge did not encourage us to use it again. Although we are Silver members, we had to wait in a queue to enter the lounge, because of the many people paying to use the lounge. The lounge was crowded, with very limited seating inside: the atmosphere was like a student mensa, not offering the peace and quiet we were hoping for. Tea and coffee facilities were limited, with no milk available. Overall impression was dirty, noisy and crowded.

Lounge was extremely crowded and there was nowhere to sit. The situation with this lounge has not changed for many years, I can only therefore assume that Finnair have no interest in fixing the situation.

A large, spacious, quiet place with comfortable couches and clean bathrooms. A feature that caught my eye was a mechanical shoe polisher - I inserted my boots to give them a bright shine! There was ample food and drinks of all kinds - all self service. A row of windows overlooked the security check in area. International magazines were on racks. A perfect place to while your time before your flight is called. Easy to get to just after security - go up in an elevator; take it down to go to your gate through duty free shops.

The lounge is located in Terminal B at Dusseldorf airport. Access is allowed i.e. with Priority Pass. Staff are very friendly and efficient. The ambience is quite sober but friendly. There is plenty of seating available. Food selection seems to locally inspired and is not not huge. Everything I tried was delicious. Drinks selection is not large but there are coffee, tea, soft drinks and wine/beer. I think maximum stay is three hours.

Without any doubt one of the worst lounges visited in recent years. The place reeks of cigarette smoke, the wine is almost undrinkable and the food revolting. It was 21.30 and the food on offer was limited and had clearly been "simmering" all day. Avoid this lounge - sadly the only offering for Qatar Airways Business Class
Dreadful place on every level. 1980s decor, filthy, loud, muzak blaring at a decibel level at which it's hard to work or relax, terrible selection of sad looking sandwiches. Typical Copa.

Mediocre lounges Terminal I & 2 have identical food, essentially appetizers. Dips, raw veggies, tiny sandwiches, cookies, and taco chips. Breakfast includes fruit and oatmeal. Enough to keep you from being hungry, but not a satisfying meal. Decent bar. Coffee drinks tend to be very sweet. Terminal 1 leather chairs look very grimy. Doubt they have ever been cleaned. It is basically, one large room, so can get quite noisy. Very tired, a bit dirty. Lots of food debris on ground, by evening Terminal 2 lounge is new, so much cleaner, brighter. One section has a good view of the concourse, but also consequently noisy. The sectioning of the lounge into several areas, partly with a glass wall, reduces noise in inner areas. Toilet paper gone by 11am and bathroom floors dirty. Seems to be better maintained, with fewer dirty dishes piled up. More appealing bar.

Poor lounge with non existing food or drinks except cheap packaged foods and soft drinks served at the bar, on demand, in a plastic cup. Unrestricted access as the noisy lounge is overtaken by ultimately any credit card holder and their families, including infants and shoppers returning from their shopping spree in Orlando.

Disgusting. Hands down one of the dirtiest lounges I've ever had the misfortune of stepping foot in. The seats? Filthy. The chairs and sofas are absolutely revolting, covered in crumbs. The food selection is actually decent, surprisingly. The staff weee roo busy gossiping to even pretend to care about the state of the place. This dump is ancient, falling apart at the seams. And the music? Some god-awful techno that's supposed to be 'relaxing'? Please. Avoid this place at all costs. It's an absolute disgrace.

Lounge is tired. And apparently due for upgrade in a year or two… But the staff are super friendly and helpful even when they are really busy. Food is okay (the chef’s savoury mince is great but it is only on the menu at certain times of the year) Reasonable selection of drinks and snacks. But the staff are its biggest asset.

The concourse C lounge in Dubai is woeful. Totally inadequate toilet and shower facilities for the size of the lounge. Having to “book” a shower in an airlines home lounge is ridiculous, and 3 toilets only for hundreds of people is unacceptable. Food offerings ok.

It was like entering a timber mill or woodwork factory. Anything that wasn’t wood, was the same shade in colour. It was that and the overpowering smell of wood that hit me the moment I entered. It looked old and tired and with a low ceiling. The staff are pleasant enough but there were very few passengers, and it was obvious why. It was the complete opposite to the onboard experience. There was no a-lar-cart dining experience here. It was a serve yourself buffet and while it looked white good – nothing was hot – the egg omelettes were cold and so was the bacon to go with them. There’s café style seating or lounge seating – neither was comfortable. I was pretty happy to leave.

A great lounge with all the necessities offered. Tons of space and seating with ample power outlets. Shower is plenty and cleaned before use. Food and beverage options abound with many options available (e.g., healthy food including detox juices, vegan options, and an ice cream stall). The terminal is designed that passengers are allowed to board their planes directly from the lounge. Great experience indeed.
Multiple food stations, enough seating available and a lovely champagne bar to wind down. Showers are a little small, but no complaints. Washrooms kept very clean.

An outstanding Emirates lounge, recently reopened after covid closure. First rate variety of hot and cold food and likewise with drink, both alcoholic and non alcoholic. The staff could not do enough for me; first class service who help at every stage. In short a great way to begin the journey from Bangkok. Emirates at its very best!

We visited this lounge on 04/28 morning 5-7:30 AM on stopover between LAX and BKK. Entry was granted as member of UA Club and Hubby as my Plus One. The lounge has really good selection of buffet, both hot and cold food. There's some wine and spirits and a ton of fruit juice and soda to choose from. There are two espresso machines that were always busy. A separate dessert section have local sweets like mochi. The lounge starts to get busy around 6:30 AM when passengers start showing up for flights to other Asian cities. Cleaning service were very active and they clean the tables quickly. The only issue I see here is the size of the restroom that might be too small for a lounge this size. However the toilets here are very nice with functions like bidets and heated seats. Too bad the instructions are only in Chinese so I don't know what all the features are there.

Very nice lounge with excellent amenities. EVA staff have provisions for lounge occupancy. Nice clean managed shower service. Diverse warm food options, self serve scooped ice cream, however very limited liquor options? Adequate seating and good wi-fi and power access from most seats.

Very nice pre flight lounge, warm food, showers and self poured cocktails/sprits/wine and beer. ice cream and fresh fruit as well. Very helpful staff and attentive. Adequate seating and very comfortable with good wi-fi and power outlet access

The lounges of EVA are probably among the worst I have encountered. The lounge had no sandwiches, salads, snacks (peanuts, chips etc) and the set up was a depressing set of steamed foods that appeared to have been sitting there for a long time. There are several lounges but only one is actually available to business class passengers. It is a terrible pity because the airline experience is positive but EVA relies far too much on its reputation and not on the upkeep of it.

I am only giving this lounge a less than average review because when we arrived very early in the morning we quickly realized that so do the majority of Iceland air flights from the United states that connect onwards to Europe very early in the morning. The lounge was extremely crowded, you could not find a seat, the buffet offering breakfast selections was less than average. I just got a cappuccino to keeep awake and left it at that. The ground airport lounge staff really worked their hardest to keep the food replenished and the tables cleared but it was obvious that the lounge was simply too crowded. I give the staff in the lounge a 5 star rating for having to copy with this many people and with a smile so early in the day.

A very spacious lounge, and it even has some beds, though very few truly lounging seats. Most are at tables for working or eating. The food selections is not huge and mostly cold, except for a delicious soup. Wide range of beverage, both soft and alcoholic, and coffee machines dotted all over the place. A useful haven, if not an especially luxurious one, and particularly handy because Keflavik airport can sometimes resemble a bus station.
The lounge was quite full, but there was plenty of food and tables were cleaned regularly. I could charge my laptop and mobile phone in a individual table. A good experience.

This lounge is offering a wide choice of drinks and food. Lounge is very spacious but rather busy and crowded. The tables were constantly cleaned up and dishes and glasses taken away. There are both cold and hot dishes, self service is re introduced after the pandemic. Different wines are offered. Restrooms were clean. Reception was done with a smile.
Very nice and spacious. At the bar a great choice of wines, jerez etc. which is a very good idea. Nice seats and not overcrowded. Food (cold only) could be improved but good overall impression.

I've been to about a dozen lounges now in India and this is easily one of the best. I've been here twice and on both occasions there was plentiful seating. Chefs can cook you fresh food (dosa as it was breakfast time when I visited) and there is also some western as well as local food, both hot and cold. Good range of alcoholic (pay extra) and non alcoholic drinks. All in all it ticks all the boxes and I would definitely recommend!

Very crowded, with no simple breakfast offerings, (at 8 am), as Curry Rice or Pasta are not really my thing at that time of day. No knives to butter the croissant, but butter knives produced after asking. This was the Business class lounge on the 4/F. Found the one on 5/F to be better organised, and less busy.

I was looking forward to this lounge after reading about it on JAL's website. What a disappointment. The lounge itself was nothing special and not up to first class standard. Food can only be ordered by app that needs to be downloaded. That caused huge problems but a very helpful and patient English speaking staff member assisted. After 20 minutes she couldn't even get the app to work went away to get a printed menu which allegedly doesn't exist. 10 minutes later I got the app to work. The food is disappointing and does not live up to the hype on the website. Plus it's hard to identify what you are actually getting from the tiny thumbnail pics on the app. I had intended to eat my evening meal here before boarding the overnight flight to Sydney so I could sleep on the aircraft but this didn't happen. I hardly ate anything other than a few pieces of sushi, but definitely not enough to get me through the log haul flight back home. Just before boarding I noticed passengers eating plates of fresh chicken salad and udon that I hadn't found on the menu. It was too late to order anything else by then. As boarding at Haneda was by bus and a total shambles (flight nearly 1 hour late departing due to a shortage of buses) it's a huge failing that the lounge doesn't notify their premium passengers so they can have a realistic time for going down to the gate. This was consistent with all my travel on JAL where information was minimal to non existent.

I checked in to the IGA Lounge by presenting my credit card(Lounge Key) and boarding pass, then proceeded to enter by scanning my boarding pass at the rotary gate. It felt like entering an airport within an airport. The lounge's size is comparable to that of a small city's airport, and it also has it's own duty free shop. Gazing ahead upon entering we were welcomed by the site of a pool table, a bar, and a masseur at work. Upon walking a few meters and turning right we found an expansive buffet with live cooking stations preparing pidde(Turkish pizza), pasta, and kebabs, along with a buffet offering a fairly wide selection of Turkish food and self service coffee machines. The food was fresh and tasted surprisingly good for an airport lounge. The lounge had considerable seating capacity offering various types of seating - sofas with coffee tables, recliner chairs, and workstations. The seating is comfortable, we did find some seats that were not clean but then managed to find clean ones. Most of the seating was being used, which resulted in an environment that was busy but also fairly quiet. The staff are efficient - some are friendly and others indifferent. None were rude or unpleasant. The shower was clean, spacious, and comfortable. The water was warm with decent pressure, and the quality of the shampoo and shower gel provided was good. They provide a sealed disposable towel, so you don't have to worry about whether it was washed. The WiFi was problematic. The connection kept dropping, and upon speaking with some other guests I found a number of us were encountering this issue. The IGA Lounge exceeded our expectations and made our eight hour layover a breeze without us needing to spend any money at the airport.

Lounge is very far away from duty free and relatively far away from gates as well. However, lounge is very nice and specious; it has some nice food stations with great taste as well as beverages and nice Italian coffee. Toilets are clean and staff are really nice and friendly

ITA airways lounge where Skyteam Elite Plus members have access, situated in the Satellite of T3. Very comfortable relaxing seats. Catering - cheese, ham, vegetables in acceptable choices but not excessive. Drinks included - coffee, water, beer. Nice and clean lounge.

Really enjoyed the KLM Crown Lounge in the non-Schengen terminal. While entering, seeing all the KLM Delfts Blue houses is a nice welcome. The lounge facilities are great, with showers, several bars and probably the biggest lounge I’ve been in since this one has two floors has a lot of space to sit everywhere (also in quiet to work). There was not much food to choose from, but the quality was good. The whole design throughout the lounge is fantastic and the crew was friendly and attentive. It was not always as clean as it should be and some chairs and tables needed some maintenance but overall the experience was very positive.

The lounge is accessed either by escalator or elevator. Glass walls by the escalators display the massive collection of Delft pottery houses which are offered to PX on long-haul flights. The lounge, whenever we have visited has been very crowded, and although huge, seating is hard to find. There are two refreshment areas, one at either end which offer different food items, so it is worth looking at both. Upstairs there is a restaurant-type situation at lunch and dinner times. I cannot comment as we have never used it.

I had free access on this trip as a guest of a frequent flyer, based on his Delta Status. I really like the KLM lounges, the staff are very helpful and pleasant. The options and layout are really nice and although the lounge seemed quite busy, we found space to sit and nap. They have showers,  a really good selection of drinks and I personally like the coffee, however the food is not good. I'd give it a 3 out of 10. I don't understand this as access is usually 50 euro with your boarding pass, and if you need to eat your are not getting value for your money. The food on the plane was better. KLM, you need to step that up. You're serving food that's worse than anything you can buy in a cheap diner.

The KLM Schengen Lounge (25) is nothing to speak of. Very busy at peak times; children running around, babies crying, numerous people talking -loudly- into their mobile phones. Limited seating. Plastic chairs at the tables are very uncomfortable. Only a few more comfortable seats, but they’re always taken by people, sitting in one seat and their feet or luggage in the other. Only one of the two counters was open for food. Not enough plates; took ages before they were restocked. Quality of the food so so: Very bland. Very limited choice. Tables were not cleaned after people had left. 2 out of the 3 coffeemakers on the non-food side were out of order. The restrooms were appalling: 3 ladies restrooms out of order. No more paper towels. Paper all over the floor. Restrooms that were not out of order were dirty! Same for the men’s restrooms: All out of order on one side of the lounge. On the other side, my husband noticed that only 3 men’s restrooms were available. Also very dirty. This lounge is an absolute disgrace for Schiphol and KLM.

This is the KLM Skyteam standard lounge at Schiphol Airport with a modern interior. Lounge is getting very busy at business times but there is usually plenty of room. The food and drink selection is ok although nothing special.

Nothing positive to say. It's crowded, it's loud filled with people talking loudly on mobile phones and babies screaming, there are no quiet zones, the lights are very bright with no dark spaces to try to rest, the food is institutional slop that looks unappetizing and tastes as such, even the showers are lame - they give you one thin towel, no hand towels, no bath mat. It's a third rate lounge from a third rate alliance and unfortunately I'm stuck here for six painful hours.

Went in with high expectations based on several public reviews. I thought they were all wildly off base. This was a very disappointing experience in many ways. I'll start with two positives: the lounge is aesthetically appealing and the staff is very nice. Beyond that it's third rate. First of all, it is way, way too crowded. It's impossible to find a place to sit and if you are fortunate enough to do so then you'll wait in a long queue for poor quality food that's basically poor institutional grade. There were over 30 people waiting in the feed line when I visited. This isn't a quality experience in any way. A lounge is supposed to be a haven and respite away from the madness if the airport. I also checked out the sleep cabins as an alternative and they are pathetic and overpriced. The cabin I was offered had an upper bunk bed that felt like I was in a hostel or pod hotel and was extremely spartan. The Crown 52 lounge is anything but that. I wouldn't buy a business class ticket to access this as a perk nor would I pay to hangout here. It's a huge disappointment and I won't return. KLM should be ashamed of this product.

It is big and well equipped but the food and snacks are rather disappointing I find. Warm food is tasteless and too obviously made in large quantities. Thankfully at a certain point they brought in lasagne that went quickly and was edible. Other skyteam lounges all over the world have so much better food. Drinks are fine, so too are some of the cold options. It can get crowded.

This is one of the best business lounges I have been to. Food is good, drinks especially the Heineken bar is great. Its huge with lots of room, and several themed sections - one for work, for entertainment and relaxing. Wifi was awesome and staff friendly and efficient. I was heavily jet lagged after a nightmare departure from Canada and was able to crash out for 2-3 hours in a relaxation , quiet area. Overall, I had an 8 hour layover which normally would have been a nightmare. But I spent the whole time in the Crown Lounge and the time passed really quickly. Thank you! One piece of constructive feedback. I couldn't find any newspapers or magazine which would have been a bonus.

After three years it was my first visit at the Crown Lounge in Amsterdam.  It starts with the nice staff at the entrance. After I asked for the shower they showed me the way. Unfortunately the system did not work. Therefore I had to go back to ask the staff to help. One minute and I had my key card for the shower. The shower room is a bit small but big enough to have a nice shower. The food area is huge and at lunch time there are plenty of choices. Its true that around noon the lounge is very crowded.  My most amazing spot in the lounge was the outdoor terrace, to sit and get some fresh air. Especially after an 12 hours flight and another 11 hours flight coming up. This lounge is impressive and the staff is great.

Not crowded, enough space. Seats good for sitting to dine and relax. Variety of warm food a bit poor. Coffee was good. Would have appreciated if they had offered gluten free meals, too. As it was offered for a reduced price, the price-value-relation was okay. We would do it again instead of lingering around in those bleak halls with expensive fast food stands and restaurants.

China Airlines VIP Lounge at Terminal 1 was such a hidden gem! Not only it was very large but also extremely elegant and luxurious. Once passing through the check-in counter, we were amazed by a long and beautiful corridor. There were many comfortable seats in the lounge. Shower and toilette were clean and nice. F&B selection was generous, tasty. We really liked the hot station. WiFi was fast too.
The Lounge is a Long stair down. We went for breakfast, it was Basic, low quality and tasteless. Really disappointing for this airline. They close at 10 PM

Divided into several lounges, according to whether you're flying Latam or another codeshare carrier, these lounges are very good. The Latam customer lounge (Premium) is bigger and better but all have plenty of seating, good food choices which are kept refreshed regularly, good drink choices and fast free wi-fi. They have beds (reserve on arrival) and showers. The only negative is that there is no view or windows these days.

The Pearl Lounge was huge and well maintained. The food options were good but I wish they had lunch options as well - they used to offer lunch options in the morning as well back in the old Airport Lounge. The staff were excellent and the lady who was serving at the middle section pictures was super friendly, attentive and professional. The toilets were clean and well attended but I did not appreciate the dim lighting.
Brand new lounge, a great experience. Latest vibe, high quality food and drinks. Finally it seems that KE invests in their customers comfort now they can do the same for their old fleet
Lounge offers a variety of foods and drinks, but rather small and often packed. But it is adapted to the airport and my guess most of the time it is not so crowded. The lounge is very clean

The lounge was not only served KAL passengers, but also some other Syteam members'. It was located near Gate 28 in the main concourse, so if you are departing from the satellite, please board the shuttle train after using the lounge. It was quite a big one with great view, and had a lot of natural light. Food and beverage was good. We liked the Korean ramen, chicken and the beer. Shower needed to be reserved and wait about 30 minutes. In overall, it was a nice place to relax before continuing the journey.

The Royal Lounge operated by Hokkaido Airports was located right above my flight's boarding gate and duty free shopping. It was such a hidden gem, not only because of its super cleanliness but also the beautiful interiors. There were massage chairs, private meeting room. Food was amazingly cooked and prepared. Really loved the hot ramen here. Absolutely one of the best airline lounge in Japan!
The lounge at International terminal was located almost at the end of the terminal was clean but quite small with limited selection of food and beverages. Staff was friendly and nice.
The lounge at International terminal was located almost at the end of the terminal was clean but quite small with limited selection of food and beverages. Staff was friendly and nice.
The lounge is nice, spacious, and de facto world class. Separate areas, good, varied food options, changing over the day and night. Well assorted bar, sleepers, smoking room, proactive staff.

The food at the lounge was inedible and sparse, of the 7-8 food items they had none was edible. I had to go out and eat at one of the restaurants at the terminal.  The sleeping zones were loud and no pillows or blankets were provided. The service and food at the normal credit card lounges is a million times better than this so called business class lounge

Although I am furious with Kenya Airways right now I will acknowledge that they are trying to improve their lounge service. There is a cook making eggs and omelettes as requested and their cappuccino is excellent. Food rather boring and minimal but a relatively good range of drinks. Wifi is good.

3rd party lounge used by Kenya Airways. Lounge is still good, food is improving, more hot dishes, and more hot savory snacks. Drinks options sparse, but there are good stocks. Lacks windows terribly. No music.

Very disappointing. Tiny for a Business Lounge with too many tables and chairs crammed in. Little choice in the cold buffet with each plate clingfilmed so you first had to unseal the clingfilm, take what you wanted and then reseal the clingfilm. Surely rigid covers which could be lifted off and then replaced would make things much easier? The also limited choice of hot food looked like it had been sat there for hours. Kenya Airways now use this lounge while most others use the vastly better Dzimbahwe Executive Lounge. I shall avoid flying Kenya Airways on a Harare route in future so I don't have to visit this lounge again.

While the Sasco-lounge is being one of the most expensive agent-lounges worldwide, it's also one of the worst lounges I ever have been to: usually messy and overcrowded with no left seating abilities, stained tables, trash not being removed quickly. Not even standard beer-brands are offered but just the cheapest Vietnamese beer in the market. The same is true for the wine-selection. In addition, in terms of spirits, all whats available is the cheapest Hanoi-vodka, Ballantines, Gibson's Gin and Captain Morgan Rum. The selection of soft-drinks is poor, as well, not even offering Tonic Water for a Gin&Tonic. While food-selection looks impressive, it lacks taste and texture. The 'signature-dish', the local Vietnamese soup 'Pho' does not reflect at all the rich taste and flavor of the original. There are no newspapers, the staff is not helpful and even the screen where to comment how you liked your stay does not work. At peak times (unfortunately I must use the lounge quite often) waiting lines at the entrance are long because of lack of staff. When commenting about the service (yes, there is a comment form) no feedback is given and nothing is changed. Sasco got a monopol (no other lounges allowed at the airport) and uses it to maximize profit to the disadvantage of its customers. The only positive is that the bathrooms are usually clean - which is true for the whole airport however.

There are few lounges at Warsaw Chopin Airport. Some of them are managed by airport, they are really poor. BTwo of them - Polonez (Schengen area) and Mazurek ( non- Schengen area) - are managed by LOT Polish Airlines and they are much more interesting. Polonez Lounge consists of two parts - bigger one for Star Alliance Frequent Travellers and smaller, more cosy for Gold, HON Circle members and business class customers. Food and drinks are almost the same - usually two or three options of hot meals; sandwiches, salads, decent selection of sweets and alcohol beverages. Both lounges are often crowded, especially in the morning and late afternoon.

I had a longish layover in FRA with a late flight out and was planning to eat here so I could sleep on the flight. The food selection is absolutely abysmal for a airline lounge. Meatballs, rice and some disgusting looking white dumplings. That was it for hot food. Really, you need to leave the lounge to eat decently. The lounge itself is large, clean, soulless. The drinks are abundant. But you'll have to drink on an empty stomach.

The LH Lounge at Frankfurt is absolutely one of the most unimpressive facilities.  The only  benefit of the LH Frankfurt business lounge is supposedly the quiet seating area, but the loud  staff interactions that continually came from the kitchen area negated this benefit. In addition, the food offerings are pathetic, along with the warm beer.

The Lufthansa lounge in Washington Dulles is very disappointing, with a poor choice of rather low quality foods. We were on a late flight (10:20 pm) and our goal was to have dinner in the lounge in order to go to sleep immediately after takeoff. The food offering was what you can expect from a school cafeteria. Vegetarian options were particularly pathetic, with essentially no protein available. The coffee machine was out of milk when we tried it and we had to alert the staff for them to refill (the coffee machines are filled with real milk and the replenishing process is rather time consuming). The staff was sparse: only one person in sight when we arrrived (not counting the receptionist). A second attendant showed up a little later. Only positive point, the seats are confortable and modern looking but the lounge is rather small. Star Alliance passengers have the option of using the Turkish lounge instead, which is a much better choice in our opinion foodwise (provided the lounge is not overcrowded).

Since long time one of the worst Lufthansa has on offer for their premium customers “Senator. Besides the uninspiring food (some overcooked mini sausages and cold salads), non-functioning beer tap (in Germany!), warm white wine (cooling system not working) and the friendliness of those working there to say at least unacceptable: attitude of not knowing why being there and for what purpose, arrogant, unfriendly etc. Exception to be made for the nice lady who cleared the tables. I know Lufthansa outsourced all services related matters within the lounge, but this visit was really no good to Lufthansa’s reputation. Unfortunately in Munich it is quite often a hit or miss.

First time transit in the new airport of Berlin and I was positively impressed. Same for Lufthansa’s Senator Lounge there. Granted entrance because of my status. Very nice interior, bright and reasonable offering of food and drinks. Had to spent 2 hours there, had enough space to get my work done and could have lunch before catching my low cost and no frills flight with Lufthansa Group‘s airline Eurowings.

By far, this was the best airport lounge we visited on our four stop trip to Europe (BKK/VIE/ATH/VIE/BKK). The lounge is located a short walk past security control. It is well marked and easy to find. The lounge is divided into two sections - dining area and quiet reading/relaxing area. There are also a few enclosed booths for phone calls, a business area with printer and a few reclining sleep chairs. Restrooms are outside the lounge in the gate departure area. The food and beverage selections were extensive (great wine, champagne, and hard liquor choices) all very high end with a mixture of Western and Greek dishes. Seating was comfortable. Highly recommend !!

Entry permitted because of my Star Alliance status. This contract lounge generically open to business and first class passengers and Priority Pass. If you love paper cups for your coffee, plastic for your drinks, worn out seats, modest (packed) food options, no papers nor magazines, you are absolutely in the right place.

The lounge is very ugly, the food option not many, the drinks are ok, but no Champagne available. It’s not that easy to become senator, after you become a senator you get a bad lounge, not difference than this one from business class.
Good lounge with a decent selection of food and beverage - warm and cold meal, non-alcoholic and alcoholic drinks Other than general LH service, the lounge is good.

This is the recently refurbished/opened new Lufthansa Senator Lounge at BER airport. The facility is located opposite gate B20 and accessible by lift or stairs. The lounge is clean and follows the plain and sober design of the other LH lounges. There is plenty of seating (I used the lounge several times and always found a free seat). There is a small salad buffet and some biscuits and fruit. The drink selection is also not very extensive but there is coffee, tea, wine, beer and soft drinks.

I am quite critical regarding Lufthansa’s tacky approach when offering lounges to their own premium passengers but in Milan Malpensa they have done a wonderful job! The lounge is pleasant, very relaxing with all kind of seating opportunities: work, relax and eat, just a joy. Food offering is outstanding compared to what normally one gets in their lounges. Drinks could be a little more exciting (or better to say less mainstream), but all in all I am impressed and I wonder how on earth Lufthansa isn’t able to offer the same standards in the main hubs.

First time visit in this lounge so didn't know what to expect. The lounge is modern, bright and airy. It has modern communal seating with tables and chairs along with secluded alcoves for a little more privacy, free wifi is available. The lounge also has a viewing terrace overlooking the airport and the Julian Alps. There was a number of Bottled local drinks, including beers, soft drinks and water, long with a wide selection of very good quality wines and a few spirits. There was a Draught beer pump too which was very nice indeed, a selection of local food and sandwiches were in cool cabinets and various snacks, fruit, bread rolls, Cakes, cooked meats and cheeses. There were various savoury snack dotted about amongs the seating.

The Bellini Lounge at Catania Airport is located in the main terminal. One has to go up a flyer of stairs (or lift) at the far end of the (small) terminal to reach the lounge. The lounge us tiny and can officially accommodate 35 people but I‘d say 20-25 people is more realistic. There is a fridge with a few soft drinks and some Prosecco and a bottle of red wine is also available. A small selection of surprisingly tasty snacks is also available. So, the lounge is modest to say the least. The toilet is located outside The lounge and is clean. Most bothersome to me were the masses of fruit flies coming out of the waste bins. Those bins are rather prominent and for some reason, were positioned just under the screens. Don’t make the mistake of paying for a guest as one will get a much better deal at one of the restaurants in the airport.

This is the Schengen Senator lounge in Munich opposite Gate G28. Like the non-Schengen version on the floor above, which I visited a couple of days ago and didn’t like, this lounge is boring and just functional. The food was not very tasty and the selection was very small.

This is a standard Lufthansa Senator’s lounge located opposite Gate H24 at MUC (non-Schengen) The layout is rather modern and functional. It feels a bit sterile but clean and welcoming. There is a selection of German food complimented by salads and sweets. The lounge offers a full bar which is a nice touch. Staff are efficient but not very friendly. The toilets are located outside and seem to serve both, the Business and Senator’s lounges.

A miserable overcrowded experience. Food uninspiring, horrible wines, no seating during this Friday afternoon, tables not cleaned or dirty plates being taken away. Definitely the worse experience ever in a Lufthansa Lounge! Better do oneself the favour to sit elsewhere in the terminal and enjoy in one of the lovely restaurant facilities LHR has on offer: pay a little (or much) and enjoy good food and nice wines! Alternatively, if one has Gold Status and some time, go rather to any other Star Alliance lounge in the Terminal. Consider this lounge as your last option!

Non-Schengen departure, in concourse B. Visited both Lufthansa’s Premium Senator and regular Business Class Lounge. Interestingly Lufthansa pampers Star Alliance Gold Card Members more than their paying business class passengers. At least, that is what Lufthansa still says. While this definitely was true before Covid, now it is not the case. Though furniture and setting are superior in the Senator Lounge, there is basically no real difference between the two lounges: same drinks, same dull and definitely not premium food in both lounges.

On April 17, 2023, we arrived at the Lufthansa Business Lounge in Athens around 3:45pm. The lounge was quite empty but we didn’t think much of it. I went up to get a glass of wine for myself, and some juice and water for my kids. Each time I took a glass, the same lady was on the other side of the kitchen replacing the glasses with clean ones and slamming them down aggressively. I thought it was strange but excused her behaviour as a cultural difference. Afterwards, I poured two small glasses of wine, to determine which varietal I would like to enjoy with my salad. Before I was done, one of the kitchen staff came over and gasped and looked at me. She had a container of ice in her hands so I moved the two glasses out of the way so she could put the ice down. She took the ice bucket and slammed it down on the counter which startled me and my son. She then proceeded to stare at me and then at the empty wine glass. I moved the glass out of the way and asked if there was somewhere else she would like me to put the glass as it was clear that she was angry with me. From there, the lady that was restocking the water glasses yelled that I should leave the glasses on a table by the kitchen. I explained that I wasn’t done and that it would be simple to ask if I could bring the glass to that table rather than coming over and yelling at me and having her colleague slam a bucket of ice on the counter next to me and my young son. I thought I was doing them a favour by bringing the glass back to where they were working and this is what I would do in Canada, and it would be viewed as a gesture of kindness. The kitchen staff continued to slam things down on the counter and dominate the area where people were trying to get drinks and food, making it very awkward for everyone. They had no respect for the travelling passengers and cared more about their unwritten rules of keeping the counter clean and the glasses stocked, than trying to maintain a happy environment with good customer service. When I went back to my table, some passengers sitting next to us explained that they observed the staff being confrontational and rude with other guests. This didn’t surprise me but I said I would go and speak to the ladies at the front desk to determine how I could provide some additional feedback about this incident and I would also go and see if we had access to the lounge next door. Before leaving the Lufthansa lounge I stopped at the front desk and spoke to the two ladies and requested an email address so I could file a complaint. They refused to provide me with this information and told me that as a lounge customer I should know better, and that I should leave empty glass on the table by the kitchen rather than bring it up to the counter. At that stage, it was clear that the kitchen staff spoke to the ladies at reception and rather than work to diffuse the situation they made it worse. I explained to them that rules are different in every country and if we are required to leave glassware on a table by a kitchen, that can’t be viewed from the lounge area, then they should have signage within the lounge that explains that to international passengers. If you are a Star Alliance member, do yourself a favour and do not use the Lufthansa business lounge until they change the attitude of the staff. Go next door to the Aegean Lounge where you will be greeted with a smile and kindness.

Overcrowded and no possibility to sit anywhere except on a high barstool. Very nice Lufthansa representatives at the welcome desk, very helpful checking me in for the return flight (Lufthansa’s App was down, again). Totally different story with the others working in the lounge, obviously not Lufthansa employees but rather working for some service provider. No eye contact, no smile or nice word. I understand it is tough sometimes, but still one can make an effort. Food so-so, drinks okay this time.

The lounge is a very quiet place - excellent reception desk people and service was outstanding. It was breakfast time so I had everything I needed. There is plenty of food, decent quality however cannot match the lounges by the mid Eastern companies. Unfortunately the quality of the Champagnes was sub par in comparison with all the premium whiskies and hard liquors. Extremely clean restrooms as well and a very personal goodbye when leaving the lounge.

Due to Star Alliance Gold Status got granted access to the Sala Leonardo lounge. A fairly ok generic frequent flyer lounge, with a reasonable choice of drinks and food. Bit of too much plastic wrapped food, plastic forks and glasses, which of course is sending a wrong message, besides transmitting cheapness (which definitely doesn’t reflect Milan).

Seems Lufthansa‘s management added a new feature to the many measures, which already miserably downgraded this airline. Not to replace empty bottles. Furthermore, one cannot understand why with all excellent white wines Germany has, Lufthansa insists on disgusting Italian and French sparkling wines. Food, for a premium lounge was average, though acceptable.

We were on a 6am Austrian Airlines flight, so had a short stay in the Senator lounge - access gained by a business class ticket. The lounge opened at 5am sharp - there was quite a queue of people waiting. The Senator lounge is slightly better than the main business class lounge, but there isn't much in it. It was significantly quieter though. Good breakfast selection. Full range of drinks including sparkling wine. Very good coffee machine. Best of all, a magazine selection is back! After 2 and a half years of no mags. Overall, I was pretty impressed.

Because of Gold-Status with Star Alliance, have access to this lounge also when flying in Economy. Senator Lounges are “on level above” regular Business Class lounges with Lufthansa. Food is uninspiring as it has been over the many years (except one adores meatballs or Frankfurters). Wine selection is quite satisfactory, though the champagne once offered in the lounge disappeared and now all kind of more or less poor quality Italian alternatives are being offered (Italy has great sparkling wines, but they are not to be found in any Lufthansa lounge, unfortunately Lufthansa seems also not to have a clue when choosing own German sparkling wines, but that’s another story). This lounge has a nice feature, being the only lounge (except the First Class Terminal) with a bar service. Though staff in the lounge is kind and helpful, this morning/early afternoon at the bar the level of service was dreadful: clearly the lady had a problem coping with people.

Undoubtedly Lufthansa went from good to mediocre and nearly all recent reports confirm this. But this experience was surprising. Having missed a connection through Munich and being it impossible to get me on the last flight to final destination, being LH-Gold I went straight to the lounge to get re-booked. Within minutes this was done, boarding card for the first next day’s flight was given, plus vouchers for an airport hotel (they booked directly, I had not to bother) and transfers by taxi. Within 30 mins I was in the hotel: I was surprised. Visit to the lounge leaving next day was good, with reasonable breakfast and good selection of drinks (appreciated very much the freshly squeezed orange juice). Was nice to see newspapers and magazines back, which one is free to take with.

Terribly underwhelming, from seating to food and beverage. Poor selection of food and drinks, not to speak of the practically no seating for the many visitors. However, better than what happens in the terminal, so even if one doesn’t find seating, it’s recommended to stay inside, as outside it is worse!

I didn't have much time to visit this lounge, but I thought I might as well visit the lounge for a drink and a bit to eat. The selection of food was disappointing compared to other business class lounges I've used. The beverages were fine and the staff were friendly and helpful. Not great, but OK.

The lounge is the only of the two present at the airport that actually works. The lounge has unpleasant smell, unfriendly hostess at the reception, and a very basic selection of food. Very few vegetarian options. Out of baked good, there were only doughnuts and they were not fresh. The tables were not cleaned and in 4 hours there has not been a cleaning person cleaning anything in the lounge.

There are no signs to take you from the airport to the lounge. I crossed and recrossed a busy road and tried to enter a car park before finding a waiting taxi driver and asking the way. Inside the lounge, the few staff are quite busy: Cleaning up, checking invoices or looking at computer screens. Just don't expect anyone to hurry over to serve you. (And a large chunk of the lounge is reserved for smokers.) I loved the private security desk, and the limo to the plane is a great idea in theory, though our stuffy shared minibus was less alluring. I'm just surprised at the lack of attention to detail. Don't expect the kind of service you get from the better Asian and Middle Eastern airlines.

At Terminal 2, there are several lounges and I visited two, on the outbound and return journey. There were no smiling welcomes, and I was  gestured towards the entrance. Layout wise they are similar, both in Lufthansa colours and furniture styles. Plenty of space for those who wished to work, standard tables and chairs for dining, and comfortable sofas to relax in. There are shower facilities, so useful for long haul travellers with connections to be able to freshen up. Although fairly crowded on both visits, the places were spotlessly clean and tidy. There was a continuous movement of staff clearing up tables and food leftovers. The bar areas were well stocked with both alcoholic (including some premium liqueurs) and nonalcoholic drinks. Unfortunately, in both lounges, the selection of hot and cold food was disappointing. The choice was limited to just a couple of items of warm food, like sausages, meatloaves and pasta, and paulry-looking salads. However, there was a selection of sweets in jars, like smarties and jelly beans which I noticed several others could not resist. One other disappointing feature is that there are no views of the apron or runways, other than car parks and buildings. On my return journey, I had a three-hour layover, and was able to use a locker to store my cabin luggage, and wander about at ease. However, with nothing interesting to look at, other than browsing the newspapers, phone, and sampling the unappetizing food, I decided to leave the place and explore the airport shops instead.

A very good lounge, which it's main feature is the wide selection of drinks, both alcoholic and non-alcoholic. However, it isn't the same for food options, as they were slightly limited. For a business class lounge, the amenities were very numerous and the quality of them was amazing. I cannot judge the wi-fi because I used mobile data.

This lounge was very disappointing for the simple reason that there were no bathrooms within the lounge. One has to use the bathrooms in the terminal. Why pay for membership to use a lounge when one of the basic amenities (bathrooms) are not available. Notwithstanding the above, the facilities were clean and the lounge had the usual hot and cold food choices plus beverages (soft drinks, water etc.) available with Turkish breakfast items available (olives, cucumbers, tomatoes and various cheeses). If I had known that this lounge had no internal bathrooms, I wouldn't have wasted $$ to enter the lounge.

This is one of the best non airline lounges. The lounge is very spacious. The lobby is very welcoming. The long hallways stretch the length of the lounge reflect the Islamic and Omani architecture. There is plenty of seating. There is a main food station plus 2 others at either end. Given our early morning departure, the buffets had breakfast items (both western and Arabic), cut and whole fresh fruit, salad bar, pastries and assorted breads. The main food station has a live cooking area where one can order eggs/omelets any style. I did not use WiFi so I can comment on connectivity. Restrooms were very clean and seating was very comfortable.

This is a small lounge. The food quality is good. The portions are tapas sized which can be ordered from the menu by scanning QR code on the tables. The lounge had a variety of alcoholic and non-alcoholic beverages available. Service staff was very polite and friendly. WiFi was very easy to connect too and very fast with plenty of outlets to charge phones. The only drawback to this lounge is that the bathrooms were out of order on this visit meaning guests had to use the facilities in the terminal.

This lounge is small and very crowded for an early morning flight. There was a dearth of sitting options. From what I observed, the food/beverage service was very limited. Worst of all, there is only one bathroom in the Lounge. I chose to leave the Club and use the facilities in the airport and waited for my flight at the gate. We were able to use this lounge because of our business class tickets. It seems this is the only lounge available in Terminal 3 so there is no choice but to use it.

The Club at CLT is a welcome addition to this airport for those who are not AA's Admiral Club members. I was pleasantly surprised with this small Priority Pass lounge. The staff is very friendly. Unlike most clubs with a buffet selection, this Club offers an automated albeit limited menu. Scan the QR code and order. Unfortunately, due to the lateness of the day, the Club ran out of the entrée I ordered. Nonetheless, this lounge was well worth the long walk from Concourse B. Bathrooms were clean and the WiFi had a strong signal.

This Swissport lounge is pathetic. The only nice thing about this lounge was the gentleman receptionist and the hot chocolate. The seating is basically nothing more than a barebones seating area. Snacks, soft drinks and a few alcohol offering are the extent of its food/beverage service. We were able to use this lounge because of our business class tickets. However, I certainly wouldn't pay to use this facility. It would be throwing money away. WiFi worked but I felt it was spotty.

Spent 8 hours in transit in this lounge. Lounge quite comfortably appointed however it could really use some more comfortable high back chairs. The shower suites were exceptionally nice (Emirates take note). Great tarmac views. Now the food. Small buffet offered and an à la carte menu, which at lunchtime was solely Asian inspired food. Would be good to have a European option available.

The Plaza Premium Lounge at Gate 1 was amazing to us (not operated by Vietnam Airlines, though its Business Class and Elite passengers were invited). It was lunch time and the lounge was not crowded, easy for us to find an empty table actually. Staff was friendly, quick, and helpful. Shower and massage were available but we did not use. The food, especially the beef noodle and the dessert bar were really worth to explore as the dishes were tasty!

Visited this lounge as I was a Skyteam Elite Plus. It was operated by Plaza Premium Lounge, not Vietnam Airlines. The lounge was shiny and bright, beautiful and elegant. Staff was friendly and helpful. Food selection was quite limited. No toilette or shower inside the lounge, which was quite shame!

The Plaza Premium lounge in Terminal 3 is a welcome oasis from the crowds in the concourses and gate areas. Simple decoration, very clean, nice ambience and very comfortable. The staff is very friendly. The food & drink selection consists of the usual sandwiches, snacks, juices, coffee and soft drinks and most importantly a hot buffet with 4 entrée selections including one vegetarian entrée. The chicken kabob skewers were excellent. more than adequate (cereals, sandwiches, juices, coffee and soft drinks). The lounge was busy but not overcrowded. The bathrooms were very clean and maintained frequently at regular intervals. Wi-Fi was very strong and fast.

Used this Plaza Premium lounge at T4 on a Sunday evening, and it is not fit for purpose. More customers than seats, the lounge was filthy, the toilets even worse. As a Business Class customer on China Southern I expected better than this, and it has to be one of the worst lounges I have ever visited. An absolute disgrace, Plaza Premium should be ashamed.

The lounge unfortunately must substitute the closed Star Alliance lounge on a SWISS flight. Obviously when paying everybody can enter this lounge, which is far too small. The place is looking very dated and overused, very poor choice of food, "hot" food lukewarm to cold. Soda drinks out of dispensers not chilled enough and lack of ice. Also guests have to pay for alcoholic beverages. Restrooms not very clean, unfriendly staff. I left this overcrowded place and went to eat something decent with a decent glass of wine outside.

Plaza Premium US Departures lounge. What's not to like about this brightly lit lounge with clean bathrooms and hot breakfast/hot lunch. The hot breakfast offered scrambled eggs, a selection of breads and other dairy products such as yogurt and fresh fruit. The hot lunch offered salads along with 2 other entrees (Asian style chicken and a pork entrée). The lounge was quite busy late mid-morning and just before lunch time. The WiFi was easy to connect too and fast. There is a bar in the middle that divides the two seating areas. Staff was very friendly and welcoming. I would not hesitate to use this lounge again the next time I fly through YVR.

A generic lounge used by numerous airlines and is also pay for use, so probably at peak hours it might get crowded. However this brand new lounge at Soekarno-Hatta Terminal 3 International Departures is definitely a huge improvement compared to the previous far smaller facility. Spacious, lots of seating, nice coffee bar, excellent bar service (though there isn’t a very wide range of alcoholic drinks) and decent food options. There is even a Spa for a quick massage before your flight (did not use it, but prices seemed to me reasonable). Spend some relaxing time and really enjoyed it.

This is my second visit within 5 months but the Lunch menu was same as before. I think they have a fix menu for everyday lunch. Although the food taste is good as authentic Indian food that is the positive thing there. Next month may be I visit this place again. I hope I will not find this Menu again.

New Plaza Premium lounge finally open at Clark Airport. This is a proper lounge. On the time of visit there were three main course meals available, a reasonable selection of wines, no spirits, soft drinks, and a damn good coffee machine. There is also a smoking area. What was outstanding about this lounge was the quality of the staff. Absolute sheer perfect service. Very friendly. Very professional. Very well presented and smart.

Use quite often this lounge as all Star Alliance Airlines do use it for their business class passengers and also Gold Members. It is quite basic but still good. There is bar area, where one can get coffee, beer and wine (haven't seen spirits) and a buffet area. It tends to get a little crowded (and hot) sometime, but behind the buffet area there still is more seating (where it is normally very quiet and cooler).

Plaza Premium lounge used on Westjet Airlines trip. Crowded pathetic and dirty washrooms, not impressive. 15 mins to gate 2a with no real directions. Closed at 8.30 luckily I followed other WestJet travellers who knew that 2a was in that direction. Food options were non existent when I arrived.

The lounge is relatively convenient with tables and decent wifi. However, the food selection is uninspiring and several of the trays remained empty despite having paid for the ‘diner package’. The $35 cost does not include alcohol and you have to request coffee or tea. The toilets, although clean, were not impressive. The most annoying aspect, however, was a near-constant barrage of loud conversations between lounge staff and other airport workers. As well as helping themselves to generous portions of food the staff seemed to wander in and out at random. This lounge is best avoided.

First time using Mabuhay Lounge at Terminal 1, and this is a huge improvement from the previous lounges offered by Philippine Airlines to its passengers. Spacious, wide variety of food, bar and with showers. It has premium feel to it. Excellent view of the aircraft while sipping cocktails.

Philippine Airlines have just moved International flights to Terminal 1 Manila in July 2023. They no longer have their own lounges and use 3rd party lounges on our forward journey - the lounge had limited western food available [plenty of options for Asian palette] and no showers. The return lounge today at least has showers but no hot water or hairdryers, but the only food that looked appetizing were the tubs of ice cream. The seating all needs to be thrown away and start again. No comfortable seats with leg rests to stretch out.  I think the cleanliness needs reviewing also. They are catering to an international clientele, so please cater to non Asian palettes, or at least some less spicy options. We have been in lounge for several hours now, and pleased to see a good rotation of food being replaced after so many hours with fresh items. No quiet zones, so many people talking loudly using earbuds. This particular lounge is quite small compared to others, so hard to stretch out and relax. Reception girls on reception very pleasant. Bar, apart from some wine, nothing else on offer [no beer or spirits]

At check-in at Terminal 1, I was given a card map indicating the location of the lounge, but it was hard to find. I had to ask several people for directions and was then led to a private transfer by a BMW to the satellite terminal (where my flight was). Inquiring for further directions, I finally managed to locate the lounge tucked away at the far end of the mezzanine floor, or somewhere around there (not sure). At the gleaming entrance, I was warmly greeted, which immediately helped me forget the 'journey' that got me here. This is a large open-spaced lounge, with plenty of comfy sofas, high chairs and dining seating areas. On one side is an excellent view of the apron. The lounge has all the facilities one may wish to indulge in - showers, private nap rooms, family room with a children's play area, prayer room and a smoking room. It was not crowded, which added to the quiet ambiance. There was a fair variety of dining options - both Asian and International cuisine. At the noodle station, a chef would prepare a soup bowl to your liking. There was also a good selection of desserts and finger food. The Grilled Salmon and Chicken with Noodles I had was delicious. There was also a lot of staff who made me feel welcome and were constantly busy clearing up and offering to serve coffee to my couch by the apron. One item to note is that alcohol is not served in the main lounge. But just at the entrance was a bar where I was able to have a coffee and cognac before heading for my boarding gate. Overall, it was a very pleasant and restful experience.

Not a great Experience! 1st ever visit - maybe the last! Food was abysmal. Beef was chewy in Hot Dish and Chicken was tough and cold in the Curry with Potato. Young Children running around everywhere getting under your feet. Service Staff were not very friendly. To be honest it felt very much like a low cost carrier lounge. Not a great experience and hope I not go there again.

In itself the lounge is not too bad - spacious, with reasonable tear and wear, and in terms of food offer it is on the verge of reasonable and mediocre. its three sad aspects are that (1) it is severely and unevenly air-conditioned (something not very unusual in tropical climates), (2) its staff absolutely hates their job and everyone, starting from the receptionist is eager to share this attitude, and (3) it is the best kept secret of KLIA and Malaysia Airlines - I am here for the fourth time, I remember where more or less it should be, yet it takes at least 30 min of circling around, as any navigation is absent or confusing, and it is not visible from the passenger hall level. Now, when the airport is under renovation, it became even worse.

Last week, I checked in at the check in counter in Kuala Lumpur international airport for my flight to Melbourne. Being a senior citizen, I requested the personnel at the counter to help me gain entry to the Golden Lounge, using my frequent flyer Enrich reward points. I have plenty of Enrich points which I hardly use. To my surprise, I was told that Malaysia Airlines was a separate entity from the Enrich frequent flyer programme and that they could not help. Why isn't Malaysia Airlines aligned with its Enrich frequent flyer programme in its system. It is so inconvenient, especially for senior citizen to to get into the Golden Lounge without the help of personnel at the Malaysia Airlines check in counters. I am very disappointed.

It's a big lounge. At around noon, it's quite empty, However, it is inadequately staffed. The chef for the noodle station were no where to be seen, I had to signal the cleaner to go looking for her. I also noticed most staff are busy playing with their cell phones, almost totally ignoring their guests. This can only be attributed to poor management of MH. The 4 food offerings were just a beef curry, potato chickpea masala, a tomato based pasta and a veggie fried rice. A sign that the airlines is struggling to survive by going on a strict budget. It might be a while before MH can go back to its glory days.

Their Platinum lounge is tired old, stuck in the 1980s and stale (like the bread rolls). Having been a frequent flyer with MH for a decade I would think that the 2 years of the pandemic would have been a perfect breathing space to revitalise the Platnium (and also the golden) lounge product. One World has some excellent lounges at the emerald level - Cathay’s Home lounges in HK, Qatars lounges in Doha and QANTAS lounges in Sydney. The decor of the lounge while dated is still warm. The failings are on service and food/beverage offerings. In the mornings the bread product should be fresh and the cereal offerings should be more than cornflakes or coco pops. In all honesty the a golden Wing lounge has far superior choices - there you have a coffee machine with a barista - plentiful selection of fresh food All in all I have to say marketing 101 philosophy is your premium customers fly with you say 70x a year or more. They have One World flexibility. Why chose MH when the lounge reflects a sort of apathy towards the upper echelon frequent flyers?
Very disappointed. Cold food and only 2 choices and only 3 drinks available. Also tasteless and boring. Outside food much better and cheaper. Very disappointed.

Front entrance staff were great, very pleasant and polite, but can't really say the same for staff inside the lounge. Often felt like we lounge guests were being nuisances and interrupting their conversations about the guests themselves. Even taking food from the buffet feels awkward. Too many flies in the lounge as well.

Air France leverages the Royal Air Maroc Oasis Lounge in Marrakech which is a really pleasant lounge even though slightly small. Size was not a problem when we flew but wondering if they can manage during busier times. I was very pleased by the level of service including table service provided by very attentive staff members. They have a very good food and beverage selection though some of the food options may have been better hot than cold (e.g. the quiches).

The Royal Air Maroc Zenith I VIP Lounge is a comfortable, relaxing place and offers good snacks, drinks and the famous Moroccan Mint tea. There is even an outside area for those who like it and the staff is ready to serve you in case you wish so. The bar on the upper floor offers you better coffee and alcoholic drinks, as well as more comfortable seating. Be aware that many of the power outlets do not work and there are no adapters available.

The access to this lounge was denied even I could confirm my OneWorld Oro Sapphire status. They checked some papers and were not even ready to scan the boarding passes to proof if my demand was legitimate or not. Very poor attention. This has nothing to do with the airline, just arrogance or poor knowledge of staff at Swissport GVA Airport

Overall a perfect lounge. The lounge was spacious with plenty of seats and shower facilities. They offer a wide range of cuisines including dim sum and the famous BBQ pork rice. The staff was nice. Highly recommended

There’s only one word to describe this lounge – depressing. As well as Qantas, the lounge serves passengers on codeshare flights. But despite having one of the best first class international lounges in the world, the Qantas business class lounge experience is not much better than a self-serve cafeteria. Given the state of the furniture and carpet, Qantas has removed all official images of this lounge to hide how bad it is. The only thing it has going for it is the pleasant friendly staff and great coffee. The signs saying a new lounge is under construction have been up all year, yet according to the staff who work there, this doesn’t begin until October with the opening planned some time in 2027! I can’t imagine what it will look like by then.

I am gluten free. I went to get something to eat and noticed no GF foods, apart from salad. I asked for something gluten free, and was told they didn't have anything. I dont know how I pay a lot of money to be in business class, and my choice is rabbit food. Sick of it!
The lounge was pretty grim, no windows to look out. Food choices were very limited. Seating was limited most likely due to the time of day. Bar is a self-serve fridge.

Qantas have really let their standards slip. The lounge has average beverages. Same quality I can get at home, $15 bottle wines. The food is non existent. Some cubed cheese, salads, bread and soup. No actual hot food items for lunch. I used to like visiting the lounge for a meal and superior wines before a long trip. No such thing here. This cannot be the flagship Qantas lounge. It’s embarrassing compared to most other airline lounges. All I can say is the seating is okay and free drinks are okay.

The lounge is absolutely filthy, chairs and couches are all stained everywhere. Carpet hasn't been vacuumed or cleaned for a very long time. The fabric lounge seats are in disrepair. A very very poor choice of food. Actually, not much to choose from at 11:30 am, 3 old salads some grapes, stick vegetables and hummus dip. That's it. Such a disgrace, and shameful for Qantas. Better off staying downstairs, with much much more food choices.

Food was poor, and a lot of the cutlery looked like it had only been rinsed - not washed properly. The lounge was filthy and most of the furniture threadbare. The carpet in some spots was disgusting. The male toilets had excess spare toilet rolls stacked up everywhere and the sink overflows were black with mould and filth. The ladies bathrooms were worse with most of the stalls out of order. One member of staff could barely speak English. Qantas should be ashamed of this. Very disappointing to be flying business class with a ticket that was paid for personally.

The lounge is large enough, easily accessible but very busy. The service is friendly and efficient, the food is good, drink choices and quality are great, cleanliness is great, seating is comfortable. Large windows look out onto the airport apron.

Crowded lounge with a limited offer of drinks and food. Nothing special to arrive early for but still better than waiting at the gate. But it's definitely not a special experience and not Qantas standard.

This Qantas Business Class Lounge is very tired and poorly staffed. Floors are dirty. No Towels for showers (they didnt get their delivery I was advised by front desk staff with a smile) and they told me to use paper towels to dry myself off! Tap handles missing and mould throughout showers. Absolutely disgusting.  Do not visit if you do not have to. Oh and if you are coming off long haul and want a shower like me, bring your own towel, and a wrench for the tap handle.

LHR Qantas Business Lounge is a pleasant surprise.  There is a restaurant at the ground level which has a nice selection of food with table service. Although the side note is that Platinum members appear to have access to reserved tables so it can be limited options if you are not a member. The desserts were a bit more limited and are self-service. Upstairs is a bar and seating area. Not quite as high quality as the lower level and a little bit hectic, but overall it is still a pleasant environment to wait for a flight. And feels of higher quality than the lounges in Sydney.

It all starts with a very abrupt and patronising welcome by the gatekeepers. It sets the tone for the rest of the experience: terrible coffee, food that is of such low standard and very, very limited options. All this in a lounge that feels dated. Really an embarrassment to Qantas.

I purchased a flight ticket from the Qantas website on a China Airlines codeshare flight from Sydney to Taipei. Upon arriving at the front desk of the Qantas business class lounge, I presented my flight ticket with my flight code and Qantas membership number. I asked the front desk staff to verify my lounge reservation (as the lounge was redeem with an AMEX credit card invitation). She didn`t even notice my flight ticket and she said "we never work with with China airline, I don't know where your ticket is from". Eventually she probably realized she was wrong, and she let me into the lounge room. As you can see on the photo, the buffet area was messy and uncomfortable. Nothing was refilled and seem no one do cleaning. I only stayed for about 30 minutes or so. To sum it up, the experience was terrifying.

Overcrowded and lacking in all that you would expect from a Business Class lounge. Due to flight delays we were in the lounge for around 7 hours. Extremely poor food offering - no decent breakfast option and lunch only after 12 noon. Lunch is a generous description - if you call unappealing chilli con carne (a cheap, stingy and "cop-out" offering also favoured by British Airways and a universally unappealing meal choice) a decent lunchtime offering. Officious staff which I found rather a surprise - like they're doing you a favour by letting you into "their" lounge. So many lessons to be learnt here - of what not  to do.

Had the opportunity to use the newly opened Qantas lounge at Changi on the 10th of April and cant say that I wasn't overly impressed at all. Cold uninviting and lacked any atmosphere at all. The staff however are wonderful and made up for what the lounge itself lacked. Am wondering who may have designed the space and secondly who approved it I expected Qantas to come up with a lot better.

Had the opportunity to use the newly opened Qantas lounge at Changi on the 10th of April and cant say that I wasn't overly impressed at all. Cold uninviting and lacked any atmosphere at all. The staff however are wonderful and made up for what the lounge itself lacked. Am wondering who may have designed the space and secondly who approved it I expected Qantas to come up with a lot better.

Lounge entry ok. Grumpy barista serving coffee. Horrible toilets and very long wait to use one! Lounge needs to totally redesign toilets and incorporate high quality urinals to speed up wait times. Toilet problem is not just the lounge but the whole of Copenhagen airport!

Totally overrun. Loud, crowded, children running and screaming around everywhere. Nowhere to sit. Obviously too little capacity. SAS in Norway particularly (but also Sweden) has this ridiculous policy of basically selling gold card membership to everyone. All you need is an Amex Card and a second Eurobonus credit card (total cost for the cards is 350 Euro per year), fly twice and bingo you have a gold card. Massive deflation effect on actual gold membership. When boarding you see a third or more of the passengers get on the plane during business class/gold boarding although there is only 6 rows of business class? So the privilege of early boarding is useless. Less queues when boarding economy :) In fact, all the privileges of a business class ticket is gone due to this policy. Long lines and fewer screening machines at priority security check. You can see the economy security line going much faster. Early boarding is more crowded than economy boarding. Sitting in SAS Lounge is far more crowded, loud and stressful, than sitting in nice lounge chairs located at most gates. So paying for actual business class ticket with SAS hasnt been worth the money for a long time SAS, but now it has become less efficient, more stressful then economy because it is half the plane is a gold member.

Overcrowded, dirty, wine from the tap, no spirits. This Lounge is a shame for any Star Alliance Airline. We are very much disappointed especially because we booked first class from Zurich and are on the way to this flight.

We flied business class on Thai Airways therefore we were able to use SAS lounge at Stockholm Arlanda airport. The lounge is OK but not so big and was quite crowded. Not varieties of food and drink to serve.

We flied SAS to Oslo from Stockholm on economy class but we were able to use Norrsken Lounge because we are Priority Pass nember. The lounge is not so big but not so crowded. However, we found that the food and drinks were quite limited. By the tine we used, there was only one staff to take care the lounge which made her very busy to serve many passengers.
The lounge was so full we could not get in. People sitting everywhere. Unfortunately, lost gold so my J class ticket did not allow me to enter the LH lounge. Bad business class value

No information given by the counter ground staff upon check in/ bag drop. The Prime Class lounge used by Saudi Arabian Airlines is located after the immigration and can be easily found. It shares the same roofing as the whole airport (open ceiling - just walls) and therefore uncomfortably cold as the rest of the airport. You can only use the lounge for 3 hours. Whether you want to use it during the first or last part of your arrival to the airport is up to you. The lounge is beautifully decorated, giving me the impression of Arabian tents. However it is a small lounge, sufficient as the number of passengers are not many at the time I was there. Very limited food/ drink options. Toilets are satisfactorily clean. Staff are polite.

The lounge in Jeddah spacious, clean and comfortable; the buffet is ok for those without pretensions, the wi-fi in the lounge was instead a problem to be able to connect. La lounge a Jeddah spaziosa, e pulita, devo dire confortevole; il buffet ok per chi non ha pretese, il wi-fi alla lounge è invece è stato un problema per riuscire a connettersi.

SATS Premier Lounge located in Changi Airport Terminal-3 can best be described as a low grade, badly arranged, poorly equipped lounge offering mediocre food of low quality with little or no Indian vegetarian options. The "Check In" PIC was totally unprofessional & though we were 3 adults & a 16 month old Infant, she scanned the Dragon Pass that we had & charged for an infant even though infants under 2 yrs of age are free! (I believe this is incorrect since we have availed lounges all over the world (travelling after Covid) & never had an issue with an infant). The layout was cramped, badly arranged with mostly seats facing each other ,giving no privacy except staring into the opposite person's face. Tables & Seating for families were few & difficult to secure. The food was awful! Apart from a "veg pasta dish", there were no other Veg offerings which is shocking, since Singapore has a large Indian Population & most Indians are Vegetarian. A number of food containers were empty & had no food in them (at 12 Noon).There was hardly any hot Indian Veg dishes available. There was some bread slices but NO butter. Salad was a mishmash of tomatoes, cucumber, onions etc. Even Salt packets were missing. Apart from Yoghurt cups, there was no other Dessert.
