Some Hard Drinks, Liquor & Soft drinks were available, which we did not avail. The Staff were most unfriendly, communicated little. Even the " massage chairs" were mostly inoperational. Out of the two toilets, one was bad. Overall view is that this lounge is of pedestrian quality and it is shocking how badly this SATS Premier Lounge is operated. This lounge should be avoided by those passengers who are looking for a decent meal, quiet ambience & a relaxing environment.

I’m surprised of the bad quality of this Singapore Airlines lounge in Terminal 2. It’s like an old canteen, noisy and uncomfortable. I don’t understand how Singapore Airlines can offer this to their premium customers.

You’ll find this lounge on Level 4 of the Departure Hall in the International Terminal near Gate 81.  It’s looks a bit dated so it’s not about to win any awards and it’s on the small side but this is to be expected. Despite a fairly full flight there were no more than 10 people there when I visited so it was peaceful and quiet. There was a surprising range of hot and cold food available as well as a selection of desserts. I was starving so sampled most of everything and took advantage of the coffee machine to have a cappuccino before my flight. All in all it was a pleasant surprise and well worth a visit.

This lounge offered great tasting food & I had the breakfast which was wonderful. Food was hot & quite a good choice available being morning. Juices were fresh & the mango in the small bottles were extremely good. Seating choice was good but lacking proper recliners which would have been nice. As with most business class lounges these days they become overcrowded very quickly & don’t cater to the true business class passenger anymore so this lounge needs to be expanded to provide more space & comfort due to the increase in passenger traffic. WiFi here was good & stable which gets a plus point. Toilets again need to be expanded as only 2 proper toilets with about 10 urinals. 3 showers only so again needs to be doubled. On the plus side they were kept very clean. Staff were very efficient in cleaning up used plates & dishes which was good to see & very respectful towards the passengers using this lounge. Overall these days I tend to use the lounge to eat have a quick sit down then off into the main areas of the airport due to lounges being overcrowded. There are quieter areas in the main airport than lounges these days. Best thing in this lounge was the food which is worth visiting for before you board your flight.

The only good thing about this lounge is the food. It’s a lounge that is well overcrowded, loud & imagine only 3 showers! We didn’t stay there long as your better off in the actual terminal which is less crowded which is hard to believe! It badly needs expanding in all areas & there no windows so feels like a prison. Best to avoid & use the one at T3 if you can.

What impressed me first was the elegant entrance. A screen of floral art, resembling Japanese paintings, and the SilverKris logo beyond gave it a feel of elegance. Receiving a warm welcome I was ushered inside. It's not a particularly large space, and I was later told it could cater to around 100 passengers. It was seven in the morning, and delightfully quiet.  The excellent mood lighting, design, and soothing colours added to its ambiance. There was a plethora of varied styles of furniture and seating. Some also have semiprivate booths, with a reading light and USB charging point - ideal if you need to do some work. The layout seems carefully designed. The first half of the lounge is typically the seating or relaxing area, in the middle features the bar, and beyond is the dining. What secondly made an impression on me was the well-appointed large bar. It looked attractive, with colourful glass and ceramic ornamentals placed above that added to the design. The selection of alcoholic drinks and cocktails was vast. Despite the early hours, I was treated to a glass of Lanvin & Fils champagne. I was promptly offered a second round and later I came back to be served with a large cappuccino. There was also self-service Asahi and Singha draft beer. The third and final thing that greeted me was of course the food section. There wasn't an extensive selection. As it was breakfast time, the hot food dishes seemed minimal. But the variety of other food items made it all so appetising. It was equally the presentation, lovingly laid out with added floral decoration that made it all look so good. Even the boring old white-bread sandwiches looked upgraded! There was a chef circling and replenishing any items. My favourite was the Chinese Dim Sum. The selection including, Cha Siu Buns, Prawn Siu Mai and Steamed Prawn Dumplings was delicious. Tempted to go for seconds, but resisted knowing that breakfast would be also be served on my flight. There were plenty of hot and cold drinks, and the most refreshing was the fresh young coconut water. Although deserts are not my thing, I did indulge in a chocolate Ice Cream from a Hagen das Fridge. All the usual facilities are available, like WiFi and charging points. The washrooms are basic and there are no shower rooms. No sleeprooms either. I guess these are due to the flights being short-haul, and not necessitating such additional facilities. It's clear that the lounge is not designed for long layovers. Overall, this was one of the finer lounges I have visited and reflects Singapore Airlines reputation. I was there for just under two hours, but would have been happy to stay longer.

I am not sure why they were playing Christmas Carols on 17th January 2025. There were many main-courses but none of them could be described as western, the nearest food item being spicy tuna sandwich or egg sandwich. The TV volume was overwhelming when it should actually have been in silent mode (with subtitles). It is probably the worst airline lounge of all of the airlines that are 4* or 5*. Some customers had PED's on full volume and the place was hardly conducive to a pre-flight relaxing experience. The seating was standard except for a couple of lap-top tables. I expected something better of Singapore airlines so was surprised and disappointed

Terminal 2 is not as fancy as Terminal 3 and that is also reflected in the lounge. Terminal 2 being a bit older The lounge is a good size but often very full so not so comfortable in term of noise. Food choice is ok but far below the lounge in terminal 3 There are not enough staff, for example ice cream bowl and spoon runned out. Not enough staff going through the lounge to pick up dirty dishes.

One of only two lounges at Phuket airport, there's no real choice. This lounge is second rate - the staff are pleasant but food and beverage options are poor and very limited. Food doesn't get updated regularly it seems. Seating comfort is average and seating seems old.

My ticket was with Asiana Airlines but as a Star Alliance Gold member I was able to enter the SilverKris Lounge of Singapore Airlines. The food is superb (they were serving chili crab for lunch and a made-to-order bowl of laksa), the bar is well-stocked and well-staffed, the facilities are top-notch , they offer skincare masks for the face and neck). Definitely the best lounge in Incheon T1.

Visited in June 2023 and the lounge was amazing, there was a various amounts of meals, beverages to choose on. I visited the lounge on dinner time, they had an option of bolognese pasta with cheese, French fries and nuggets, dim sum, prata, etc. Everything is free to grab, all the meals are displayed in one area and you can grab as much as you want. They also had ice cream in the fridge. They also provided wine, champagne, soft drinks, coffee, water, anything you’d like to drink. The lounge was very clean, there was many staff coming to each table, looking if you’re done with your meal so they can clean up the mess and the dishes. The lounge is also very big, bathrooms inside were clean. Showers are also provided, as well as the towel, hairdryer, soap, toothbrush. Be reminded you have to book a reservation for the shower! There was also an area where you could sleep or rest for free. No reservations needed for this one. Wifi was very strong, I could play games, scroll through TikTok, open instagram, text in WhatsApp, etc.
A very busy lounge in the late afternoon. Good food offering, alcohol only available from manned bar and pretty standard. Difficult to get two seats together.

Wonderful lounge to rest before catching the flight to Dubai. This lounge has improved since the last time I flew with SQ. The lounge was nice and kept clean at all times! I was happy enough with the much and better improved lounge at Changi Airport Terminal 3.

First time in new lounge, absolutely packed, seating layout is not well thought through here, many 6 seater semi circle bays were taken up by 2 people either lying down to sleep or full of their bags. Other lounger seats with kids lying asleep. Use of space very inefficient. Aircon not working well and Wi-Fi not working. I have been traveling SQ business class for 30 years and this is by far my worst lounge experience.

Flying with EVA Air, I had the option of Air Canada's Maple Leaf Lounge or Singapore Airline's Silverkris Lounge. I decided on the latter, based on my high expectations of SA. However, I was warned it can get crowded. There was no smiling welcome, but a polite gesture towards the entrance. My first reaction was how small the lounge was, considering it shared it with other airlines as well as two night flights that evening with Singapore Airlines. There was a variety of seating options, tightly spaced restaurant style dining tables, lounge chairs, stools and a few cubicles, but which did not offer any privacy. One side of the lounge had a view of the apron with aircraft in their air jetties. Within half an hour of my visit, the place had got so crowded, that one had to share the seating where others were grouped and chatting. This prompted me to head to the tiny bar which had four bar stools. The drinks selection was limited, but a friendly barman made all the difference, and he was grateful when I showed him how to make a Manhattan cocktail for me. This opened up a chat and along with a few other fellow passengers who gathered standing around, and engaged in small talk, which helped to pass the time pleasantly. One passenger did complain when asking for champagne, was offered only prosecco! When I commented on how busy the place was to the barman, he replied "it can get a lot more crowded than this". There was a nice selection of finger food and salads, elegantly displayed, but small items of hot food - vegetarian noodles, chicken curry, pasta and boiled rice. I loved the little freezer filled with tubs of chocolate ice cream too. The toilets were basic, and although clean, there were no toiletries whatsoever. With all the praiseworthy reviews about Singapore airlines, one expected the lounge to reflect that glamour too. Sadly, while all the basic comforts were adequately provided, nothing outstanding helped to enhance the experience one expected. The lounge layout itself felt too crammed and no quiet areas to relax in. Perhaps too many people in too small a space.

Could use this lounge normally only accessible to Business Class and PPS Members, as the SQ Gold Lounge was still under renovation. Very impressed by the new concept, though seating can be a challenge during peak times. There is a good food and drinks selection and a nice perk is a full serviced bar for cocktails.

My first visit to SIA's new 1st class lounge (which in fact is a lounge for Solitaire PPS members only, because first class-passengers may use the 'Private Room') was disappointing. Located in a dark, not well lit tunnel with no daylight, where you can look from the bathrooms in the very end all the way to the lounge-entrance and believe you are located in an ordinary waiting-room rather than a cosy place to relax. The lounge is half of the size of the former 1st class lounge and was overcrowded. In the center you find a huge dining area, which seems compared to the places to relax, oversized. A small bar (less than half size of the former one) is located on the right and behind it you now find a big open kitchen, taking again space from the lounge itself, rather than hidden in the back as in the former lounge. The restrooms are in the back and while the toilets itself now are equipped with Japanese toilets (water flushing and cleaning), one urinal was covered with fluid and paper-waste was on the ground of the handwashing-area. The showers are an improvement, because they have a private toilet, as well now. The amenities however are poor: no shaving foam anymore, just shaving-cream. New is that they got 4 closed rooms, where you can sleep either on Slumberettes or real beds - but for a maximum of 2 hours only - which is by far too little for a good sleep. Boarding Passes also cannot be printed at the lounge anymore, so you need to walk to a SIA-transfer-center outside to get changes done. Wine is being served out of machines, another human touch gone. The choice of drinks is also lower, e. g. no Grand Marnier any more. As for the food, taste was good while cheaper dishes are offered: chicken satay instead of lamb or eggs any style for breakfast only - with neither hash browns or beans offered. No cheese or sushi-platters, overall the difference to the business-class section of the lounge (which I also visited) is marginal. Magazines and newspapers are not available. In the very end, I decided to move to the business-class section of the lounge with bright sunlight, more empty space and a by far more friendly atmosphere. Yes, the quality of the wines and the champagne is still better in the 1st class section, but other than that and the free Häagen Dazs ice-cream offered there, it's not worth all the money you have to spend becoming a Solitaire PPS member just to enjoy this disappointing place.

A very good lounge with good service a la carte dining ordering via app. Food nothing super-special but sufficient portions and options, and all in all definitely okay and above standard. Showers not exceptional but oK. Friendly staff.
Basic lounge, not comfortable or relaxing. I arrived late in the evening, was tired, but found nowhere quiet to sit and pass the time. Food was good though.

The Al Safwa First Class Lounge was once a model of calm, a true refuge for the weary traveller. In recent times, however, it has become more crowded and less pleasant. The service remains warm and earnest. Al Safwa no longer feels genuinely exclusive; it increasingly resembles just another premium lounge rather than the sanctuary it once was. One is left to wonder whether entrance standards have been relaxed. Access to this lounge is not inexpensive, and I pay those fees willingly for a particular level of experience. I would not hesitate to pay more if it meant restoring the older Al Safwa climate - quiet, restrained, and unmistakably First Class.

Qatar Airways doesn't have a First Class Lounge in Dubai to the same level as Doha. Instead, First Class passengers flying Qatar are invited to the Ahlan First Class Lounge, which offers a calm luxurious atmosphere, with exceptional restaurant-quality food and drinks. Most importantly, I found the staff to be extremely friendly and attentive.

When it comes to sheer size, design and facilities, the Qatar Business Class Lounge in Doha has no equal. If you were to describe it with one word it would be – ‘breathtaking’. The attention to detail, quality of furniture and fittings are outstanding. This is matched by the food and beverage offering that includes a full al-a-carte dining experience.  Unfortunately, I suffer from terminal cancer and require wheelchair assistance between the lounge and the boarding gates. Despite assurances, this has never gone without a hitch, but this time was the worst. As instructed, I sat in the small waiting area near the lounge entry station. The boarding time printed on my boarding pass came and went without any sign of a wheelchair. I expressed my concern to the staff, only to be told it was too soon, as they were only pre-boarding. My question, “Isn’t pre-boarding for people in wheelchairs?”, received another rebuke. It was only when I demanded to be taken to the aircraft that a wheelchair appeared, still with a member of staff talking insistently in an attempt to justify himself to the point I had to demand he cease talking to me. I was the last passenger to board and very nearly missed the flight.

This lounge is like going to a 5 star hotel with family, quiet and prayers spaces. The quiet places are bedrooms with a shower. One can for a fee soak in a jacuzzi, get massages and mani/pedis. This is a vast lounge with open spaces. Doesn't feel overcrowded even during busy periods. Artifacts from the Museum of Islamic Art are on display. The lounge has its own duty free shop. It has a 250 seat restaurant that serves full service tapas type meals. Staff are welcoming and very professional. For connecting flights, the lounge has its own departure gate which transports passengers in 12 seat buses to their gate. The bathrooms are very clean with constant cleaning by attendants. Since we had a 9 hour layover, we booked one of the bedrooms to rest and shower before our next flight.

This is huge and spacious lounge on two levels. The lower level has plenty of seating with drinks stations dispersed throughout its length. The upper level has a full restaurant with buffet stations and a full service menu serving tapas sized meals. Having experienced the Al Safwa lounge on our outbound flights, this lounge appeared overcrowded especially on the restaurant level and a bit of let down. The staff is very friendly and welcoming. The only drawback to this lounge is that there was only bathroom on the restaurant level. Nonetheless, this is one of the best business class lounges I've been through.

Al Safwa First Lounge, Doha I have visited Al Safwa several times, most recently in August 2025. Physically it is an exceptional space, an oasis of calm. What sets it apart from other great lounges in the same league - such as Lufthansa’s First Terminal or the Swiss First Lounge - is its staff, composed largely of Asians (predominantly Indians), whose warmth gives the place a character unique to the region. By contrast, the European lounges, while elegant and luxurious, can feel somewhat sterile. It was therefore with some dismay that my latest visit fell short of past standards. The lounge felt more crowded than usual, and the wait for a shower exceeded an hour. My sense is that the entry requirements have been relaxed. I would urge Qatar Airways to preserve the exclusivity that once defined Al Safwa.
Outstanding Business Class lounge at Doha Airport offering different dining options, comfortable seating, and shower facilities. Highly recommend the facilities.

This has to be the best business class lounge in the world. It is huge, on two levels, offer many food and drink options, including a la carte. The lounge is very comfortable and There are also showers, luggage storage and plenty of staff members to assist you in any way. i needed assistance to get to a gate far from the lounge, I could not have been more pleased with the service, much appreciated!
Excellent lounge. The best for a long time ago. Perfect service, good food, great comfort, sunny atmosphere at 11 floor. Excellent staff - warm welcome. Congrats !!!

First time visiting this beautiful lounge and definitely not the last. I decided to check out this lounge after previously visiting the same one in the South Pier of the airport. Compared to the South Pier lounge, the Platinum and Gold Lounge North offers a more spacious and open ambiance, providing plenty of room to relax before your next connecting flight. The food selection was excellent, offering both à la carte and buffet options. The staff were attentive and had a great sense of humor, which made the experience even more enjoyable. The only downside? The long queue for the shower rooms. But overall, it was a great experience!

lounge_name: Platinum and Gold Lounge Concourse C
review: The Qatar Airways lounge for Platinum and Gold members at Concourse C is a perfect blend of luxury and relaxation. The space is beautifully designed—spacious and comfortable, offering an ideal atmosphere to unwind before a flight. Every detail feels thoughtful, from the comfortable seating to the variety of quiet corners. The hospitality is exceptional; the staff are attentive, elegant, and always ready to assist, making you feel truly valued as a member. Whether you're enjoying a meal, catching up on work, or simply relaxing, the lounge experience is peaceful and seamless. It’s a fantastic retreat that elevates the entire travel experience.

Nicely located lounge close to Gate B2 with friendly staff at reception and plenty of space for guests. Good variety is limited but I personally find it one of the best lounges in HIA with excellent WiFi and clean toilets.

Incredible eating options, with excellent bar services. Service generally outstanding, friendly and helpful. I wish I would always have this standard when travelling business class, also with other airlines. It comes close to what a real first class lounge should be, even if travelling in business class. Not airline or lounge to be blamed, unpleasant are some co-travelers dressed like going to the beach or coming from the gym. I am afraid that is a general trend while travelling long haul, but I think it is a little disrespectful towards the well groomed and impeccable staff.

This the best lounge at Dhaka International Airport. Very well decorated lounge that has a very nice prayer room for Muslims and clean toilet. It serves Indian, continental and Thai-Chinese food; food was delicious. The beverages include fresh juice, soft drinks and tea-coffee. The food was prepared by the Westin Hotel, Dhaka. There is a small library to read books, magazines and newspapers.

This lounge is absolutely the best. Customer service is outstanding. As I was walking gingerly with a full cup of macchiato coffee to my seat, a service came right over and offered to take the coffee to my seat! He even made an extra coffee because I spilled some from the cup onto the saucer. The other agents kept track of my connection flight times and reminded me to proceed to the gate. The only suggestion I have is that the rest rooms could have been larger with shower amenities.

A visit to the recently refurbished Al-Safwa lounge at Doha's Hamad airport is always an extraordinary experience. Admission is only for passengers travelling in Qatar Airways First Class or QR Platinum members. Status customers from other Oneworld partners have no access. There is an escalator to the spacious reception where people need to go to be admitted. There seem to be more staff than guests and the atmosphere is friendly and warm. People can go enjoy a drink at the bar or have a meal at the à la carte restaurant. Service at the restaurant needs to be streamlined. I think the staff have not been properly trained as waiters. I hadn't finished my starter yet when soup and main course arrived. The selection of food is great and all I ordered (lentil soup, wagyu beef carpaccio and lamb) was delicious. The champagne was Lanson Brut Black Label. After dinner, I went to the spa and had a great massage. It needs to be mentioned that the spa treatments are not included and have to be paid for. Altogether a fantastic experience difficult to be topped.

Beautifully appointed lounge with plenty of quiet and relaxed seating area. Very nice restaurant area and small but very adequate food range. Very nice toilet and shower facilities . Attentive service. Very clean.

Nice lounge. I arrived around 8am for my 11am Malaysia Airlines flight to KL.  I headed straight to bathrooms who had attendants waiting outside to service regularly. I sat in lounge area which had ample charging facilities and a nice view of some departure gates. I went to dining area which had a sumptuous display of cold items available. The buffet hot food was a little tepid in temperature but tasty enough. Service was efficient without being over bearing. I was advised that non Qatar flights were not announced so you have to check the screen yourself for boarding updates. The lounge was very clean and well presented with drinks and snacks available to help yourself to.  Very pleasant experience.

This is a fabulous lounge. Service is impeccable. Beautiful view of the Garden area of the airport. The staff are friendly and attentive. They try to anticipate what the guest wants. Any reasonable wish will be fulfilled. The selection of food is variable and large. One can order à la carte or use the buffet. There is even a sushi bar. Premium drinks are readily available. There is a quiet area with several tastefully decorated resting rooms which operates on a “first come, first served” base. Drinks cannot be taken into the rooms though. The lounge is exceptionally clean and well kept, but it only opened a few weeks ago. There is a Louis Vuitton cafe which, unfortunately has not opened yet. This is one of my favorite lounges and the best business lounge I have been to lately. Certainly better than First Class lounges of most airlines. Can’t wait to use it on my next flight via Hamad International.

Very nice and big lounge. During my stay there was only a handful other people at the lounge which made it a very nice experience. Also the staff was very lovely and helpful. Food was buffet style but of good quality. The wine on the other hand was surprisingly bad.

While three people scanned my boarding pass to access the lounge and they all noted that there was a problem with the boarding pass, no one could tell me what to do or where to go - or what time I needed to leave the lounge to arrive at the gate in time. Very large and airy lounge with lots of seating and food and drink areas. I couldn't access the menu though was my boarding pass didn't have the required QR code. The shower wait was one hour which seemed like too long. Luckily at the very chaotic gate I received the new and correct boarding pass.
Lounge in Bangkok is small, but good with a la carte dining. A single champagne, Gosset, was offered. Lounge was almost full and quite vibrant. One of the three best lounges in BKK.

El Safwa is too huge with little load. No fish, terraria, no music, no gym.  Worse for me is the design and the granite, glass, and steely. Not a single cozy place. The dorms are OK, very small; lack windows. The high ceilings allow for fresh air. The a la carte dining offered is supposed to be an asset, however my waiting time is >30 Minutes. There is no buffet in the lounge.
Excellent service and well managed lounge with comfortable seating. The overall cleanliness and attention to detail is hard to beat. Quality of the food and wines were terrific.

A lounge with 2 sections. We were guided to the premium section where we were for approx. 2 ½ hours. The lounge is decorated in an attractive way and very comfortable. Unfortunately almost no daylight and a little dark. View on the departure hall. We can imagine that when crowded, people feel slightly unpleasant, perhaps claustrophobic. Great internet. We did not notice if shower facilities were available. The lounge was clean. Food and drinks were pretty well sorted, varied and of good quality and above all tasty. Staff was nice.

Before covid, Qatar Airways used the Qantas Lounge. Apparently they switched to the Marhaba Lounge. Unfortunately and bad choice. The lounge is small, and the sound of the TV filled the room in a very unpleasant way. Although no one was watching, the attendant refused to switch off the sound. We seriously considered to go to another lounge and pay a fee for entrance. The lounge consists of 3 rooms: a bar/buffet with very unattractive furniture, a room to work, however very dark and the main room with the TV noise. Shower facilities were very poor: small space, no vent. Food and drinks limited but OK. Nice view on the tarmac.

The Premiere Lounge is OK but nothing more. WiFi password on a sign at the reception counter. Voucher is not enough to get in so keep your boarding card ready. Alcohol behind the bar so you have to order it. Coffee maker broken so no coffee with milk was available.
This first time I came to the Mariner Lounge since I have been seafarer. It was really best experience, Sohan from f&b was very humble and friendly. Thanks a lot, and all here are free of charge

Qatar Airways use the Menzies Executive Lounge at Stockholm Arlanda Airport, and it is the worst lounge I ever visited! Boring, small and dirty. Extremely limited drinks and food. Stale bread, tasteless cheese, bad red wine on tap, tasteless beer on tap. When you finally got a glass, it was warm. I'll never go back to this lounge. I rather pay for a good tasty sandwich and beer in the terminal. I don't understand how a prestigious airline as Qatar Airways can use this lounge.

This lounge is world famous for its size, design and great services. I had not used it for several years during the hiatus of the pandemic. But on the last trip, transiting through DOH, it was a chance to re-acquaint ourselves. The main priority was to use the showers. But there was a queue of about 10 people waiting to use the only 2 working showers in the larger of the two shower facilities. The other shower facility also had a long queue, with no Qatar staff managing its usage. The lounge itself was extremely busy, with very little seating availability. For their flagship lounge, Qatar Airways seem to have greatly under planned the demand, or over-offered its availability. Luckily there was a very helpful member of staff who helped take us to the Gold Lounge and to use the facilities there, so we managed showers, and to catch our connecting flight. That is impressive, but if Qatar Airways wants to retain its premier title, it needs to rethink its strategy here. And quickly, with the upcoming FIFA tournament.

I used this lounge when it first opened about 4 years ago, and it was excellent. Had read that it was not maintained properly, but on the recent departure from Bangkok, everything was in good working order, with excellent service from staff, and good snacks, The only quibble was the champagne: only Pommery, which was corked. They opened another, but it too was corked. There was quite a wide selection of hot and cold food, and given the dire food service inflight, it would have been wiser to choose to eat here, especially as we complied with the airlines recommended 3 hour pre-flight check in, (which took about 30 minutes, from check in to lounge).

The Al-Mourjan lounge in Hamad International Airport. As with any lounge experience the second time round is often better than the first. I had specifically chosen to have a long layover in Doha as, due to my age, I find that two shorter flights with a layover between is a much more comfortable experience. My first visit to the lounge was a seven hour layover between flights. I didn't know of the quiet area and that I could have a sleep for awhile so I didn't take advantage of that on my first visit. However I did use the shower facilities which were absolutely superb. It will be difficult to find anything bad to say about the staff in the lounge is they were attentive clearing used plates and cups not intruding when it was clear that they were not needed. The lounge is magnificent it's been awarded a place as the number one business class lounge in the world and I can easily understand why. I was there during one of the busy periods when I arrived in Doha, and even so there was plenty more seating available food was available links for available and the number of staff employed were easily enough for the guests in the lounge. We now come along to the food in the restaurant. The breakfast was very nice I had eggs Florentine they were beautifully presented wonderfully served with excellent table service, I had arrived at 7 o'clock in the morning and the lunchtime service didn't take place until 11 o'clock in the morning, had I known then what I know now, I would have taken the opportunity to go and have a nap in the quiet area. However since my flight to London was a little after 12 o'clock I didn't want to miss the chance of lunch in the restaurant so stayed awake. Once again in the restaurant presentation was beautiful service was excellent unfortunately the quality of the food that was served was a huge disappointment, the two options which I considered to be and salmon. The salmon although the presentation on the plate was absolutely beautiful was crunchy on the outside and dry as a bone on the inside. I did try the beef and was told that medium rare was not available as it is prepared by a catering company outside the airport and the restaurant reheat and serves it therefore it has to be well done. Some people may like well done beef, it certainly is not to my taste. To the credit of the restaurant staff I did tell them that the salmon was really rather overcooked, which was an understatement, and they insisted on preparing another piece of salmon for me to try, the chef who cooked it came to the table, I was too embarrassed to tell them that it was virtually no different from the first piece crunchy on the outside, which could be out an okay thing, but still dry as a bone on the inside, so I politely declined to tell them my impression of the second piece. I didn't have time to try anything else on the menu as my flight was being called.

Qatar Airways has closed their own lounge in Bangkok airport during the pandemic, I'm not sure when it's going to reopen. As a result they using the Miracle lounge in Bangkok airport. I would say that the Miracle lounge is only really so-so, the drink selection is quite limited as is the food selection. Whilst of course as in any business Lounge you can eat as much as you like and drink as much as you like the selection really dissuaded you from doing that. The lounge is okay, you do have a multitude of power points so it's not difficult to find a seat with a power point adjacent to it,. Of course you can eat as much as you like I found that a curry and rice was the best option available to my taste, there were few other snacks that I tried but nothing really exciting. During my 4 flights I tried three different lounges one in Bangkok one in Doha, twice. and one in Heathrow Airport the Bangkok Lounge was definitely at the bottom of the list. It's definitely better than waiting in the main terminal or at the gate with no question as to that, I sincerely hope that Qatar Airways is able to reopen their own lounge in the near future.

Since the upgrades to the terminal Qatar Airways now use the 1903 lounge and it is is bright, airy and well laid out with lots of comfortable seating areas and a very good choice of food and drinks available. We were there at 5am and were welcomed by a very friendly member of staff who handed us over to Alexander and Janine who looked after us superbly. I would thoroughly recommend this lounge to any traveller using T2 it makes a wonderful start to your journey.
Very clean lounge with both a buffet for food as the possibility to order freshly prepared food. Impressive selection of beverages. Friendly service and very clean restrooms

Probably the most luxurious lounge I ever saw, and feeling very sorry that it was so early in the morning so i could not try some of the great wines available including 2 second growth Bordeaux. I had a great breakfast with delicious fruits and could not resist one glass of premium Champagne. Extremely friendly service and luxurious and clean restrooms

The Coral Lounge in Phuket operated by AOT must be the worst and most depressing business lounge ever. Super small with furniture from the 1980s. No champagne, ice cold red wine and seating like a school dinner hall. A few armchairs are there but since the lounge is so small you are lucky if you get one. Though you can have a neck and shoulder massage while you drink your cold red wine. This is not where you want to spend 1 or 2 hours waiting!!

The lounge is nice and very spacious; it has plenty of options for food and beverages; it is also family friendly. I like the special corners of Al Ameed coffee and the ice cream. Staff are nice and helpful. Perhaps number of toilets should be increased and praying area can be improved

I flew in from Riyadh on RJ. And I had a 6 hour transit before my next flight to Heathrow. As a QNB First Holder I was entitled to both Petra and Crown Class Lounge. I proceeded to Petra Lounge who did not allow me to enter as it was a long transit. Which was disappointing. I headed to Crown Class Lounge. Which from the outside looks like Al Safwa First of Doha. But when you actually experience it you wish you just sat in the main airport lounge instead. There was no food. And I was starving after the long journey. Seating was uncomfortable and it was overall the worst lounge. I’ve sat in lounges all across the world and its safe to say this was by far the worst, 0 standard and rude staff !!

Great quality regional Business Lounge. Quiet area for work and relaxation. Kids room in lounge behind thickened glass. Wide selection of food and refreshments. Staff professional and attentive. Showers clean and well maintained. Best regional lounge I have experienced for a long time, clean and well maintained.

Excellent service and very polite staff. There is a shower room and to separate room with to separate rooms for relaxing and getting a power nap. The use of the facility is limited to 2.5 hours, but the staff just rescan your membership and boarding card for extension without any extra cost.

If you are flying Business class / international/ out of terminal 5 and airline is in STAR ALLIANCE you have no lounge! I have flown EVA last year and Air India coming up this December and your 3 hour wait is without a lounge. Star Alliance prominent presence, United has no lounge in terminal 5, nor do any other Star alliance members. United Lounges, including the one POLARIS, are only in terminal 1 or 2. So you could check in at your airline in terminal 5, take the ATS "train" to terminal 1 or 2, go thru TSA, use a united/ star alliance lounge, then only from the hours of 11:30-22:30 can you take TTB/ terminal transfer bus to go back to terminal 5 without going thru security again. If is morning flight, would have to pass thru TSA again on return to terminal 5 via the ATS/train. I would not fly business class STAR ALLIANCE airline out of ORD unless on UNITED.

The Star Alliance lounge is located after passport control in the departure area of Terminal 3 at Cairo Airport. Staff are efficient but a bit cool. The seats are standard business issue and functional. There is only a small selection of food which is rather bland and nit very nice. The lounge is brightly lit and quite loud - so forget relaxation.

Visited the LAX Star Alliance Lounge again 05/09/23 at 8-11 PM on our way back from SE Asian trip with Hubby. The lounge was quite busy due to many flights to Asia leaving around midnight. However there are still seats available, and buffet and drinks always replenished timely. The cleaners are making more rounds now, dirty plates and glass cleaned quickly so newcomers can find empty seats right away. We chat with an EVA Air rep for the lounge who asked our opinion comparing this lounge with others such as United's. We told her we like both; this lounge due to the better food and beverage selection, but United has a more spacious lounge in Terminal 7 even though the food and especially beverage selection couldn't compare with Star Alliance lounge. There's always tradeoffs between these two that we need to consider when we're visiting LAX, including the terminal we're leaving from or arriving to, and time we need to travel between terminals.

Used this lounge on 04/26 at 9-11:30 PM as beginning of trip to SE Asia with Hubby. This is still one of my favorite lounges to use. Large seating area (unfortunately the outside area is too cold to use), good drink selection and decent salad buffet. There is a noodle bar in the back, and even though the food buffet only have limited selection most of the items are crowd pleasers (thai green curry, apple crumble etc.) and get replenished quickly. There was sparkling wine and several selection of both white and red wines available, a chilled counter for different types of juice (orange, apple, cranberry) and there is an espresso machine and soda fountain as well. Cleaning service make rounds but perhaps needs to be more frequent, since sometimes there are still dirty plates and glass on tables that make people confused whether they can use the seats or if the seats are still occupied.

Probably one of the worst Star Alliance lounges. The variety and quality of food is 2 out of 5, the service is even worse. There is no buffet and all food is displayed and you have to order a very limited number of dishes. The dishes are mostly low quality carbs (what they call pizza is a disgrace of an Italian pizza) and an extremely salty chicken dish which visually looks like vomit. There is almost none at the bar and you have to find a person to serve you. The coffee is decent. The variety and quality of drinks is well below average. During afternoon hours the lounge is exposed to the sun and there was no air-conditioning making the lounge very uncomfortable.
The Star Alliance Lounge was crowded, upper floor was closed, poor food and drink offerings, cheap Cremont Sparkling wine instead of Champagne, water dispenser not working, not recommended

The new Belama Club is located upstairs in the new International Departures Terminal at Honiara Airport in the Solomon Islands. It is located airside after going through passport control. It is primarily intended for Solomon Airlines Business Class and Belama Club members, but I was able to access it when flying on Qantas (Business/Platinum/Gold/Qantas Club). It is pleasantly airconditioned, with a view of the tarmac and the waiting planes, and it has meeting rooms and toilet facilities. It is a small lounge, but the demand on it is also fairly limited. There are plenty of drinks (alcoholic and non-alcoholic) self-serve from a refrigerator, and coffee is also available from a self-serve machine. The staff member on hand was polite and cheerful and helped me through the intricacies of the coffee machine. Food offerings are limited - some sandwiches and fruit, and packets of savoury snacks. If you want a substantial meal, you might need to use the cafe downstairs in the departures lounge. Decor is appropriate, and reflects the designs and decor of the Solomon Islands.

Sri Lankan Airline's business class lounge was a quiet place to relax for a couple of hours. At the entrance, I was welcomed by two receptionists attired in the airline's turquoise blue-green saris with peacock feather motifs. They informed me that there were no flight announcements, and had to be aware of the boarding times. Not a large luxurious venue like those of bigger airlines. However, it serves its purpose, with simple but comfortable seating, a small section for restaurant-style dining, and a quiet area for stretching out. Much of the hot food is Sri Lankan, as well as Western dishes and finger food. Alcoholic drinks can be requested at the bar, and although there was not a huge selection, the local Lion Larger beer was excellent. There are two shower rooms (I did not use one) and the toilets are very basic, and was disappointed by the lack of any toiletries. One side of the entire lounge has a view across the apron and a partial view of aircraft taking off. Unfortunately, my view was obscured by building works and maintenance. It never got crowded, and I did enjoy my time there.

My recent visit to the SWISS First Lounge at Gates E was a sublime prelude to my journey. I was welcomed into an atmosphere of calm elegance. The lounge offers a well-curated array of spaces. The seating options are abundant and comfortable, with plush armchairs that got panoramic views of the tarmac and distant Alps. A particular highlight was the dayroom. Outfitted with a remarkably soft bed and minimalist design, it provided the ideal sanctuary for rest.  The culinary offerings deserve special mention. From refined à la carte dishes to a buffet selection showcasing Swiss and international flavours, the menu is generous and sophisticated. The presentation was elegant, taste impeccable, and the service discreet yet attentive. Connectivity was seamless, with strong WiFi. That said, the initial login process required scanning one’s boarding pass and then entering a code online which was a minor inconvenience that could perhaps be streamlined. In sum, the SWISS First Lounge at Gates E is a serene enclave of refined comfort and thoughtful design.

Big lounge in the main terminal. Quite busy in early afternoon but still adequate seating. Hot food limited to cous-cous with veg and rice, which was disappointing but fairly good salad bar. Plenty and varied drink offering including draughty beer.

The lounge is very small and there were a lot of guests during our stay. There was a very good breakfast and the service was very courteous. There were no toilet facilities in the lounge. These were located outside and were shared with the other business lounges.

This lounge was incredible. The food was delicious (and had ordered options with cooking in front of you), including a nice slow-cooked chicken dish and many delicious puddings. There were unlimited drinks, tasty buffet food and a nice, comfortable seating area.  It was also clean. The wifi also worked well and was free. I have Lufthansa Frequent Traveller status and therefore had free access, but the price of purchase was CHF 49.00 which I would was was expensive for what it was, even if it was lovely especially because Zurich airport is quite nice.
The size of the lounge is too small, it is too crowded and seating possibilities are too often not given. Food is ok but missing air condition. ZRH AP needs to improve this lounge.

Nice design and a lot of space. 2 bedrooms with view to the runway, several shower rooms etc. and a lot of option to avoid other passengers. The lounge is located on the to floor of Terminal E with outdoor view, and has a huge terrace with view to the alps and the runway. Dining options and wine on offer are like in a gourmet restaurant. This time I just asked for a cheese plate and was not disappointed: beautifully arranged with a nice variety of Swiss hard and french soft cheese. The staff is friendly and knowledgable about food and wine. A truly First Class experience.

Return visit to this appalling "Business" lounge. Dirty, filthy carpets, chairs with armrests actually blackened with dirt, dirty seats. How on earth have you allowed your business lounge to be in such a disgraceful way. Dreadful choice of food. We left without eating a single thing. I am sure there is a serious hygiene issue here. Shame on you Swiss.

Redesigned and seems a bit smaller, but nice inside. Always a bit crowded but always 3 hot meals selection, plus cold dishes and good drink selections. Unless you want the quiet section (old longest bar area), nicer seats downstairs. Apart from the food offerings, go to the Alpine Lounge, but this lounge is a good if busy, product

Very poor lounge and more so as its a Swiss business lounge. A dreadful selection of foods and and equally poor selection of beverages. It is quite a soulless lounge with no atmosphere at all.  What did not add to the ambiance was the toddler who insisted, to the joy of her parents, to scream continually while we were there. This is not acceptable to the others in the lounge. Politely asking the father if he could perhaps take the child outside or ask her to stop was met with a very aggressive stance by him. I did not engage this man who looked a bit worse for wear.

Very nice lounge, much quieter than the normal Business Class Lounge. Great views of runway and a chef to cook you hot dishes. Good selection of drinks and very friendly staff. Only for Lufthansa Group Business Class & Senator etc., so more exclusive feel.

It is a beautiful lounge. There is ample food for breakfast however drinks are rather basic. The service was friendly on reception as in the lounge. Soft drinks are from dispensers. Still no newspapers or mags. Computers were not working decently . Very clean restrooms.

This is a lounge were you simply pay. It is a very dated place with old furniture. There were many drinks to chose from. However you still were not allowed to take the food yourself and I had the impression the people who were serving were instructed to give as less as possible. I had to insist to receive 2 slices of cheese. Service was far from friendly, not on the reception desks nor in the lounge. Cleanliness of the restrooms could be better.
Nicely designed, decent wine, food selection not great (but good Pao de quiejo) Not too crowded, there is varied types of seating.

They renovated their catering offer which is now much better than before. The lounge can get very crowded, even forming queues outside it but this time it was rather bellow average occupancy. Staff is now different too and much more courteous. Well done.

Horrible experience and way below average of what you expect of an airlines main or flagship lounge! The space is too small for the amount of people using it, food and beverage options are terrible, hot food on my visit was something looking like chicken breast but tasting like fish! Rice was full of sauce rests as people would just use any spoon to dig in. Not even at my school canteen I got such terrible food! Finally, space is so limited that passenger bags block passage. Toilets were also in a deplorable state. I would not recommend this lounge to any non-business class travellers paying their visit. Tap advertised this lounge recently as refurbished and better than before. My last visit to this lounge in 2019 was definitely better than today!

Outstanding lounge in Bangkok. Professional service as I booked the fast track departure which included assistance through immigration and access to this lounge. Nice selection of hot and bike foods as well as drinks. Free alcohol. Very clean space to relax with Wi-Fi. Staff were amazing and attentive. Assisted on round trip arrival also. I was out of the airport in 15 minutes.

Small lounge at KHH was primarily used to serve not only China Airlines', but also Skyteam's frequent flyers. Entrance was easy to navigate as it was right after the immigration. Staff was super friendly. Hot dishes were available, with acceptable quality.

I had no idea why Vietnam Airlines used this lounge as it was a pay-to-use one, meaning everyone could enter. Staff at check-in desk was inefficient slow. The lounge was super busy, crowded, and hard to find a seat. Food was limited in both quality and quantity with cold and tasteless dishes.

The lounge was located right after passing the immigration and KIX duty free area, on the 3rd floor. It looked quite new, modern, bright with many comfortable seats. Toilette was large and clean. WiFi was fast. Food and beverages were the downside, instead of being the star of the lounge. Empty trays were everywhere, and food quality was so-so, not as excellent as expected.

I liked how the lounge had been renovated to be brighter, modern and offered a warm welcome to the guests. Food and beverage selection was really good, with some hot dishes were available. WiFi was free and fast. Staff was nice, helpful and dedicated, even the lounge was so crowded since flight was delayed. One thing to be improved in the future: no toilet in the lounge.

The Miracle Lounge at Concourse F was one of the worst lounge ever! It was located on the 3rd floor without clear direction. The lounge was relatively small, with limited number of seat. Food and beverage was at average quality and quantity. No toilet in the lounge. And staff did not mind to help us find a seat. Bad experience, and have no idea why Vietnam Airlines keeps using this awful lounge!

Lotus Lounge was operated by Vietnam Airlines and dedicated to its VIP, Business Class, and Elite passengers, located on an upper floor of the international departure, close to the security screening. In overall, it was a nice and big lounge. We luckily got a table with a view to the tarmac and runway. WiFi was free and a bit slow though. Food selection and quality were good, particular the Vietnamese noodles at the hot station. However, cleanliness was something an issue here. Someone threw trash in the toilette and it was cleaned. Worse, we took a pair of "new" chopstick at the food bar, and found the leftover on them!

Took a chance to visit Vietnam Airlines Lotus Lounge 2 which was right next to Gate 18 before flying. It was relatively small with beautiful view to the tarmac and the gates where we could see planes taking off, landing, taxiing, parking. Seat was comfortable, and to us, quite elegant. WiFi was fast. Food selection, however, was quite limited with average quality. Staff was quite friendly though.

The lounge was not large but very new, elegant, clean and beautiful. It was located right next to the security (after security screening). Staff was friendly. Food was nice, with hot dish was available.

I went into the Lotus lounge. I was shocked to be honest for business class it was horrible. No arrangements of alcohol wine and poor canned beer that was it. No choice of wine either, just super sweet and it tasted old. The only food that seemed to be good was the fruit options. I tried to have a salad and found a big black hair in it. No salad dressings to be had just a piece of lime. I tried to have the chicken and way over cooked rice.  It is not worth the visit at all unless you drink like a child and love pop and juice and have no appreciation for a well made drink or even the lack of ability of making one because there is nothing to make one with. I asked for vodka and you would think I had three heads! I went downstairs and got a really cold tiger draft beer and some Pho it was delicious and I would rather pay and get something delicious and worth it rather than eat a drink what they serve for business class at the Lotus lounge domestic. Dreadful and not worth the effort of calling it a business class lounge! Very disappointing and dissatisfied. The should be ashamed. The bathrooms didn’t even have soap! I think they have something or someone that isn’t very well versed on what business class is or should be.

Paid to use this lounge when travelling with VietJet Air. Food options are ok. Comfort is ok. Only 2 beer varieties and not cold, no wine or spirits. By world standards not very VIP. Not really worth paying to come here.

Da Nang International (T2) is dominated by SE-Asian tourists and a lot number of small airlines. The Airport is renovated and a pleasure. The Lotus Lounge that Skyteam airlines use, is extremely nice and well maintained; it is a huge, unexpected gem find in a small airport. The Lounge has very good food offerings; cold delicatesses, and at least 7 hot meals in buffet. Drink options are a bit below average and only cheaper, local products (2 cheap wines and 4 beer brands, all alike) are offered. Background music appreciated. The décor is of high standard; even smoking and business rooms exist. The lounge appears underutilised, I found only 5-10 other visitors during the 3 hours I spent there.

Accessed this lounge based on Skyteam Elite Plus frequent flyer membership. Few type of sandwiches available, some yoghurts and soft drinks. Limited variety of alcoholic drinks. Couches not very comfortable, one can seat at table as well. iPhones cannot be charged at the charging station, but only with your charger connected to a power socket.

Huge lounge, average food and drinks, but extremely friendly staff. Though filled with people and being noisy and definitely not nicely set, quite enough seating options. Not the best I have seen, but ok for a short stay.

The lounge was luckily not very crowded. While the buffet and drinks were very limited, the staff ended up being very friendly and made me some vegetarian wraps as there were no savoury vegetarian snacks on the buffet. The coffee bar was efficient.

Unfortunately the lounge was very crowded, yet the upper floor remained closed. Food options were ok, as there were several vegetarian dishes/snacks available. Biggest draw back was the shower. It was dirty, no shower curtain, shower gel was empty, mirror broken. For a lounge this was a disgrace. Also lines for the customer service in the lounge were very long.

This lounge remains one of the best lounges I have visited. I last visited 4 years ago and the lounge has become very crowded. WiFi has become easier to connect to. No more getting a WiFi code. Instead one logs into Turkish Airlines WiFi, enters flight number and seat number, and voila you're connected to fast internet. As with my last visit in September 2022, the lounge has an open airy feel. Its food offerings are varied/excellent with various cooking stations throughout the lounge to satisfy one's palette. One definitely gets a taste of Turkish cuisine. The salad bar is extensive with a wide variety. We were not able to get the free massages to the neck and shoulders this time around, but, one can't go wrong with offering this type of service.

International business class passengers with Turkish Airlines have the choice of 2 separate lounges. The Turkish Airlines Business Class Lounge opposite Gate E1 is the primary location. The second option is the Turkish Airlines Miles & Smiles Lounge opposite Gate C1. Both occupy and area of 5,600 m2 and can accommodate 765 guests. To enter, you simply scan your boarding pass at one the turnstiles. Then you can stow your carry-on baggage in an all-glass locker and join the fray. There are street-style cooking stations where chefs serve hot pide breads stuffed with meats and cheeses and fresh pasta dishes or head for colossal salad bar where you’ll find a remarkable selection made from fresh produce. There’s the typical barista station, self-serve selection of local and French reds and whites as well as prosecco in golden bottles. Plus, there soft drinks, a water or beer available from open fridges. If that’s not convincing enough there are roving masseurs giving free 10-minute massages to weary travellers. If you haven’t got the time or patience to circle around in search for a seat, I recommend you head for the Miles & Smiles Lounge were there are usually much smaller numbers.

Big lounge but very crowded. We were lucky as a few minutes after we arrived the lounge was completely full. Food was good with various stations around with different cooked food options. We visited in the evening on our outbound leg and in the morning on the inbound. Big let-downs were the fact that there are no sodas available in the lounge. No Coke or Pepsi products at all and, when I went to ask about a shower, the wait time was three hours! Seating very hit and miss due to the crowding. Nice touch are the lockers you can use for bag storage.

The lounge at Istanbul's old airport was phenomenal, so the expectations at the new airport were high not even close - no place to practice golf swings, no toy race tracks for the kids, no huge display of desserts from Do and Co Vienna, no chandeliers in the rest rooms, and only 6 stalls in the ladies' room, causing the inevitable queues food counters with onsite chefs were still good but what a disappointment overall! (also a bit hard to find even with wayfinder in the Turkish Airlines app - it's upstairs but how to get up there? eventually we found the entrance for disabled passengers and the man there was kind enough to let us in)

This is an overcrowded mess. I pass through that lounge 4 times a month and now I really feel like commenting. Before you go upstairs you have some rude staff who easily greet you with "where are you going". No excuse me Can I help you ! This happened many times to me. After you have passed these staff you go upstairs to the lounge where you enter with your boarding pass. So really why do you have people downstairs ? Once inside, doesn't matter the hours, I was in a refectory atmosphere and not a lounge. It is overcrowded with not enough seating. It is loud and no quiet area at your service. Although, THY thought of all amenities to make the stopovers as comfortable as possible, many of those are not used and just occupy space. I am an Elite plus card holder and qualify for that many times within one year There is no extra area dedicated to them. The food stations although impressive are busy with preparing food instead of serving. The cooks are overwhelmed by the amount of passengers annd are doing their best to keep up. The food buffet for cold dishes is always well stocked and no problem to serve yourself. In the last visit I left. There was no space. At 5:50 am. It is for me ungraspable how a lounge at such a big airport has to be in the middle overlooking shopping areas and not have a view to the tarmac. This could have been easily one of the best lounges in the world. Instead people rate it as excellent merely on the food options available if available. This is not a lounge where you feel or experience some sort of privilege.

The lounge that I went to on my recent flight with Air Serbia was very good. There were 2 lounges available for Air Serbia flights: the Turkish Airlines lounge and the ProPass lounge. The views and the drink options were both magnificent, but the food, well not so much. There weren’t many choices and the choices provided didn’t look fresh. The staff were nice, but the lounge was a bit noisy. The mini chocolate muffins were amazing, a must try! The toilets were very clean and had a pleasant odour. It also was a bit crowded and there was limited seating, but the seats were amazingly comfortable! The WiFi was great too! (Also I don’t know if there were showers!) In conclusion, this lounge is great and I would recommend it!

While the Turkish Airlines business class lounge highlights private rooms as a premium feature, the actual experience is anything but premium. The showers follow a reasonable queue system, but the private rooms are an elusive and undignified ordeal. Despite being advertised as part of the business class offering, they seem more like a marketing ploy. There’s no queue system in place for these rooms. Instead, passengers are expected to pop in and out, begging for availability. The staff, with stiff body language, offer vague and inconsistent time estimates—anywhere from 25 minutes to over an hour. To make matters worse, there’s no time limit for how long guests can occupy the rooms, leaving others in a constant state of uncertainty and frustration. This process leaves passengers feeling more like beggars than valued patrons. Turkish Airlines should either implement a proper queue system or charge a fee to ensure a fair and transparent process. The current setup is nothing short of undignified and far from the business class experience one would expect. I finally got my room after 3 hours of waiting in uncertainty, and it should not be like this.

This is a very busy lounge with Priority Pass members being put on a waiting list for approximately 45 minutes. Seating was scarce on the first floor. The food quality is excellent. The lounge had a nice selection of Mediterranean cuisine e.g. kefta kabob with tomatoes and aubergine, grilled creamy chicken, assortment of cheese and crackers, hummus and Turkish Tea. WiFi worked flawlessly. There were lines for the bathroom given the number of passengers in the lounge. Nonetheless, the bathrooms were clean.

I travel business class internationally due to poor health conditions and advanced age. I have heart disease and cannot walk very far, and my wife has nerve damage and also cannot walk long distances. We both require wheelchairs. We arrived to IST on February 7th, at 2:43 pm, from Toronto. We had a 7-hour long layover in Istanbul, before our flight TK708 departed for Karachi, Pakistan, at 9:55 pm. Because of the long connection, we tried to reserve a nap room and specifically chose IST for this purpose. My wife was unable to sleep on the 9 hour flight from Canada and was exhausted. A young lady at the concierge desk provided unprofessional and rude responses to us when we asked her for a nap room. She first said there were none and to come back every 30 minutes to check. My wife walked back and forth (with great difficulty) from distant seating areas over the course of 2 hours, every 30 minutes, because I cannot walk very far. The young lady at the concierge desk did not have the courtesy to take our phone number or to put our names as next in line. After 2 hours, we tried again (the 4th time), and a younger man quickly walked ahead of us to the desk. The concierge desk then gave the next available nap room to this young man, who only showed up the first time to the desk, instead of my wife and I, after we were waiting for 2 hours and had been to the desk 4 times. We pleaded with the young lady at the concierge desk, asking why she gave the room to the other man. The concierge simply said "he came to the desk faster than you". For 7 hours we were unable to rest and sat in regular seats in the lounge, waiting for our connecting flight. This has been the worst business class experience I have ever faced in my life.

I miss the old TK lounge at Ataturk airport. This lounge is always packed. And the food variety and quality goes downhill every time I’m here. And now, with Turkish (or Turkiye) boycotting US products, there are not only no Coke products, but no soda of any kind. Sorry. I’m headed into the terminal. Worthless to sit in the crowded lounge and you can’t even get a Coke. Turkish has really dropped its game in their lounges.

We definitely received very good service. They provided every service in the best possible way. The food is very delicious, the seating areas are comfortable and wide, and there are many activation systems to pass the time. So you will lose track of time while waiting for the transfer.

Exclusive Turkish airlines lounge, huge space, different rooms to relax, big variety of food and drinks, local sweets. There is also a piano, sometimes they play it. Easy to spend a few hours here. Free Wi-Fi

I had on other trips been in their excellent business class lounge and flying this time in economy but being in possession of a Star Alliance Gold Status I had been granted entrance in this CIP Lounge.  I read it is inferior to the Business Lounge but besides just a couple of food stations less, I must see I truly am impressed: excellent food and drink selection, lovely atmosphere, simply a great place to be and spend some time.

I heard that this lounge was opened to give passengers who paid for a business class ticket a slightly more exclusive experience by leaving out status customers and thus making the lounge less crowded. This has not worked. The TK lounge at Ataturk airport used to be really fantastic and special and it was one of the reasons I booked with TK all the time. This time seems to have passed. I am just sitting in the TK Business lounge at Istanbul new airport, feeling like waiting in an overcrowded train station. This feels more like a free fast food restaurant or an all-you-can-eat holiday venue, than an exclusive space to relax and wait for the next flight. Virtually all seats are occupied, mainly by bags and coats to reserve a seat for people who seem to be wandering around. People are shoveling piles of food onto their plates and leave the tables completely covered with leftovers and rubbish. Even the supposedly quiet areas are overcrowded. Having been in the fantastic Qatar Airways Business lounge at Doha airport, this is the complete opposite… crammed, crowded and ordinary.

Using this lounge on a SWISS flight. The place is simply horrible. There are plenty of alcoholic drinks especially whisky, served by a bartender - the food is terrible and extremely poor. There was a very salty soup, a lot of vegetables and bread with tuna salad. Some small kind of a saucer with limited food like pieces of cheese with one grape, pineapple, melon and berry. Another 3 cubes of chocolate cake. The soft drinks in the fridge were lukewarm, in a basket some melting ice. I left the lounge and went to an eatery to have a decent sandwich. Maybe this lounge is Ok if you want to drink alcohol but not for a decent snack at all. The restrooms were not very clean.
After all the hype I was expecting something above average. What a let down, seating in the food area was very poor, no bar, and incredibly complicated internet access.

Transited twice through this outstanding and impressive lounge. As with my last visit in May 2022, the lounge has an open airy feel. Its food offerings are varied/excellent with various cooking stations throughout the lounger to satisfy one's palette. One definitely gets a taste of Turkish cuisine. The salad bar is extensive with a wide variety as is the tea bar with its variety of teas. On both visits we were able to get free massages to the neck and shoulders. Can't go wrong with this type of service. WiFi connection was excellent. Bathrooms are very clean and maintained by attendants.

I was looking forward to visiting this lounge because I had heard so much about it. Well, maybe the food is ok but not for Vegans. Even the lentil soup and white rice had butter, nothing for Vegans but a bowl of green salad. Next time I can arrive at the airport a bit later and have food outside - complete disappointment.

Turkish Airlines' flagship business class lounge is outstanding and impressive. The lounge is on an open-level overlooking the main part of the terminal. There is plenty of seating and space. The seating is very comfortable. The lounge is immaculate and its food offerings are superb featuring freshly cooked food at various cooking stations throughout the lounge ranging from grilled foods, pasta and baked cheese, spinach and meat pies, cheeses/olives, salads and desserts. One definitely gets a taste of Turkish cuisine here including Simit (sesame seed bagel) and coffee/tea. The latter can be served in glass cups you get in Turkish restaurants. There are quieter darker seating areas akin to seating in a library like area. There is a room with 12 TV screens to catch up to the news. The lounge also features virtual golf and a holographic flight experience. The bathrooms are very clean and maintained by attendants. Our flight was at 2 pm so all the cooking stations were manned and food aplenty. Depending on the food station there were some queues. The staff kept the tables clean removing used dishes/utensils promptly. WiFi worked just fine; however, you had to scan boarding pass to get WiFi password.

What a great lounge! From the freshly cooked dishes ranging from typical Turkish kebabs through Moussaka, Chinese spicy chicken stir fry and pasta stations you could see all those being prepared. In addition various meze options and a few sweets including an array of the ubiquitous baklava variants. Drinks stations (DIY) were dotted around. One nice feature was the lockers in which you can leave your bags, using a combination of your choosing. There is a golf simulator and other adult toys including a Scalextric track! Comfortable seating in a variety of types and a quiet atmosphere.

The only hot food was toast. Other than that, it was pre-packaged rubbish.  The coffee was weak, stale and tepid. There was no draught beer, only tiny cans. It is probably the worst airport lounge of any big city in the world and a national embarrassment. The WIFI involves fiddly codes that you must obtain from machines.

My inbound flight was 09h30 min, and my outbound was 06h30 and in between a layover of 14h. I was denied a sleeping room while it was given to passengers between 04 and 09h layover. So, I spent the whole 14h in the lounge, couldn’t get near nor shower.

United Club in Terminal E is deceptively small but has plenty of seating. Given our early morning departure, the lounge was a bit crowded; however, the crowd dissipates as early flights took off. The usual food options were available - one could choose from 2 hot entrees, sandwiches, various salads, a charcuterie board and cookies/brownies. There are electrical outlets at every seat and USB ports but not USB-C. WiFi was very easy to connect to and very fast. Restrooms were very clean. WiFi was easy to log in and fast. This lounge has large windows overlooking the tarmac.

This review is limited to United Club in Terminal E. Its a huge and very busy lounge; however, it became less crowded as early evening flights departed. Surprisingly, there was only one hot entree available (Caribbean Jerk Pork). This meant that Muslims/Jews who do not consume pork were unable to have a hot entree. There were the usual offerings available - Soup (garden vegetable), cheese board, sandwiches and 3 types of salad. WiFi was fast and easy to connect to. Restroom were very clean.

This lounge was surprisingly not very busy 2 days before Christmas. It was not crowded at all. Good view of runways and tarmac from the floor to ceiling windows. For food, one could choose from 2 hot entrees, sandwiches, various salads, a charcuterie board and cookies/brownies. The lounge no longer has a soft drinks machine, one has to go to the bar to request a soft drink. There are electrical outlets at every seat and USB ports but not USB-C. WiFi was very easy to connect to and very fast. Restrooms were very clean.

Limited selection of hot food in the morning. (Scrambled eggs, breakfast sausage grounds). Cheap danish. Yogurt and fruit. Breakfast options were either empty or just sad remains of eggs for at least 15 minutes before they were refilled. Coffee machine option was limited. Overall, a cheap low tier experience typical of domestic US airlines.

On the whole a sub-par lounge and even a dangerous one in one instance. Large and impersonal. Arrived after a red-eye flight with a long layover ahead. Used one of their quiet areas. There are very few, and I was warned that if things got busy, my stay would be limited to 45 minutes. I was lucky and that didn't happen, but overall the experience provided little privacy, and I felt like in was in a dentist's office with lower lighting. Shower was good. Long walk to get food - main dining area was full and noisy. If there was sit-down service, it was well hidden. Salads were pretty good. Hot food was another story. The chicken I had was raw in the middle, which is completely unacceptable. Fortunately, I detected it before I ate any. I quietly let an employee know, and it was removed from the buffet. Drinks poor. The flavored waters had no flavor at all. Given the price of a United business class ticket, I think the overall experience could be much better.

This is the best lounge I have been to. United has a great lounge, with tons of food options for lunch and dinner, and very good desserts. During the time we went to the lounge, it was dinner time. Options they had that day for dinner were pasta salad, chicken and rice, corned beef, and a chicken sandwich. For dessert, they had cookies and brownies that day. They have lots of drinks including beer, soda, wine, and much more. You can get this once a year if you have a United Explorer MileagePlus Card, which is only $99 a year! This is also available with First and Business Class.

A perfect lounge with good food options, excellent bar service with lovely cocktails, wine and champagne. Very dedicated team, throughout whole lounge. Was really impressed. Entrance entitlement because of Star Alliance business class ticket.
Rude, surly lounge staff who didn’t smile. We were made to feel like a burden. Any semblance of comfort is offset by the attitude of the staff. Avoid this mess.

This lounge was very busy with late afternoon departures. Nonetheless, there was plenty of seating available. The usual food options were available - cold and hot plates. I passed on the hot plate of grilled citrus cream chicken and opted for the Asian chicken salad and corned beef baguette. The attendants replenished the food offerings on a regular basis. WiFi was easy to log in and fast. This lounge has large windows overlooking the tarmac. The only blemish was that the bathrooms had an unpleasant odor and could have been cleaner and fresh smelling.

Visited the Polaris Lounge at Terminal C, Newark before flight back to London. It is bright, modern, clean and offers a lot of seating options - it was quiet in this early morning period. The food and beverages were okay, although hot food standards were "canteen" like and lacked any proper choice, dried out and flavours were poor. Staff at Reception were the usual United Airlines standard - gruff and unfriendly, and certainly never meeting their statements about flying the friendly skies! Lounge waiting staff were nice and helpful. A step up from older United lounges, but why can they not get staff who try to be more friendly or hospitable, since this is an ongoing weakness for United Airlines?

This United Club lounge is deceivingly spacious. For an early morning departure the lounge was not busy. There is the usual staple of food and drink of breakfast items (cereals, pastries, oatmeal, tea, coffee etc plus a hot of scrambled eggs and breakfast potatoes). I could not eat the latter as they mixed sausage with the breakfast potatoes. Staff was very friendly and the bathrooms very clean. Wi-Fi connectivity was excellent.

The lounge was bright, fresh and comfortable. There was a wide range of food (evening) and drink choices and staff regularly clearing tables. The bar was a nice large bar with a huge variety of drinks available. I'm not aware of any showers available but the toilets were spotless. There were a variety of seating, lounge and outdoor areas available.

The SFO United Polaris Lounge was very disappointing. I frequently fly long haul flights to Asia out of San Francisco and have used the Polaris Lounge many times. Usually the food selection is excellent, this time not. Arriving shortly after 8PM, the sit down restaurant was already closed, even though the lounge is open for another couple of hours. The food selection in the buffet section was dismal; salad looked wilted and not appealing, a tray of two different sandwiches, four hot dishes, some assorted cheeses/meats, no French bread or rolls to be seen, just a few crackers and a tray of two dessert squares. The secondary food section in the quite zone was also closed. The best way to describe the food experience was "Cheap". Because of my United flight status I was able to switch to the United Club in the main terminal. Night and day difference, better food, wider selection, offerings such as candy and other assorted sweets. The Polaris Lounge at SFO used to be the Premium place to relax before a flight - not any more.
Unacceptable opening hours (from like 9am to 4:30 or 5:30pm). Only option for Star Alliance Gold members at Mexico City Airport meaning no option. Never again.

Due to the flight disruptions, this lounge was very busy throughout our stay in the lounge. This is a huge lounge and we were able to find seating.
