There is natural light flowing in from the large windows. The added bonus of the window seats is plane spotting especially the foreign carriers taking off and landing. There are power ports for AC and USB at every seat. The selection of food and drink was decent with a buffet set up which included a hot plate (korean style bbq chicken), soup, salad bar, sandwiches/wraps and the regular fare of nuts, cold cuts, cheese, fruit, coffee and sodas. The attendants kept refilling the buffet hot plate and sandwiches/wraps. The bathrooms are very clean and maintained by attendants every 5-10 minutes. Wi-Fi connectivity was excellent.

This United Club was quite busy during the post early morning travel period. Nonetheless, there was enough seating available with natural light and views of the tarmac. There was a parse selection of food and drink. An employee rudely told me they were out of scrambled eggs. The remainder of the offerings were nothing I liked (porridge, biscuits, cheeses and cold cuts plus the regular fare of nuts, cheese, fruit, coffee and sodas. The lounge is comfortable with clean bathrooms and a very friendly staff. An agent put us on a standby flight from SFO-YVR when the agent at check-in would not do so. Wi-Fi connectivity was excellent.
Going to stop flying United. Can't even access the club with passes due to "overcrowding". Selling too many club accesses when you don't have capacity.

Visited this lounge 04/26 between 3:30 to 5:30 PM with Hubby on the way to LAX then SE Asia. We usually go to the larger lounge at Terminal "E" but since our flight leave from gate C1 right next door, we decided to use this lounge. The lounge is smaller than the "E" but still have good amount of seating. Regular buffet offering from UA and there is a bar with very friendly bartender. Cleaners were very proactive, there's hardly any dirty plates or cups on any tables. All employees in this club seems to be very competent and works hard. I will not hesitate to use this club again in the future if my flight leaves from Terminal "C".

This lounge was very busy during peak afternoon travel period and then the crowd dissipated until the beginning of the peak evening travel period.. There is plenty of seating available with natural light flowing in from the large windows. The window seats are a great place for plane spotting especially the foreign carriers taking off and landing. There are power ports for AC and USB at every seat. Opposite the bar area, there is a table and chairs that the stretches the length of the lounger. There was a decent selection of food and drink. A buffet set up included a hot plate (taqueria), soup, salad bar, sandwiches/wraps and the regular fare of nuts, cold cuts, cheese, fruit, coffee and sodas. The attendants kept refilling the buffet hot plate and sandwiches/wraps. The bathrooms are very clean and maintained by attendants every 5-10 minutes. Wi-Fi connectivity was excellent.

Surprisingly, the United Club was not very busy during the peak evening travel period. There was plenty of seating available with natural light and views of the tarmac. There was a decent selection of food and drink. A buffet set up included a hot plate (a pasta dish), soup, salad bar and the regular fare of nuts, cheese, fruit, coffee and sodas. The lounge is comfortable with clean bathrooms and a very friendly staff. Wi-Fi connectivity was excellent.

British Airways passengers flying to LHR are entitled to use the lounge which is located where the D and E concourses converge. It is not obvious. The lounge is small but well equipped with a short menu of snacks and light meals and a bar (with a $5 charge for premium beers and wines). State laws forbid the sale of spirits. Friendly and helpful staff. For spotters there's a great view of the runway

The United Club at DFW has large windows with great views of the tarmac/apron. The windows also help bring a lot of natural light into the lounge. The lounge looks small but there is a lot of space. Seating is comfortable The food offerings are rather sparse. Ham/cheese sliders, potato salad, soup and snacks. There is a nice bar area. Bathrooms were very clean and the receptionist very friendly. WiFi has a very strong signal.

This is a bright and airy lounge with views of the tarmac/taxiways. There is plenty of seating. Unlike the United Club, food offerings is a significant upgrade. The buffet has 3-5 entree choices in addition to the United Club fare of cold cuts and snacks. There is a huge L shaped bar in the middle with plenty of seating. WiFi easy to connect and very good signal.

United Club lounge, Terminal 1, next to  departure gate, gate B17. One word: awful. Overcrowded, poor food offerings, tattered chairs, dirty bathrooms and loud staff chattering to each other in the lounge in Spanish. However, all the staff I encountered were very pleasant, from the ones at the front desk when you check in to the staff at the disastrous buffet to the ones who clear up the dishes. They went out of their way to make some small talk and to wish passengers. The Wifi was good but that's all. The ambience was just uncomfortable, not an oasis of calm or comfort. The only bit of hot food for breakfast was an awful sausage sandwich in a 'biscuit' with cheese dripping out all over the wrapping. I would have been better off in McDonald's.

Visited United Club SFO Terminal 3 with hubby on our way to Hawaii on Thursday 02/10/22 morning at 11:45 AM. The Agents at the front desk who checked our boarding passes were very helpful and give us information on how to verify our Vaccination status for our flights to Hawaii. They gave us a card with QR code that link to United's help services and the person at the service desk communicate with us through text to get our particulars and used it to verify our vaccination status in Hawaii's Safe Travels website. When we got the verification, the gate agents then give us United wristbands that enable us to bypass the vaccination verification process when we land in Honolulu. It saved us quite a lot of time and we can go directly to the baggage claim.

Food is terrible. All water dispensers are empty. Nothing available except nasty sandwiches. This lounge has really taken a nose dive in the last few months. It’s time for members to start speaking up and not tolerating this horrible service. Have a sandwich and an orange. It’s so nasty. A COVID cesspool, but let’s keep up impressions and wear our masks, even though we don’t clean anything!

This is a very ordinary United Club with the standard soup, salad, and sandwiches offered for food. There is an attended bar offering free drinks with house liquor, including prosecco. There is, however, one exceptional feature that propels this club to the front of the line - an outdoor patio with comfortable furniture and perfect views of arrivals and departures. There was also a great variety of indoor seating so that the club never seemed crowded. There were a sufficient number of attendants so that tables were kept cleared, and the whole lounge remained clean and orderly, I certainly plan on returning here whenever the opportunity presents.
I went to the Orlando, FL United club; I've been in many airline clubs and I've never been to one so bad. It was small, over crowded, and very little food selections. It was very disappointing.

The lounge was dirty, dated, and seriously needed to expand and makes lots of more space for those travelling with families. The Phuket Airport was awful and seriously needed renovations and to improve its cleanliness and to provide a nice and quiet and also clean environment.
I understand that Thai has gone thru some difficult times, but the lounges are old, food is awful, surely it can't be too hard to provide something edible? The staff are very polite.

I was in transit from Phnom Penh to Udon Thani and spent 2 hours in the Domestic Lounge at Suvarnabhumi, I have not spent any time in this lounge since just prior to COVID and I thought as I was traveling on Thai Smile, I would be refused entry, but I was not. It was explained as I  boarded a Thai Smile flight in Phnom Penh I was eligible to use the lounge. Thus, if travel on Thai Smile commences with an international flight so long as one holds a Thai Royal Orchid Plus Gold Card one can use the lounge. It was fairly quiet, but the food was excellent or at least compared to the business class lounge in the airport at Phnom Penh. There was no alcohol available, but I recall pre-COVID there was only beer anyway, strangely enough the experience was great but perhaps I detected a sense of normalcy post-COVID. I also fly Bangkok Airways, which is very good, and they have lounges all can access irrespective of the fare one pays.

I visited this lounge twice, once in the evening and once in the early morning. The rush of flights leaving in the evening meant that the lounge was very crowded. However, we did find seats in a corner together. The lounge decor is very green and bright. There are a variety of seating options - but no napping chairs. There are an abundance of power outlets, and the seats were laid out in such a way that you can have some food relatively easily. The food in this lounge is a highlight. There are two buffets - a halal section and the main section. The main section had a large salad bar, a variety of sweet and savoury pastries, and hot food on offer, as well as pad krapao - stir fried chicken with basil made to order. The halal section had mostly Indian food - butter chicken and samosas. There are two bars, and you could get cocktails from either of them. I used the shower facilities here, and the showers are relatively simple, a rain shower suite, toilet, seat and sink. I did however, have to call the lounge in advance to ask about the shower facilities since the website showed that they were still not open due to social distancing, but the receptionist told me that it was just opened a week before my flight. In the morning the food on offer was also pretty good.  This lounge is a good one, even though I could've used the EVA Air lounge which was closer to my gate on my second visit - I chose the long walk to this lounge because it was  better. Thai used to be quite poor in terms of lounges, but their new offerings put them on par with EVA Air and  ahead of Lufthansa and United. If the royal orchid lounge is too crowded, the royal silk lounge next door, with slightly less brash, colourful decor still has the same food offerings and is usually a lot less crowded, and you are allowed to walk between the two lounges in case you would like a cocktail from the prestige lounge's bar.

We had a Thai Airways flight operated by Thai smile. The lounge staff do not recognize Star Alliance gold membership in this case. Also, their machines could not read my priority pass card. So they just rejected us. Even speaking to a manager did not help. It is unacceptable that Thai Airways does not honor Star Alliance gold of other members on their flights if those are operated by other airlines and reject clients if their systems do not work.

I visited the Thai Royal Silk Lounge at Bangkok airport, as well as the Thai Royal Orchid Lounge at Chiang Mai, both of which were enjoyable stays. These domestic departure lounges I found quite relaxing places to spend an hour or so, and have a bite and a drink before a short flight. What impressed me was how large and beautifully designed the lounges were - some of the decor reflecting the Thai Airways colours. There was plenty of spacious seating, some brightly lit, as well cosy areas if you wanted to do some work or have a little privacy. No alcohol is served, which was not an issue anyway. And there were no views of the apron on runway. Both lounges had a good selection of hot and cold food, snacks, salads, and plenty of soft drinks, tea and coffee. Even though I was not quite hungry, I couldn't resist the Thai Chicken Curry, and steaming hot Chinese Dim Sum. There was also a smaller selection of western finger food, salads, pies and cakes - green tea cake was delicious! The washrooms were clean and well maintained. Neither of the lounges was crowded, and the staff were attentive at quickly clearing up tables. They were also happy to explain some of the food items on display, inviting me to try them out. Considering these are used in domestic flights, I was surprised how nice they were and certainly better than a few international departure lounges I have been to.

We flied business class on Thai Airways to Stockholm and were able to use business lounge at Bangkok Suvarnbhumi airport. The lounge location is quite good only one floor next from immigration service. The lounge is quite large and comfortable. The foods and drinks are quite good with many choices. The staff are quite polite and friendly.

We visited Thai Airways Lounge at Chiangmai International Airport using Priority Pass Member. The lounge is not so large but the staff are very friendly. Although there was not much food and beverage to choose, the atmosphere is quite good and comfortable. Nice lounge to visit and enjoy your waiting time before flight.

Small, but not crowded. limited buffet with only one hot dish and another cold noodle-dish. There are 6 staff here, even though there are only a couple guests. They are watching us, and it makes me very uncomfortable. They are just standing outside the ONE washroom waiting for you to be done in there. Also at the mini-buffet they are trying to pick the food for you and staring at every move. It is so exhausting and not at all relaxing as a lounge should be. the screen with flight-status. is not at all updated. the flight is delayed, but it does not say how much. the new boarding time is not possible to get even when asking the staff. The seats are comfortable, but the tables are super low, and makes it hard to work while I wait for the flight. The lounge is noisy. The staff has good English and are helpful (in their Benagli way) There is an espresso machine but the coffee is not the best quality. the price for the lounge access is less than 1000 taka.

My husband wanted to surprise me with business class tickets to Cancun for our 30th anniversary & my 50th birthday. We we arrived at the airport for our 6 hour layover we tried to get into the lounge at 2:00am so we could rest and freshen up, but they wouldn’t allow WestJet business class in since they were closing at 3am and reopening at 6:00am. We paid a lot extra for business class but got no value from it. West Jest has screwed us almost every time we have flown with them. 0 value for our dollar. Beyond frustrating, especially when we are exhausted and were told when buying these tickets the lounge is included.

Dreadful, dated, filthy lounge. Poor, uncomfortable sagging seating. Areas under semi-permanent repair. Broken, stained table lamps. Bad food. Try to avoid passing through Shanghai Pudong airport if at all possible.

I’ve used this Primus Lounge a couple of times now. It’s very small and can get crowded. Only water and hot drinks and only a couple of choices of hot food. No snacks are available. Not one to write home about
A relatively quiet lounge meant I had a choice of seating. Food was plentiful with several hot options. Has its own wifi. Overall one of the better lounges I have visited in India

Busy, as a lot of Indian lounges can be, however there was sufficient seating inside. A good choice of food, with 3 or 4 hot dishes to choose from. Not much in the snack depart, just some sandwiches. Non alcoholic Drinks are free, but alcoholic ones you have to pay for. No Wi-Fi though

Very small lounge but good selection of sandwiches and snacks. Hot soup provided. Small bar with good selection of drinks. Edward provided friendly and efficient service. Surprised there was only one male toilet facility. The lounge only opens 3 hours before departure.

Excellent small lounge opposite gate A32. Two levels with views of aircraft taking off and landing. Friendly and efficient staff. A good choice of beverages - alcoholic and soft. A small food menu with a range of microwaved dishes. We had Chicken Tikka Masala which was OK and an excellent Apple Crisp.

This was quite possibly the worst Business Class Lounge we have ever visited! There was a poor choice of food, which was continually running out and not being replenished. Likewise the availability of clean plates was continually running out and when pointed out to the staff, they brought out just 1 plate! The tables were rarely cleared or wiped down properly, resulting in almost every one overflowing with dirty cutlery/glasses and plates that were simply left for over 2 hours in most cases. The staff were very few and those who were there, extremely rude. The restrooms were of inadequate number and quality. We could not find any USB sockets to plug our phones into either. I simply can not imagine why Virgin Atlantic choose to associate themselves with this company and lounge as it does not reflect well on them at all. I would avoid this lounge at all costs!

This lounge was very disappointing for the simple reason that there were no bathrooms within the lounge. One has to use the bathrooms in the terminal. Why pay for membership to use a lounge when one of the basic amenities (bathrooms) are not available. Notwithstanding the above, the facilities were clean and the lounge had the usual hot and cold food choices plus beverages (soft drinks, water etc.) available with Turkish breakfast items available (olives, cucumbers, tomatoes and various cheeses). If I had known that this lounge had no internal bathrooms, I wouldn't have wasted $$ to enter the lounge.

This is one of the best non airline lounges. The lounge is very spacious. The lobby is very welcoming. The long hallways stretch the length of the lounge reflect the Islamic and Omani architecture. There is plenty of seating. There is a main food station plus 2 others at either end. Given our early morning departure, the buffets had breakfast items (both western and Arabic), cut and whole fresh fruit, salad bar, pastries and assorted breads. The main food station has a live cooking area where one can order eggs/omelets any style. I did not use WiFi so I can comment on connectivity. Restrooms were very clean and seating was very comfortable.

This is a small lounge. The food quality is good. The portions are tapas sized which can be ordered from the menu by scanning QR code on the tables. The lounge had a variety of alcoholic and non-alcoholic beverages available. Service staff was very polite and friendly. WiFi was very easy to connect too and very fast with plenty of outlets to charge phones. The only drawback to this lounge is that the bathrooms were out of order on this visit meaning guests had to use the facilities in the terminal.

This lounge is small and very crowded for an early morning flight. There was a dearth of sitting options. From what I observed, the food/beverage service was very limited. Worst of all, there is only one bathroom in the Lounge. I chose to leave the Club and use the facilities in the airport and waited for my flight at the gate. We were able to use this lounge because of our business class tickets. It seems this is the only lounge available in Terminal 3 so there is no choice but to use it.

The Club at CLT is a welcome addition to this airport for those who are not AA's Admiral Club members. I was pleasantly surprised with this small Priority Pass lounge. The staff is very friendly. Unlike most clubs with a buffet selection, this Club offers an automated albeit limited menu. Scan the QR code and order. Unfortunately, due to the lateness of the day, the Club ran out of the entrée I ordered. Nonetheless, this lounge was well worth the long walk from Concourse B. Bathrooms were clean and the WiFi had a strong signal.

This Swissport lounge is pathetic. The only nice thing about this lounge was the gentleman receptionist and the hot chocolate. The seating is basically nothing more than a barebones seating area. Snacks, soft drinks and a few alcohol offering are the extent of its food/beverage service. We were able to use this lounge because of our business class tickets. However, I certainly wouldn't pay to use this facility. It would be throwing money away. WiFi worked but I felt it was spotty.

This lounge remains one of the best lounges I have visited. I last visited 4 years ago and the lounge has become very crowded. WiFi has become easier to connect to. No more getting a WiFi code. Instead one logs into Turkish Airlines WiFi, enters flight number and seat number, and voila you're connected to fast internet. As with my last visit in September 2022, the lounge has an open airy feel. Its food offerings are varied/excellent with various cooking stations throughout the lounge to satisfy one's palette. One definitely gets a taste of Turkish cuisine. The salad bar is extensive with a wide variety. We were not able to get the free massages to the neck and shoulders this time around, but, one can't go wrong with offering this type of service.

International business class passengers with Turkish Airlines have the choice of 2 separate lounges. The Turkish Airlines Business Class Lounge opposite Gate E1 is the primary location. The second option is the Turkish Airlines Miles & Smiles Lounge opposite Gate C1. Both occupy and area of 5,600 m2 and can accommodate 765 guests. To enter, you simply scan your boarding pass at one the turnstiles. Then you can stow your carry-on baggage in an all-glass locker and join the fray. There are street-style cooking stations where chefs serve hot pide breads stuffed with meats and cheeses and fresh pasta dishes or head for colossal salad bar where you’ll find a remarkable selection made from fresh produce. There’s the typical barista station, self-serve selection of local and French reds and whites as well as prosecco in golden bottles. Plus, there soft drinks, a water or beer available from open fridges. If that’s not convincing enough there are roving masseurs giving free 10-minute massages to weary travellers. If you haven’t got the time or patience to circle around in search for a seat, I recommend you head for the Miles & Smiles Lounge were there are usually much smaller numbers.

Big lounge but very crowded. We were lucky as a few minutes after we arrived the lounge was completely full. Food was good with various stations around with different cooked food options. We visited in the evening on our outbound leg and in the morning on the inbound. Big let-downs were the fact that there are no sodas available in the lounge. No Coke or Pepsi products at all and, when I went to ask about a shower, the wait time was three hours! Seating very hit and miss due to the crowding. Nice touch are the lockers you can use for bag storage.

The lounge at Istanbul's old airport was phenomenal, so the expectations at the new airport were high not even close - no place to practice golf swings, no toy race tracks for the kids, no huge display of desserts from Do and Co Vienna, no chandeliers in the rest rooms, and only 6 stalls in the ladies' room, causing the inevitable queues food counters with onsite chefs were still good but what a disappointment overall! (also a bit hard to find even with wayfinder in the Turkish Airlines app - it's upstairs but how to get up there? eventually we found the entrance for disabled passengers and the man there was kind enough to let us in)

This is an overcrowded mess. I pass through that lounge 4 times a month and now I really feel like commenting. Before you go upstairs you have some rude staff who easily greet you with "where are you going". No excuse me Can I help you ! This happened many times to me. After you have passed these staff you go upstairs to the lounge where you enter with your boarding pass. So really why do you have people downstairs ? Once inside, doesn't matter the hours, I was in a refectory atmosphere and not a lounge. It is overcrowded with not enough seating. It is loud and no quiet area at your service. Although, THY thought of all amenities to make the stopovers as comfortable as possible, many of those are not used and just occupy space. I am an Elite plus card holder and qualify for that many times within one year There is no extra area dedicated to them. The food stations although impressive are busy with preparing food instead of serving. The cooks are overwhelmed by the amount of passengers annd are doing their best to keep up. The food buffet for cold dishes is always well stocked and no problem to serve yourself. In the last visit I left. There was no space. At 5:50 am. It is for me ungraspable how a lounge at such a big airport has to be in the middle overlooking shopping areas and not have a view to the tarmac. This could have been easily one of the best lounges in the world. Instead people rate it as excellent merely on the food options available if available. This is not a lounge where you feel or experience some sort of privilege.

The lounge that I went to on my recent flight with Air Serbia was very good. There were 2 lounges available for Air Serbia flights: the Turkish Airlines lounge and the ProPass lounge. The views and the drink options were both magnificent, but the food, well not so much. There weren’t many choices and the choices provided didn’t look fresh. The staff were nice, but the lounge was a bit noisy. The mini chocolate muffins were amazing, a must try! The toilets were very clean and had a pleasant odour. It also was a bit crowded and there was limited seating, but the seats were amazingly comfortable! The WiFi was great too! (Also I don’t know if there were showers!) In conclusion, this lounge is great and I would recommend it!

While the Turkish Airlines business class lounge highlights private rooms as a premium feature, the actual experience is anything but premium. The showers follow a reasonable queue system, but the private rooms are an elusive and undignified ordeal. Despite being advertised as part of the business class offering, they seem more like a marketing ploy. There’s no queue system in place for these rooms. Instead, passengers are expected to pop in and out, begging for availability. The staff, with stiff body language, offer vague and inconsistent time estimates—anywhere from 25 minutes to over an hour. To make matters worse, there’s no time limit for how long guests can occupy the rooms, leaving others in a constant state of uncertainty and frustration. This process leaves passengers feeling more like beggars than valued patrons. Turkish Airlines should either implement a proper queue system or charge a fee to ensure a fair and transparent process. The current setup is nothing short of undignified and far from the business class experience one would expect. I finally got my room after 3 hours of waiting in uncertainty, and it should not be like this.

This is a very busy lounge with Priority Pass members being put on a waiting list for approximately 45 minutes. Seating was scarce on the first floor. The food quality is excellent. The lounge had a nice selection of Mediterranean cuisine e.g. kefta kabob with tomatoes and aubergine, grilled creamy chicken, assortment of cheese and crackers, hummus and Turkish Tea. WiFi worked flawlessly. There were lines for the bathroom given the number of passengers in the lounge. Nonetheless, the bathrooms were clean.

I travel business class internationally due to poor health conditions and advanced age. I have heart disease and cannot walk very far, and my wife has nerve damage and also cannot walk long distances. We both require wheelchairs. We arrived to IST on February 7th, at 2:43 pm, from Toronto. We had a 7-hour long layover in Istanbul, before our flight TK708 departed for Karachi, Pakistan, at 9:55 pm. Because of the long connection, we tried to reserve a nap room and specifically chose IST for this purpose. My wife was unable to sleep on the 9 hour flight from Canada and was exhausted. A young lady at the concierge desk provided unprofessional and rude responses to us when we asked her for a nap room. She first said there were none and to come back every 30 minutes to check. My wife walked back and forth (with great difficulty) from distant seating areas over the course of 2 hours, every 30 minutes, because I cannot walk very far. The young lady at the concierge desk did not have the courtesy to take our phone number or to put our names as next in line. After 2 hours, we tried again (the 4th time), and a younger man quickly walked ahead of us to the desk. The concierge desk then gave the next available nap room to this young man, who only showed up the first time to the desk, instead of my wife and I, after we were waiting for 2 hours and had been to the desk 4 times. We pleaded with the young lady at the concierge desk, asking why she gave the room to the other man. The concierge simply said "he came to the desk faster than you". For 7 hours we were unable to rest and sat in regular seats in the lounge, waiting for our connecting flight. This has been the worst business class experience I have ever faced in my life.

I miss the old TK lounge at Ataturk airport. This lounge is always packed. And the food variety and quality goes downhill every time I’m here. And now, with Turkish (or Turkiye) boycotting US products, there are not only no Coke products, but no soda of any kind. Sorry. I’m headed into the terminal. Worthless to sit in the crowded lounge and you can’t even get a Coke. Turkish has really dropped its game in their lounges.

We definitely received very good service. They provided every service in the best possible way. The food is very delicious, the seating areas are comfortable and wide, and there are many activation systems to pass the time. So you will lose track of time while waiting for the transfer.

Exclusive Turkish airlines lounge, huge space, different rooms to relax, big variety of food and drinks, local sweets. There is also a piano, sometimes they play it. Easy to spend a few hours here. Free Wi-Fi

I had on other trips been in their excellent business class lounge and flying this time in economy but being in possession of a Star Alliance Gold Status I had been granted entrance in this CIP Lounge.  I read it is inferior to the Business Lounge but besides just a couple of food stations less, I must see I truly am impressed: excellent food and drink selection, lovely atmosphere, simply a great place to be and spend some time.

I heard that this lounge was opened to give passengers who paid for a business class ticket a slightly more exclusive experience by leaving out status customers and thus making the lounge less crowded. This has not worked. The TK lounge at Ataturk airport used to be really fantastic and special and it was one of the reasons I booked with TK all the time. This time seems to have passed. I am just sitting in the TK Business lounge at Istanbul new airport, feeling like waiting in an overcrowded train station. This feels more like a free fast food restaurant or an all-you-can-eat holiday venue, than an exclusive space to relax and wait for the next flight. Virtually all seats are occupied, mainly by bags and coats to reserve a seat for people who seem to be wandering around. People are shoveling piles of food onto their plates and leave the tables completely covered with leftovers and rubbish. Even the supposedly quiet areas are overcrowded. Having been in the fantastic Qatar Airways Business lounge at Doha airport, this is the complete opposite… crammed, crowded and ordinary.

Using this lounge on a SWISS flight. The place is simply horrible. There are plenty of alcoholic drinks especially whisky, served by a bartender - the food is terrible and extremely poor. There was a very salty soup, a lot of vegetables and bread with tuna salad. Some small kind of a saucer with limited food like pieces of cheese with one grape, pineapple, melon and berry. Another 3 cubes of chocolate cake. The soft drinks in the fridge were lukewarm, in a basket some melting ice. I left the lounge and went to an eatery to have a decent sandwich. Maybe this lounge is Ok if you want to drink alcohol but not for a decent snack at all. The restrooms were not very clean.
After all the hype I was expecting something above average. What a let down, seating in the food area was very poor, no bar, and incredibly complicated internet access.

Transited twice through this outstanding and impressive lounge. As with my last visit in May 2022, the lounge has an open airy feel. Its food offerings are varied/excellent with various cooking stations throughout the lounger to satisfy one's palette. One definitely gets a taste of Turkish cuisine. The salad bar is extensive with a wide variety as is the tea bar with its variety of teas. On both visits we were able to get free massages to the neck and shoulders. Can't go wrong with this type of service. WiFi connection was excellent. Bathrooms are very clean and maintained by attendants.

I was looking forward to visiting this lounge because I had heard so much about it. Well, maybe the food is ok but not for Vegans. Even the lentil soup and white rice had butter, nothing for Vegans but a bowl of green salad. Next time I can arrive at the airport a bit later and have food outside - complete disappointment.

Turkish Airlines' flagship business class lounge is outstanding and impressive. The lounge is on an open-level overlooking the main part of the terminal. There is plenty of seating and space. The seating is very comfortable. The lounge is immaculate and its food offerings are superb featuring freshly cooked food at various cooking stations throughout the lounge ranging from grilled foods, pasta and baked cheese, spinach and meat pies, cheeses/olives, salads and desserts. One definitely gets a taste of Turkish cuisine here including Simit (sesame seed bagel) and coffee/tea. The latter can be served in glass cups you get in Turkish restaurants. There are quieter darker seating areas akin to seating in a library like area. There is a room with 12 TV screens to catch up to the news. The lounge also features virtual golf and a holographic flight experience. The bathrooms are very clean and maintained by attendants. Our flight was at 2 pm so all the cooking stations were manned and food aplenty. Depending on the food station there were some queues. The staff kept the tables clean removing used dishes/utensils promptly. WiFi worked just fine; however, you had to scan boarding pass to get WiFi password.

What a great lounge! From the freshly cooked dishes ranging from typical Turkish kebabs through Moussaka, Chinese spicy chicken stir fry and pasta stations you could see all those being prepared. In addition various meze options and a few sweets including an array of the ubiquitous baklava variants. Drinks stations (DIY) were dotted around. One nice feature was the lockers in which you can leave your bags, using a combination of your choosing. There is a golf simulator and other adult toys including a Scalextric track! Comfortable seating in a variety of types and a quiet atmosphere.

The only hot food was toast. Other than that, it was pre-packaged rubbish.  The coffee was weak, stale and tepid. There was no draught beer, only tiny cans. It is probably the worst airport lounge of any big city in the world and a national embarrassment. The WIFI involves fiddly codes that you must obtain from machines.

My inbound flight was 09h30 min, and my outbound was 06h30 and in between a layover of 14h. I was denied a sleeping room while it was given to passengers between 04 and 09h layover. So, I spent the whole 14h in the lounge, couldn’t get near nor shower.
